## Metehan Yeşilyurt — Everything Is an Entropy Game: What Dies Between Retrieval and Citation

**Key thesis:** The internet is chaos and AI engines are managing entropy on a tight energy and token budget. SEOs are still the people who bring order. To win, understand the three layers under the hood: **tokenization** (and its English bias), **embeddings** as the front of retrieval, and **rerankers** as the gatekeepers behind them. **Common Crawl** is a partial-but-important window into LLM training data. Practical move: front-load content, reduce token waste in non-English markets, and use embedding similarity as a real authoring tool — not a buzzword.

![Title slide — "Everything Is an Entropy Game: What Dies Between Retrieval and Citation" by Metehan Yeşilyurt, Co-Founder & CGO, AEO Vision · SEO Week 2026](https://wsrv.nl/?url=https%3A%2F%2Fcustomer-assets.emergentagent.com%2Fjob_github-checker-8%2Fartifacts%2Fqj362kdl_IMG_2602.jpg&w=1080&q=70&output=webp)

### TL;DR

AI engines are running on tighter energy and compute budgets, so they don't actually read every candidate page — they sample, hash, and triage. The retrieval pipeline rests on three under-the-hood layers most SEOs ignore: **tokenizers** (with heavy English bias and real cost penalties for non-English content), **embeddings** (the entry pass — without good similarity you're never considered), and **rerankers** (the real gatekeepers, scoring quality on top of similarity). Common Crawl is the largest open window into what future LLMs may learn, but it's incomplete and increasingly blocked by major publishers. SEO is now entropy reduction: make the engine's life easier and you win.

### The framing — SEOs as entropy managers

- The internet has billions of pages, growth is accelerating, and every new tool adds entropy
- Google and AI engines are explicitly running on tighter energy and compute budgets — they need fewer, faster, cleaner reads
- SEOs are the people who **reduce entropy**: telling engines which page is the right answer for a given user intent
- This isn't just SEO — AEO, GEO, HEO are all valid framings. The job is the same: **make the engine's life easier**

![Metehan Yeşilyurt on stage at SEO Week 2026, walking the audience through the entropy framing](https://wsrv.nl/?url=https%3A%2F%2Fcustomer-assets.emergentagent.com%2Fjob_github-checker-8%2Fartifacts%2F61mkqzeh_IMG_2603.jpg&w=1080&q=70&output=webp)

### Question 1 — do AI engines actually read every candidate page?

- **Short answer: no**
- Fully reading every candidate would cost millions of tokens per query and is economically untenable
- Engines sample efficiently and rely on snippets, embeddings, and hashed signals to triage
- Speaker has a *Search Engine Land* post going deeper on this

### The retrieval flow (companion to the morning keynote)

- Same general flow Krishna walked through in the keynote, with extra technical detail on the embedding and reranking layers
- **Gemini accepts multimodal input** — PDFs, MP3s, images, text — combined into a single embedding context
- **Perplexity** is strong on ambiguous queries and exposes signals that let you compare documents using **cosine similarity** and **Hamming distance**
- Speaker decoded hashed pile signals from a browser session, published findings on August 25
- Engines use the hashed/embedding layer to find the swiftest path to a high-quality answer document

### Tokenizers — a fundamental tool, often ignored

- Tokenizers are the bridge between content and what the model actually sees
- OpenAI has iterated tokenizers actively across versions to improve multi-language handling
- Test with a random Wikipedia article: even alphabet characters can become their own tokens depending on context
- **Adding 3 emojis increased total token usage by 6** — each emoji costs roughly 2 tokens
- **Translating a sentence into another language can roughly 2× the token count** — a real cost issue for non-English content
- ChatGPT has an English bias. Even when prompted in Turkish, Spanish, or Portuguese it can return English chunks — making optimization for non-English markets harder
- Tools to inspect: **OpenAI tokenizer**, **Hugging Face tokenizer playgrounds** (highly recommended)

### Embeddings and rerankers — the front and back of retrieval

- **Embeddings** are the *entry pass* to the retrieval pipeline. Without good embedding similarity, your page never gets considered
- To reduce hallucinations and earn trust in LLMs, **use embedding similarity analysis on your own content** as part of the authoring loop
- Perplexity, ChatGPT, and Google all use embedding-based vector similarity as a crucial step
- Embeddings alone are not enough. **Rerankers sit behind retrieval and re-score the top candidates more carefully**
- Rerankers are tasked with separating *high-quality* from *merely-similar* content — they are the **real gatekeeper** for whether your page makes it to the answer
- Practical takeaway: optimize for the **reranker's quality bar**, not just embedding match

#### Reranker weights — the new "ranking factors"

![Reranker weights slide — three signal categories: Query–Document Alignment (lexical overlap, paraphrase density, named-entity overlap, entity co-occurrence distance), Confidence (hedge word density, qualifier density, absolute vs. relative claims, sentence-final certainty), and Semantic / Attention (unique n-gram ratio, cross-attention mass on query tokens, ColBERT-style maximum token-level similarity, embedding-space alignment)](https://wsrv.nl/?url=https%3A%2F%2Fcustomer-assets.emergentagent.com%2Fjob_github-checker-8%2Fartifacts%2F8ohcw1lf_IMG_2606.jpg&w=1080&q=70&output=webp)

We can't actually call them "ranking factors" anymore — the classifier phase changes for almost every provider, even per model. But here's the overview a reranker can look for:

- **Query–Document Alignment Signals** — Lexical overlap · Paraphrase density · Named-entity overlap between query and passage · Entity co-occurrence distance within the passage
- **Confidence Signals** — Hedge word density · Qualifier density · Absolute vs. relative claims · Sentence-final certainty
- **Semantic / Attention Signals** — Unique n-gram ratio · Cross-attention mass concentrated on query tokens · Maximum token-level similarity (ColBERT-style late interaction) · Embedding-space alignment between query and chunk

Any LLM can look for different patterns. **It's all about relevance now.**

#### Made-up brand experiment — entity authority lives in the reranker

![Made-Up Brand Competition results — real brands (Nike 97.63, Adidas 96.19, New Balance 93.48, Skechers 90.13) all clustering around an 87.21 average, while invented brands (Strideforge, Norvex Sole, Graveloft) score 5–22 — a 60+ point gap entirely explained by training-data presence](https://wsrv.nl/?url=https%3A%2F%2Fcustomer-assets.emergentagent.com%2Fjob_github-checker-8%2Fartifacts%2F8mc7n0m5_IMG_2607.jpg&w=1080&q=70&output=webp)

- Speaker ran 1,000 iterations (concurrency 500, model gpt-4.x, 1 iteration failed) ranking 13 brands — 10 real, 3 invented
- **Real-brand average: 84.64. Made-up-brand average: 26.86. Training-data lift: +57.78 points**
- Invented brands (*Strideforge, Norvex Sole, Graveloft*) consistently land at the bottom — Strideforge at 21.27, Norvex Sole at 5.96, Graveloft at 4.06
- Lesson: **entity authority is not just embedding match — it's training-data presence the reranker can corroborate.** Brand-new entities have to fight uphill against absence-of-signal, not just competitor signal
- "Only training data 1000×" still trails "with web search 100× times" — closing that gap is the AEO opportunity

### Common Crawl — a window into training data

- Speaker is processing **roughly 10 million URLs** across different captured snapshots
- Common Crawl is a non-profit publishing **terabytes of crawl data per archive** (March archive alone is huge)
- Common Crawl uses a **centrality / page-score** concept similar in spirit to PageRank, but distinct from Google's. Sites with more links sit closer to the core of the dataset
- **Being in Common Crawl is a partial proxy** for being learnable by future LLMs — not a complete one
- Labs supplement Common Crawl with **licensed deals, partnerships, and unauthorized scraping**. The Common Crawl home page shows visible partner logos worth checking
- The **CCBot** user agent appears in your log files. Track its share against other AI bots and Googlebot
- Common Crawl ships a **free index lookup tool** — slow, but free
- Major publishers have started **blocking CCBot** to fight unauthorized training use and content licensing concerns

### Quotes worth keeping

> "SEOs are the people who bring order to the internet." — Metehan Yeşilyurt

> "Do they really click and read all the pages? No, they don't." — Metehan Yeşilyurt

> "Embeddings are not enough. Rerankers decide who actually shows up." — Metehan Yeşilyurt

> "Every new tool adds entropy. Our job is to reduce it for the engines." — Metehan Yeşilyurt

### My take

This was the most technically dense talk of the day, and the one where the "what to actually do Monday morning" lands hardest. The framework I'm taking away is **three layers, three discrete optimization targets**:

1. **Tokenizer layer** — audit token efficiency, especially for non-English content and emoji-heavy copy. Translation roughly doubling tokens is a real per-impression cost line item, not a curiosity.
2. **Embedding layer** — bring embedding similarity into the *authoring* loop, not the post-publish audit loop. If your draft doesn't cluster with your top-converting page in vector space, fix the draft, not the meta description.
3. **Reranker layer** — write for confidence and entity overlap, not just keyword overlap. The hedge-word-density and absolute-vs-relative-claim signals are exactly the editorial moves we already know separate B-tier from A-tier copy. Now they have a measurable target.

The made-up brand experiment is the cleanest illustration I've seen of *why* AEO matters: a brand with zero training-data presence starts the race 60 points behind. That's the work — close the gap by getting cited, scraped, indexed, and entity-resolved before the next training cut.

Pair this with Jori's HEO scorecard from the prior slot and you have a complete loop — Jori tells you *what to measure*, Metehan tells you *what's happening underneath the score*.

### Open questions

- [ ] What is the actual sampling logic engines use to pick which candidates get a full read vs. snippet-only?
- [ ] How do you optimize for rerankers specifically, when their scoring is opaque and model-dependent?
- [ ] What's the right way to measure non-English token efficiency at scale, beyond per-page tokenizer audits?
- [ ] If major publishers are blocking CCBot, will future LLMs see a more skewed slice of the web? What does that do to small-publisher visibility?
- [ ] How does Common Crawl's centrality score actually behave for sites with strong topical clustering but moderate inbound links?

### Action items

- [ ] Run sample pages through the **OpenAI tokenizer**. Note token counts for English vs. non-English variants
- [ ] For non-English content, audit emoji usage and translation patterns that inflate token counts
- [ ] Add **embedding similarity analysis** to the content review loop *before* publishing
- [ ] Audit log files for **CCBot share** alongside other AI crawlers (GPTBot, ClaudeBot, PerplexityBot)
- [ ] Look up key domains in the **Common Crawl index tool** to confirm presence
- [ ] Read Metehan Yeşilyurt's *Search Engine Land* post on retrieval and snippet sampling
- [ ] Check Common Crawl's partner page for the latest list of licensed partnerships
- [ ] Decide on a **CCBot policy**: allow (training inclusion) vs. block (content licensing protection)

### People to follow up

- **Metehan Yeşilyurt** — Co-Founder & CGO, AEO Vision · [linkedin.com/in/metehanyesilyurt](https://www.linkedin.com/in/metehanyesilyurt/) · DM for the Search Engine Land deep-dive on retrieval sampling and the made-up-brand experiment methodology.
takeaways: AI engines don't read every candidate page — they sample, hash, and triage on a tight token/energy budget
Three under-the-hood layers: tokenizers (English bias, non-English costs 2× tokens), embeddings (entry pass), rerankers (real gatekeeper)
Use embedding similarity as an authoring tool — not just a post-publish audit
Reranker signals fall into 3 buckets: query-document alignment, confidence, and semantic/attention
Made-up brands score 60+ points lower than real brands — entity authority lives in training-data presence
Common Crawl is a partial-but-meaningful proxy for LLM training-data inclusion; track CCBot in your logs
SEO is now entropy reduction — make the engine's life easier and you win

## Scott Stouffer — Your Brand Is a Mathematical Object: Centroids, Clusters, and the Retrieval Boundary

**Key thesis:** AI does not *see* your brand. It **calculates** it. Every paragraph you publish becomes a vector in embedding space; together they form clusters with a center point — the **centroid** — which is what the system actually treats as your brand. Retrieval happens before ranking: queries are matched against centroids first, and if your centroid is too far away or too diluted, your pages never enter the candidate set. **No retrieval, no existence.** The work of SEO is now centroid management, not page optimization.

![Scott Stouffer on stage at SEO Week 2026, walking the audience through retrieval-boundary mechanics](https://wsrv.nl/?url=https%3A%2F%2Fcustomer-assets.emergentagent.com%2Fjob_github-checker-8%2Fartifacts%2Fb762bz2a_IMG_2608.jpg&w=1080&q=70&output=webp)

### TL;DR

AI does not see your brand — it calculates it. Every paragraph you publish becomes a vector in embedding space; those vectors form clusters with a center point (the **centroid**), and the centroid is what the system treats as your brand. Retrieval happens *before* ranking: queries are matched against centroids first, and if your centroid is too far away or too diluted, your pages never enter the candidate set. **No retrieval, no existence.** The work of SEO is now centroid management, not page optimization.

### The framing shift

- Speaker positions himself as a **search engineer**, not an SEO. Most of the industry observes outcomes (rankings, traffic). He builds the systems that produce them
- SEO teams doing everything right are still losing because **the rules changed and nobody told them**
- Pages don't compete on keywords anymore. They compete on **alignment, meaning, and intent**
- Adding more content can *increase* drift. More optimization can reinforce wrong signals. More authority can amplify the wrong footprint

### The hard rule — "not retrieved" equals "does not exist"

- If your page is not selected into the candidate set, it is invisible to AI. **There is no fallback**
- No second page, no almost-there. Just gone
- The shift is *not* from position 5 to position 3. It is from **excluded to included**
- Crossing the retrieval boundary is the only thing that matters first. Everything else is downstream

### How AI actually sees your content

- It does not see pages. It does not care about word count, layout, H1s, or domain age
- Pages are broken into **chunks**: passages, sections, individual ideas
- A single paragraph from a guide can compete independently. A definition halfway down a page can become the answer. A short sentence, if perfectly aligned, can outperform a fully-optimized page
- Each chunk becomes a **vector** — a coordinate in multidimensional space based on meaning
- Two chunks with different wording can sit close together if they express the same idea. Two chunks with the same keywords can be far apart if they mean different things
- Example: *"how to fix a leaking pipe"* and *"how to repair a plumbing leak"* land near each other. *"Apple nutrition facts"* and *"Apple stock earnings"* drift far apart despite the shared word

### From chunks to clusters to centroid

- Map every chunk into the coordinate space and similar meanings naturally group together
- How-to guides, definitions, and supporting content overlap into dense clusters even when on different pages
- **You don't choose your clusters.** They emerge from what your content actually says, not what you intended
- Aligned content produces **dense, clear clusters**. Scattered content produces **sparse, fragmented** ones
- Inside each cluster sits a center point: the **centroid** — mathematically the average position of all your chunks
- Every paragraph pulls the centroid slightly in its direction. Consistent content tightens the centroid. Scattered content dilutes it
- **Your centroid is your brand to AI.** Not your homepage, not your messaging doc, not your brand guidelines. The math of everything you have ever published

### Distance is the signal

- Visibility reduces to **proximity**. How close is each page to your centroid? How close is the query to that centroid?
- Small distance = aligned, retrieved. Large distance = misaligned, filtered out
- Doesn't matter how well-written the page is or how strong the domain. **Far away in space = not selected**
- Plain English version: *do your pages agree with your brand, or are they pulling in different directions?*
- Every page either strengthens the centroid or distorts it

### How retrieval actually works

- A query arrives. The system interprets meaning, intent, context, even ambiguity. *"Best CRM for small business"* is not just keywords — it is comparison + scale + use case
- Query is converted to a vector and placed in the same space as your content
- System looks outward for closest matches at the **cluster and centroid level first**, not the page level
- If your centroid is far from the query, your pages are not crawled, not scored, not compared. They never enter the candidate set
- If close, you enter the candidate set, and *only then* do traditional ranking signals (content quality, links, structure) start to matter
- Two sites with equally strong content. Only one is even considered. The other never gets a chance to compete

### The cluster-collision problem

- Most brands look identical to AI. Same sources, same stats, same agencies, same templates, same best practices
- Their centroids collapse into the same region of space. **No separation, no distinct signal**
- The system does not need *all* of you. It picks a few representatives and ignores the rest
- Speaker calls this **"cluster collision."** The silent killer of visibility
- Comparable to 10 résumés saying the same thing when only 2 get picked
- Following best practices makes you **collide harder, not differentiate**. The result of doing what everyone else does is being filtered with everyone else

### What actually wins

![Closing slide — "You must STABILIZE your centroid. Not just OPTIMIZE pages." Centroid stability over page-level tactics is the entire job to be done.](https://wsrv.nl/?url=https%3A%2F%2Fcustomer-assets.emergentagent.com%2Fjob_github-checker-8%2Fartifacts%2Fbymy73ez_IMG_2609.jpg&w=1080&q=70&output=webp)

- Not better content. Better versions of the same thing still land in the same crowded region
- Speaking louder while saying the same thing as everyone else does *not* move you in space
- You need a **distinct centroid**: a position in space that is clearly yours — that the system can separate, recognize, and retrieve consistently
- If your meaning is not distinct, your content cannot be either
- A distinct centroid means less competition during retrieval, fewer collisions, fewer substitutes, fewer reasons to be skipped

### The continuous-control mental model

- Centroid alignment is **not** set-and-forget. Every new page, update, or post pulls the centroid
- Optimization without alignment creates drift. Drift compounds silently
- The discipline: **measure → adjust → remeasure → repeat.** Like tuning an instrument, or a thermostat constantly correcting toward a target
- Done well, it becomes a **self-healing system** — drift gets corrected early, new content reinforces the centroid instead of pulling it off
- Without visibility into the space, you cannot correct. You can only react after performance drops
- Most teams are still guessing. The questions change once you can see your position: *"was I even eligible?"* replaces *"why didn't I rank?"*

### Quotes worth keeping

> "If you're not retrieved, you do not exist to AI." — Scott Stouffer

> "Your centroid is your brand to AI. Not what you say you are. What the system has calculated you to be." — Scott Stouffer

> "Distance is truth in these systems." — Scott Stouffer

> "The system didn't push you down. It filtered you out." — Scott Stouffer

> "Cluster collision is the silent killer of visibility." — Scott Stouffer

> "You don't write pages. You project meaning. And that meaning is what gets retrieved." — Scott Stouffer

> "Optimization without alignment creates drift." — Scott Stouffer

> "Your brand is already a mathematical object. You only get to choose whether you control it." — Scott Stouffer

### My take

This is the deepest reframe of the day so far. Mike King in the morning told us the candidate-set is everything; Krishna walked the retrieval flow; Metehan opened up the reranker layer; Jori gave us the scorecard to measure visibility. **Scott connects them into a single mental model**: you are not optimizing a page, you are stabilizing a position in a coordinate space.

What I'm taking back to the team:

1. **The "was I eligible?" question replaces "why didn't I rank?"** This is the new diagnostic. If a page never crossed the retrieval boundary, none of the on-page work matters. We need to start every audit with eligibility, not rank.
2. **Cluster collision is the practical KPI.** If our content occupies the same space as 12 competitor agencies' content, we are filtered. The right move isn't "better blog post" — it's a **distinct angle** that nobody else owns in vector space.
3. **Centroid drift is a financial control problem, not an SEO problem.** Treat it like a P&L variance — measured monthly, with thresholds, and a named owner.

Pair this with Jori's HEO scorecard and Metehan's reranker breakdown and we have the trifecta — *measure (Jori) → understand layers (Metehan) → manage position (Scott)*. This is the loop.

### Open questions

- [ ] How do you measure your own centroid in practice without access to the engine's exact embedding model?
- [ ] Which open embedding models are close enough to commercial systems that proxy measurements are useful?
- [ ] How do you decide when a piece of content is pulling the centroid in a *productive* direction (expanding topical depth) vs. a *destructive* one (introducing drift)?
- [ ] For multi-product or multi-brand sites, is there a clean way to maintain multiple distinct centroids on the same domain?
- [ ] What is the right cadence for centroid re-measurement: per publish, weekly, monthly?
- [ ] How does this framework interact with link-based authority signals once you do enter the candidate set?

### Action items

- [ ] Pick an open embedding model (**EmbeddingGemma**, **mxbai**, or Microsoft's open SOTA) and embed all chunks of the site to plot the cluster shape
- [ ] Calculate the **site centroid** and the distance from each page's centroid to it. Flag the outliers
- [ ] Map top target queries into the same space. Measure **query-to-centroid distance** for each priority query
- [ ] For each cluster collision (where multiple competitor sites occupy the same region), identify what would create a distinct **angle**, not better content
- [ ] **Stop publishing more best-practices content for highly contested queries.** Start publishing the angle competitors are not
- [ ] Add a pre-publish step: embed the new chunk and check whether it **tightens or dilutes** the centroid before shipping
- [ ] Build a monthly **drift report** tracking centroid movement over time. Treat it like a financial control, not an SEO report
- [ ] For misaligned legacy pages, decide: **rewrite to align, redirect, or remove**
- [ ] Reframe stakeholder reporting around *"are we eligible for retrieval on these queries?"* instead of rank position

### People to follow up

- **Scott Stouffer** — Co-Founder + CTO, Market Brew · 20 years building ranking and retrieval systems · [linkedin.com/in/scottstouffer](https://www.linkedin.com/in/scottstouffer/) · DM for the Market Brew approach to centroid measurement and the open embedding model recommendations.
takeaways: AI doesn't see your brand — it calculates a centroid (the average position of every chunk you've published)
Retrieval happens before ranking: if your centroid is too far from the query, your pages never enter the candidate set
'Not retrieved' equals 'does not exist' — the new shift is from excluded to included, not position 5 to position 3
Cluster collision is the silent killer of visibility: same sources + best practices = collapsed centroids = filtered out
What wins is a DISTINCT centroid (a position only you own) — not better versions of the same content
Treat centroid alignment as a continuous-control loop: measure, adjust, remeasure, repeat
Replace 'why didn't I rank?' with 'was I even eligible for retrieval?' as the new audit question

## Jeff Coyle — From Showing Up to Winning: Retrieval, Content Strategy, and the New Rules of AI Search

**Key thesis:** Most AI visibility tools measure **appearance**, not **mechanism** — the industry is repeating its old mistake of stopping at correlation. The real work is **technical AEO**: the merge of technical SEO, accessibility, and content strategy that determines whether you are even **eligible for retrieval**. Failures show up at *eligibility* (crawl, render, semantics, accessibility), not at ranking. Pages may rank, but **passages have to win**. Stop optimizing notionally — build comprehensive coverage of the **query fan-out** plus the **full customer journey**, and let editorial excellence carry it.

![Jeff Coyle on stage at SEO Week 2026 — closing the Day 1 main stage with the IR-and-systems-level view of AI search](https://wsrv.nl/?url=https%3A%2F%2Fcustomer-assets.emergentagent.com%2Fjob_github-checker-8%2Fartifacts%2Fxx16gerj_IMG_2610.jpg&w=1080&q=70&output=webp)

### TL;DR

Most AI visibility tooling measures *outputs* (mentions, citations, screenshots) but not *mechanism*. We're repeating the SEO industry's old correlation problem — same category error as rank tracking. The real win is **technical AEO**: the intersection of technical SEO + accessibility + content strategy, which decides whether the system can even retrieve you. Failures live at eligibility (crawl, render, semantics, accessibility), then extractability, then coverage, then differentiation — only *then* selection. Pages may rank but **passages have to win**. Build query-fan-out coverage *plus* full-journey coverage (TOFU/MOFU/BOFU/post-purchase). Stop FAQ-stuffing. Stop AI-editing your way to excellence. Editorial excellence is the only durable moat.

### The reframe — stop measuring outputs, start understanding mechanism

- Mentions, citations, screenshots are useful but they don't tell you whether content was retrievable, accessible, interpreted as intended, or *why* it was selected vs. ignored
- The industry built a measurement culture around downstream artifacts, not root causes. **Same category error as SEO had with rank tracking**
- Citations tell you something *was used*. They don't tell you *why you won*, and SEOs in this room are here to win, not play
- Pull failures back to specifics: crawl access, rendering, structure, semantics, extractability, coverage gaps, lack of trust, lack of differentiation
- Build a point of view, not a dashboard. Take it home. Become a **center of excellence**, not a follower

#### The mechanism — the AI search pipeline

![The AI search pipeline (Siteimprove) — Crawl (access & fetch) → Render (JS execution) → Index (snippet eligible) → Interpret (query) → Expand / Fan-out (sub-queries) → Retrieve (candidate passages) → Rerank (verify/ground) → Synthesize (generate answer) → Cite (attribution). "If you only measure the end of that pipeline, you will misdiagnose where failure is happening."](https://wsrv.nl/?url=https%3A%2F%2Fcustomer-assets.emergentagent.com%2Fjob_github-checker-8%2Fartifacts%2Fj1ejtook_IMG_2613.jpg&w=1080&q=70&output=webp)

- Nine discrete stages from Crawl → Cite. Most teams measure stage 9 (citations/mentions). Failure is almost always upstream
- Each stage has its own observability, its own owner, its own remediation playbook
- *"If you only measure the end of that pipeline, you will misdiagnose where failure is happening."*

### The eligibility gate — where most failures actually happen

- AI search exposes weaknesses faster than classic search ever did because **agentic systems need a response in sub-200ms**
- Speaker calls current AI systems **"toddler AI"** — they're 18 months old and don't yet know how to exhaustively understand your tech stack. If you don't actively monitor, things slip
- Common failures: blocked rendering, network/firewall rules that prevent AI Overviews/Gemini bots from even visiting, weak semantics, weak accessibility, thin content, weak credibility, off-topic sprawl
- **Real example:** a major nonprofit healthcare organization had myth-busting articles where the headers were the only thing the AI parsed cleanly. AI ended up citing the org as if they *endorsed the myth*. A billion-dollar messaging mistake. Caught in 3–4 days only because they were monitoring
- **Rule:** if the system can't reliably access, render, and interpret your content, you don't compete
- Discoverability for humans and AI sits on the same foundation. Semantic headings, alt text, labeled controls help the **25% of Americans with disabilities AND every AI ingestion pipeline**

### How search evolved into hybrid retrieval

- **Lexical retrieval** — what the text says (TF-IDF, BM25 era)
- **Hybrid retrieval (pre-LLM)** — pairing lexical with semantic. Search engines balanced the two depending on the query type
- **Generative changed the game overnight** — pull pages live (RAG), trust the LLM directly, or RAG over a dataset. Each new mode added another channel to manage. We now have **6, 7, 12, 15+ channels**
- The new question is no longer *"what page is relevant?"* It's *"what evidence can compose an answer?"*

### Query fan-out + journey coverage — the new topical authority

- Query expansion is now **query fan-out**: Google may run ~15 queries, pull ~20 results each → **roughly 600 candidate items per visible prompt**
- The visible prompt is *not* the whole retrieval problem. Don't accept a flat list of related questions and call it done
- Speaker's "superpower" framing: combine **query fan-out coverage** with **full customer journey coverage** (TOFU, MOFU, BOFU, post-purchase troubleshooting, conflict resolution)
- When AI Overviews launched, the brands winning consistently weren't lucky. They had strong TOFU + MOFU + BOFU + post-purchase content. They understood their users at every stage
- This is the next expansion of the topic model — not just topic depth, but **query expansion + journey + fan-out woven together**

### Pages may rank, passages have to win

- Not every passage on a page is equal. Speaker analyzes every claim individually
- Old editor-in-chief test: *"Could someone fact-check this if they wanted to?"* If the answer is no, the claim probably won't carry weight
- Look for: corroboration, passage clarity, evidence density across your graph, scope of information, unique value
- **"Information gain"** in this context means: am I providing something unique and differentiated vs. the same thing said by everyone else?
- If you're publishing a definition, it had better be one of the best definitions on the web with unique experience and information. Otherwise low chance of being the differentiated voice
- Marginalizing claims (factually thin or unsupported) drag down *surrounding* passages, not just themselves. **Passage drift is a real penalty**

### Anti-patterns that won't save you

- **You can't FAQ your way to the top.** Tacking question/answer pairs to the bottom of pages with structured markup looking for correlation lifts is a known failure path
- **You can't edit your way to success.** SEOs writing AI-generated content and "SEO + AEO this" on the way to publish are part of the problem
- The fix: **get earlier in the writer's process.** Their unique experience and expertise is the asset. Capture it before it gets stripped out by editing
- Subject matter experts and writers are the most important people in the room. Editing-only workflows lose their differentiation

### A real "12 articles for 1 passage" case

- Ran a Section 504 compliance case study. **Built 12 articles specifically to influence one passage selection**
- The targeted passage won. The supporting 12 are not waste — they reinforce the centroid (callback to Scott Stouffer's framework from the prior session) and build topical authority for adjacent retrievals
- Hard to justify in advance, but pays off in unpredictable ways. Worth doing for high-stakes target queries

#### What winning content looks like

![What winning content looks like (Siteimprove) — five pillars: Comprehensiveness (covers the full answer space without being bloated; breadth that maps to the fan-out graph), Point of view (a defensible stance the system can attribute to a source — not just coverage, an opinion), Evidence (claims backed by data, research, and verifiable facts; synthesis systems need linkifiable proof), Differentiation (information gain over the consensus — something new the system cannot get from five other sources), Topical depth (authoritative expertise on the subject; not surface treatment — structured domain knowledge). "You cannot edit your way into excellence. These qualities must exist before retrieval and synthesis happen. Only editorial excellence survives."](https://wsrv.nl/?url=https%3A%2F%2Fcustomer-assets.emergentagent.com%2Fjob_github-checker-8%2Fartifacts%2Fbw6dahff_IMG_2614.jpg&w=1080&q=70&output=webp)

- **Comprehensiveness** — covers the full journey without being bloated
- **Point of view** — a defensible stance the system can attribute to a source. If you're using LLMs to draft, point-of-view specification has to be in the prompt chain or the brief
- **Evidence** — every claim sourced or backed by data, research, or verifiable proof. Synthesis systems need *linkifiable* proof
- **Differentiation** — consensus over marginalization. Add information gain, not noise
- **Topical depth** — beyond pillar pages. Clean up orphan/long-tail pages without supporting structure
- **Editorial excellence is the only durable moat for content over the long haul**
- *"You cannot edit your way into excellence. These qualities must exist before retrieval and synthesis happen."*

### Killing competitors with content strategy

- Topic clusters are now **retrieval coverage maps**. Smaller, sharper teams can beat larger ones with better fan-out coverage
- Look for **"the cliff" pattern** at competitors: internal linking that only goes backward (new posts link to old, old never links to new). Visible in graph theory analysis. Easy to beat
- Watch for self-sabotaging patterns at competitors: AI-generated content at scale layered on top of unmaintained sites, broken internal linking, orphan sections (Health Center, product, blog) that don't talk to each other
- Many publishers are publishing **15,000 AI articles a month**. That actively *hurts* them by exacerbating cluster fragmentation. Your discipline becomes your weapon
- Use **graph theory against your competition**. Map their internal link structure and exploit the cliff

### Where you actually lose, in order

![Six-stage diagnostic ladder (Siteimprove) — 01 Eligibility (can the system access it? Crawl, render, index, snippet-eligible, accessibility) → 02 Extractability (can the system interpret it? Semantic structure, heading hierarchy, passage clarity) → 03 Coverage (can it extract useful passages? Evidence density, scope, corroboration) → 04 Selection (do you cover the fan-out space? Topic clusters, full-funnel, journey coverage) → 05 Information gain (do you add something new? Differentiation, unique POV, verifiable evidence) → 06 Outcome (are you selected repeatedly? Business outcomes — not appearance artifacts)](https://wsrv.nl/?url=https%3A%2F%2Fcustomer-assets.emergentagent.com%2Fjob_github-checker-8%2Fartifacts%2Ff8opv7zr_IMG_2615.jpg&w=1080&q=70&output=webp)

1. **Eligibility** — can the system access it?
2. **Interpretation / Extractability** — can it understand the structure and semantics? Can it pull useful passages?
3. **Coverage** — is the fan-out and journey covered?
4. **Selection** — are you in the candidate set when it matters?
5. **Differentiation / Information gain** — does it add something new to the conversation?
6. **Outcome** — are you selected *repeatedly*? Business outcomes, not appearance artifacts

If you fail upstream, downstream optimization doesn't matter.

### The 2-page reference guide

![Closing slide — "Download the 2-page reference guide" featuring the Be Seen By Everyone Venn diagram (Accessibility ∩ Search/SEO ∩ AI Search/AEO with "Shared / Foundation" at the intersection) plus the Technical Foundation Reference Guide checklist. Grab via the QR on slide.](https://wsrv.nl/?url=https%3A%2F%2Fcustomer-assets.emergentagent.com%2Fjob_github-checker-8%2Fartifacts%2Fvr1v8hpv_IMG_2616.jpg&w=1080&q=70&output=webp)

- Grab the QR off the slide deck if you can

### Quotes worth keeping

> "Don't sell this as snake oil. Let's not do that again." — Jeff Coyle

> "The page may rank, but the passage has to win." — Jeff Coyle

> "You can't FAQ your way to winning." — Jeff Coyle

This was the perfect closer for Day 1. Jeff connected every prior thread into a single diagnostic ladder you can hand to a team Monday morning:

Most content programs are still measured on output volume; Jeff is saying the right metric is *"did our targeted passage win, and did the supporting cluster reinforce the centroid?"* That is a fundamentally different operating model.

## Krishna Madhavan — The Invisible, Converged Web: Architecting Visibility for the AI Economy

**Key thesis:** Search and grounding share an early pipeline (query understanding → transformation → multi-path retrieval → candidate processing → multi-stage ranking) but diverge after eligibility. Grounding adds 4 heavier stages: evidence selection, evidence construction, constrained generation, cross-check + multimodal judging. **Citation ≠ visibility** — visibility starts at query understanding. To rank in AI, content must show up across all query fan-out paths.

### TL;DR

Search and grounding share early pipeline stages but diverge after eligibility. Grounding adds 4 heavier stages on top of search. **Citation ≠ visibility** — visibility starts at query understanding. To rank in AI, content has to surface across **all query fan-out paths**, not just one.

![Krishna Madhavan opens his keynote — Microsoft AI's grounding feeds Bing, Copilot, Gen Search, and powers nearly every major AI assistant except Google](https://wsrv.nl/?url=https%3A%2F%2Fcustomer-assets.emergentagent.com%2Fjob_github-checker-8%2Fartifacts%2F100jcxuz_IMG_2564.jpg&w=1080&q=70&output=webp)

### How the pipeline actually works

- Microsoft grounding powers **nearly every major AI assistant except one** (Google)
- Foundation models have a knowledge cutoff and hallucinate when ungrounded — the index is the live knowledge layer that fixes this
- The index is **NOT** a sorted list of pages and **NOT** a copy of the web — it's a transformed, multi-dimensional representation (content, structure, entity relationships, trust signals)
- **SEO optimizes for ranking; GEO optimizes for being selected as evidence** — much higher bar
- Pipeline split: search has ~3 steps post-branch (composition → snippet gen → SERP); **grounding has 4+ heavier stages**
- Evidence selection requires **explicit signals** justifying why a page should be cited; without them content is discarded
- Cross-check = one model critiques another's response; multimodal judging = multiple models vote on agreement

### Why query fan-out matters

- A single user query becomes **5+ rewritten variants**
- Pages need to surface across **ALL paths**, not one
- **Visibility starts at query understanding** — if not in any fan-out path, citation is impossible

### Access controls (precision vs. blunt)

- IndexNow accounts for **>50% of newly indexed URLs** in Bing/Copilot ecosystem; not a ranking boost but a freshness + crawl efficiency play
- **Access ≠ usage**. Robots.txt / noindex = blunt controls; **`data-*` HTML attributes = precision controls** (hide content from AI without losing rank)

## Andrea Volpini — Context Windows, Compression, and the Memory Layer for AI Agents

**Key thesis:** Context windows are racing toward "infinite" but cost and the **"lost in the middle"** problem mean visibility is no longer about getting into the prompt — it's about how well an agent can **traverse evidence across sources**. Structured data alone doesn't move the needle for AI systems; **entity pages with proper RDF connections produce ~29% accuracy lifts**. Two new techniques (KV cache quantization + recursive LM over knowledge graphs) make this concrete. The moat is the connected data layer, not the model.

![Andrea Volpini on stage at SEO Week 2026 — WordLift, 15+ years in symbolic AI](https://wsrv.nl/?url=https%3A%2F%2Fcustomer-assets.emergentagent.com%2Fjob_github-checker-8%2Fartifacts%2F5jzwvklq_IMG_2580.jpg&w=1080&q=70&output=webp)

### TL;DR

Context windows are racing toward "infinite" but cost and the **"lost in the middle"** problem mean visibility is no longer about getting into the prompt — it's about how well an agent can traverse evidence across sources. Structured data alone doesn't move the needle for AI systems; **entity pages with proper RDF connections produce ~29% accuracy lifts**. Two new techniques (KV cache quantization + recursive LM over knowledge graphs) make this concrete. **The moat is the connected data layer, not the model.**

### Key points

- Context window growth: hundreds of tokens → 1M (Gemini, 2024) → 10M (Llama 4, 2025) → "infinite" framing in 2026
- Two ceilings on infinite context: **(1) compute cost scales with token count** → hardware wall; **(2) "lost in the middle"** — models attend to first and last passages, not middle
- **Frontloading best content** increases likelihood of being used by ChatGPT
- SEO and GEO share early pipeline but diverge: GEO is a **journey** — agent explores multiple sources, judges trust, synthesizes
- Shift from documents → entities. AI systems blend passages from across sites/reviews into the relevant concept; **structure creates the pathways agents follow**
- Structured data's purpose is shifting from SERP enrichment to becoming the **navigable memory layer for AI agents**
- Two macro strategies for the infinite-context era: compression techniques, or **semantic connectedness** (the second is where the leverage is)

### Paper 1 — Structured data & AI retrieval

- Tested 4 site configurations on Vertex AI Search: plain HTML, JSON-LD, HTML + annotations, and **entity pages with RDF**
- **Finding:** structured data alone doesn't help AI systems (only helps when processed by Bing/Google's specific pipelines)
- **What works: entity pages that build context around pages** → ~29% accuracy increase
- Built on the W3C semantic web standard (~25 years old, non-proprietary)

### New compression technique (Google DeepMind, open source)

- Compresses the **KV cache** (the model's working scratchpad), not the context window itself
- Converts cartesian coordinates → polar coordinates (radius + angle) for vector storage
- Adds 1-bit / zero-bias realignment — eliminates the semantic drift normally caused by quantization
- **Result: ~4.5× more reasoning capacity, no retraining required, drops onto existing models**
- Implication: agents will have far more "headroom" to validate, cross-check, and traverse evidence

### Paper 2 — Recursive LM over knowledge graphs (RLM-on-KG)

- Recursive language model traverses structured data + knowledge graphs to gather scattered evidence
- **Benchmarked vs Microsoft GraphRAG (2024)**: F1 41.8 (RLM) vs 41.6 (GraphRAG) on the headline test — and crucially, **when evidence is scattered across 11+ chunks, RLM wins 56% of the time**, with **no pre-compute step**
- Built a controller that picks between GraphRAG, recursive LM, or traditional RAG depending on query complexity
- **Different base models traverse graphs with different competence** — meaning traversal is trainable on your own ontology
- Demoed applied to Gemma 4 (small LM) — **local on-device agents become powerful when paired with a well-built KG backend**

![RLM-on-KG live navigation slide — open-source RDF-native graph traversal, live in browser. Entity → Action → Data → Result loop. github.com/wordlift/rlm-on-kg](https://wsrv.nl/?url=https%3A%2F%2Fcustomer-assets.emergentagent.com%2Fjob_github-checker-8%2Fartifacts%2Fv4kizgac_IMG_2577.jpg&w=1080&q=70&output=webp)

![Head-to-Head: RLM vs GraphRAG — same benchmark, same knowledge graph, different approach. F1: RLM 45.8 vs GraphRAG 45.6. When evidence scattered across 11+ chunks, RLM wins 56% of the time](https://wsrv.nl/?url=https%3A%2F%2Fcustomer-assets.emergentagent.com%2Fjob_github-checker-8%2Fartifacts%2Fertww4aw_IMG_2578.jpg&w=1080&q=70&output=webp)

![The Model Capability Gap — Claude Haiku +4.37pp (strong gain), Gemini Flash Lite +0.84pp (marginal), Gemma 4 −0.78pp (negative). The right model with the right graph beats a bigger model without one](https://wsrv.nl/?url=https%3A%2F%2Fcustomer-assets.emergentagent.com%2Fjob_github-checker-8%2Fartifacts%2Fjmyc0ksm_IMG_2579.jpg&w=1080&q=70&output=webp)

### Quotes & data worth keeping

> "The real moat is not the model — there will always be new models. The real moat is **building the rock that can be explored by the model**."

> "Eras: GPT-3 = tokens / training data presence → GPT-4 = embeddings / similarity → GPT-5+ = **traversal of evidence**"

- ~29% accuracy lift from entity pages vs. plain structured data
- Up to ~71% retrieval accuracy lift over GraphRAG on complex queries with scattered evidence
- 4.5× reasoning capacity from KV cache quantization, no retraining
- Crawl traffic without citations is a known problem — the fix is making evidence pathways traversable

### Practical playbook from the talk

1. **Reduce ambiguity** — clean ontological core organization
2. **Build connected entities, not isolated pages with schema**
3. **Use consistent unique identifiers** across pages (Google now relies on these)
4. **Connect to public knowledge** — Wikidata, Wikipedia, schema cross-references
5. **Prioritize freshness and connection consistency** over content volume
6. **Audit not just on-page schema but cross-site entity coherence**
7. **Reframe AI visibility measurement**: from "prompt mention counting" → "**how well-connected is my data?**"

### Open questions

- Once KV cache compression hits production at web scale, does the "lost in the middle" problem persist or evaporate?
- What's the practical evaluation methodology for "connectedness" beyond the RLM-on-KG benchmark?
- How quickly will on-device models with KG back-ends become a real consumer surface — and does that change publisher strategy?
- Which models are best at graph traversal today, and how do you measure that without running the full benchmark?

### Action items

- [ ] Download both research papers from WordLift and read in full
- [ ] Audit current schema for unique identifier consistency across pages and external graphs
- [ ] Map entity coverage in Wikidata / Wikipedia for key brands; fill gaps
- [ ] Experiment with **Gemma 4 + a local KG** to evaluate the on-device agent direction
- [ ] Track release of the DeepMind KV cache quantization tool — plan for impact when at web scale
- [ ] Reframe AI visibility reporting from prompt-counting to **traversal / connectedness measurement**

### People to follow up

- **Andrea Volpini (WordLift)** — DM re: practical scoring methodology for cross-site entity connectedness
takeaways: Moat is the connected data layer, not the model
Lost in the middle: models attend to first/last passages — frontload best content
Entity pages with RDF → ~29% accuracy lift over plain structured data
RLM-on-KG beats GraphRAG 56% when evidence is scattered across 11+ chunks
DeepMind KV cache quantization: 4.5× reasoning capacity, no retraining

## James Cadwallader — Beyond the Click: How to Shape What AI Says About Your Brand

**Key thesis:** AI search has two layers. **Layer 1 is visibility** — do I show up, share of voice, citation rate — and this is where the entire industry is focused. **Layer 2 is *how* you are talked about** — accuracy, sentiment, unsolicited commentary — and almost no one is working on it. Profound analyzed **50,000 prompts across 7 industries** and found that **~50% of an AI response is non-extractive augmentation**: opinions, comparisons, caveats, and outright errors the user never asked for. ChatGPT served comparison tables in **8%** of responses; Gemini was more concise; half of what gets said about your brand is wrong, contradictory, or stale — and most of it appears *after* the user gets the answer they wanted. The fix is the **marketing engineer**: a new role that owns accuracy, sentiment, and the agentic-scale infrastructure required to find and correct what models say about you.

![James Cadwallader closing out SEO Week 2026's opening Future-track session — gray zip-up, blue jeans, SEO WEEK curtain behind him](https://wsrv.nl/?url=https%3A%2F%2Fcustomer-assets.emergentagent.com%2Fjob_github-checker-8%2Fartifacts%2F10hmx698_IMG_2746.jpg&w=1080&q=70&output=webp)

### TL;DR

AI search has two layers: *do I show up* (visibility) and *how am I talked about* (accuracy + sentiment + unsolicited augmentation). The industry is asleep on the second layer. Profound's 50,000-prompt study: ~50% of every AI answer is unsolicited "helpful augmentation" (rationale, comparisons, caveats, opinions). Southwest shows up in AI responses saying it has assigned seating — which it dropped in January. Nike gets citations with editorial provocations it never asked for. Fix this by building a ground-truth document, running FactScore-style accuracy checks, analyzing the citations driving sentiment (not just the answer text), and hiring the *marketing engineer* who owns agentic infrastructure at scale. Content has to become **original (non-commodity), fresh (13-week window), and atomic (granular claims)** — RunRepeat cutting shoes in half is the model.

### The two layers of AI search

- **Layer 1 — Do I show up?** AI visibility, share of voice, citation rate. The entire conference (and most of the industry) is focused here
- **Layer 2 — How am I being talked about?** Accuracy, sentiment, unsolicited commentary attached to your visibility. **Almost no one is working on this**
- Layer 1 is two-dimensional. Layer 2 is where reputation actually gets shaped at scale
- *"We are overlooking a huge part of the category by only looking at visibility"*

![Mike King welcoming James Cadwallader to the stage as the Future day opens — handover moment before the Profound keynote](https://wsrv.nl/?url=https%3A%2F%2Fcustomer-assets.emergentagent.com%2Fjob_github-checker-8%2Fartifacts%2F138rxvc8_IMG_2743.jpg&w=1080&q=70&output=webp)

### The "yapping" problem — real examples

- **Southwest Airlines:** showed up at 100% visibility in an AI response. The response *also* said *"pro tip: Southwest does have assigned seating"* — when Southwest **dropped assigned seating in January**. Stale information attached to a successful citation
- **Nike:** appeared in an answer with unsolicited editorial commentary like *"do you think this is the best option?"* — the model added comparison framing and provocative qualifiers Nike did not ask for
- Profound calls this internally the **"yapping problem."** Models do not stop yapping. They keep talking past the actual answer
- Consumer brand perception is now formed inside the model **before** the user reaches your site. Visibility is just the beginning

### The 50,000-prompt study

- **50,000 prompts** across **7 industries** (B2B SaaS, automotive, CPG, and others) and **5 major AI platforms**
- Open-ended and ranked questions, run at scale
- **Average ChatGPT response: ~3,000 characters** — roughly **11 tweets per answer**
- **Gemini** was significantly more concise on average
- **~50% of every response was non-extractive** — did not directly answer the user's question. Profound calls this "helpful augmentation"
- **ChatGPT served comparison summary tables in 8% of responses. Claude only ~3%**
- Most "augmentation" content: rationale for the answer, brand justifications, side-by-side comparisons, caveats, and unprompted opinions

![Profound slide — "AI answers are not direct. They're verbose." Average response character count across models: ChatGPT 1,848 chars · Gemini 2,379 chars · Claude 1,147 chars. ChatGPT writes ~1.9× more prose than Claude for the same prompts](https://wsrv.nl/?url=https%3A%2F%2Fcustomer-assets.emergentagent.com%2Fjob_github-checker-8%2Fartifacts%2Frz1nnr3f_IMG_2744.jpg&w=1080&q=70&output=webp)

![Profound slide — "What's most frequently included in unsolicited content?" Breakdown by model of how often editorial content fell into each augmentation category: rationale (9.7% ChatGPT, 8.6% Gemini, 8.8% Claude), comparison summary table, follow-up action referral, fee & terms caveats, context-dependent choice, ranking, shopping guidance](https://wsrv.nl/?url=https%3A%2F%2Fcustomer-assets.emergentagent.com%2Fjob_github-checker-8%2Fartifacts%2Fiefbnayy_IMG_2742.jpg&w=1080&q=70&output=webp)

### Accuracy as a new lever (the FactScore methodology)

- **Profound's view: objective accuracy feeds favorability over time. Fix accuracy first**
- Methodology adapted from the **FactScore paper** (UMass / Allen Institute)
- Process: ingest millions of LLM responses across platforms → identify each verifiable claim → compare against **ground truth** provided by the brand
- **Verifiable vs. non-verifiable claims must be separated.** Subjective opinion (*"this is the best"*) cannot be verified. Factual claims about features, pricing, capabilities can
- **Linear example:** model claimed *"Linear is only for engineering teams."* Linear's ground truth: they have invested heavily in product, design, and operations use cases. Verified inaccurate claim, fixable
- Profound is shipping **FactCheck** (general availability in 2–3 weeks). Upload your ground truth, the platform finds where models contradict it, tells you which platforms and prompts surface the inaccuracy

### Sentiment as a new lever

- Most sentiment analysis in AI visibility tools is surface-level. A small tab nobody clicks
- Profound runs **NLP across the citations themselves** (not just the answer text), then **matches the citation sentiment against the AI response sentiment**
- This lets you see **where negative sentiment is being pulled through into responses**. You can find the source citations driving the framing
- Shifts sentiment from a vanity metric into a diagnostic source: **which third-party content is shaping how AI talks about you?**

![James mid-keynote on the Profound stage — gray quarter-zip and tan chinos, walking the audience through the two layers of AI search](https://wsrv.nl/?url=https%3A%2F%2Fcustomer-assets.emergentagent.com%2Fjob_github-checker-8%2Fartifacts%2Ffs0gti4k_IMG_2740.jpg&w=1080&q=70&output=webp)

### Treat AI agents like superintelligent interns

- AI agents probably know more about your brand than you do — because they crawl constantly across every public source
- But they have **not lived in the world.** They have never tried on the running shoes. They have not eaten the food
- *"Humans are now a fleshy API between reality and AI."* When something happens in the world (fire on 5th Ave, news event), AI cannot know it until a human posts it somewhere
- Three implications for content strategy: **original** (non-commodity), **fresh**, **atomic** (granular)

### Original (non-commodity) content

- Pre-trained models can regurgitate any commodity content — same definitions, same listicles, same overviews
- **The exception that wins: content the pre-trained model could not have produced from training data alone**
- **RunRepeat** (running shoe review site) is the showcase example. They literally **cut shoes in half** to review the internal construction
- Their content cannot be inferred from training data. They are **dominating AI citations** across running and athletic-footwear
- The lesson: commodity content cannot get past the model's prior. **Non-commodity content has no substitute**

### Fresh content — the 13-week window

- Profound's data: **50% of top-cited content is less than 13 weeks old**
- The classic SEO playbook of *"publish once, coast on it for years"* is breaking
- Updating content frequently is becoming **structural, not optional**
- Highlight freshness explicitly. RunRepeat surfaces *"last updated"* dates prominently to signal currency to AI

### Atomic content — the granularity shift

- Generic marketing language (*"enterprise grade, industry leading, best in class"*) was written for humans. **AI cannot extract anything from it**
- AI needs **justifiable claims** it can pull through as evidence
- Get atomic. One specific claim, one specific number, one specific feature. Each claim becomes an extractable unit
- Per Kevin Indig (referenced): *"build a page that is the best answer to one question, not a page that adequately answers 20"*
- Personal example from James: **ChatGPT looked at 65 websites** to find a showerhead recommendation. Agent depth is now a normal user behavior. **If your content does not survive 65-source scrutiny, you don't get cited**

### RunRepeat as the case study

- **Original:** cuts shoes in half, reviews internal construction. Pre-training cannot reproduce this
- **Fresh:** explicit freshness signals on every page
- **Atomic:** granular feature-level breakdowns, specific claims with evidence
- Result: dominates AI citations across running and footwear categories
- Crucial second insight: RunRepeat doesn't just inform visibility. **They inform sentiment. They inform the facts being pulled into AI answers about competitor brands**
- *"This is the model for marketing in 2026 regardless of your industry"*

### The marketing engineer — the role this all requires

- Identifying inaccuracy and poor sentiment at scale will be a **P0 for every marketer on the planet** — but you cannot do it manually
- Layer 2 ownership requires someone who can **operate agentic systems**, not just edit content
- What the marketing engineer does:
  - Builds publication systems that scan the full AI inference layer for brand mentions
  - Pulls content from the CMS, scans it for outdated information, compares to ground truth, drafts updates, sends for human approval, republishes
  - Runs agents at scale to analyze content granularity across hundreds of thousands of pages
  - Owns the operational infrastructure for accuracy and sentiment correction
- This is the second layer of AI search ownership. Visibility is two-dimensional and the industry is fixated on it. **Reputation, sentiment, and accuracy are where the actual brand work lives**

### Quotes worth keeping

> "These models don't stop yapping."

> "50% of every response is helpful augmentation that didn't answer the question."

> "Visibility is just the beginning."

> "Humans are a fleshy API between reality and AI."

> "AI agents are like superintelligent interns — they know more about your brand than you do, but they have never tried the shoes on."

> "50% of top-cited content is less than 13 weeks old."

> "Build a page that is the best answer to one question, not a page that adequately answers 20." *— Kevin Indig, quoted*

> "We are fixated on visibility because humans love comparison to the past."

### Open questions

- How quickly does correcting a verifiable inaccuracy in your own ground truth actually propagate into model responses across platforms?
- If 50% of an answer is unsolicited augmentation, what is the right benchmark for "good" augmentation share for your brand?
- For sentiment driven by third-party citations, what's the right escalation path when the citation source is uncooperative or hostile?
- How does the 13-week freshness window interact with evergreen content that is genuinely timeless (academic concepts, foundational guides)?
- What's the minimum viable content granularity for AI extraction? How atomic is too atomic?
- Will accuracy tooling like FactCheck become a category, or will it consolidate into existing AI visibility platforms?

### Action items

- Run sample brand prompts across ChatGPT, Gemini, Claude — highlight every unsolicited augmentation and sort by accurate vs. inaccurate
- Build your own **ground-truth document**: facts about your products, services, pricing, positioning that AI should know
- For each verifiable claim AI is making about you, classify: accurate, outdated, false, misleading. Fix outdated and false **at the source** first
- Watch for Profound's **FactCheck** general availability (2–3 weeks from talk). Evaluate whether to use it or build internally
- Audit recent published content: how much is non-commodity? How much could AI have generated from training alone? Cut or rebuild the latter
- Add explicit *"last updated"* signals to top pages. Make freshness obvious to crawlers
- Audit content for atomic claims. Convert generic marketing language (*"best in class"*) to specific, extractable, evidence-backed statements
- Pick one priority page. Rebuild it as *"the best answer to one question"* rather than 20
- Study **RunRepeat's** content model in your category. Identify what original, non-commodity content you could produce that AI cannot regurgitate
- Run the **citation sentiment analysis**: which third-party sources are AI pulling negative framing from? Build a remediation list
- Begin scoping the **marketing engineer role** internally: who owns the agentic infrastructure for accuracy, sentiment, and content correction at scale?
- Pair Profound's accuracy framework with **iPullRank's relevance engineering metrics** from the prior session. Together they cover both layers
takeaways: AI search has two layers — visibility (where everyone is focused) and how you're talked about (where everyone is asleep)
Profound's 50,000-prompt study: ~50% of every AI answer is unsolicited augmentation (rationale, comparisons, caveats, opinions); ChatGPT serves comparison tables in 8% of responses, Claude only ~3%
The 'yapping problem' — Southwest cited in AI answers saying it has assigned seating (dropped Jan 2026); Nike cited with unsolicited editorial framing it never asked for
Accuracy is now a lever — Profound's FactScore-based FactCheck (GA in 2–3 weeks) ingests LLM responses, identifies verifiable claims, and compares against brand ground truth
Sentiment diagnosis comes from NLP on the CITATIONS, not just the answer — find the third-party sources driving how AI talks about you
Content rule of three: Original (non-commodity, like RunRepeat cutting shoes in half), Fresh (50% of top-cited content is <13 weeks old), Atomic (justifiable granular claims AI can pull as evidence)
ChatGPT reviewed 65 websites to recommend a showerhead — if your content doesn't survive 65-source scrutiny, you don't get cited
The 'marketing engineer' is the new P0 role — owns agentic infrastructure for accuracy, sentiment, and content correction at scale across the full AI inference layer
