## Christian Ward — Two Studies, 38 Million Data Points & the Blind Spot in Every AI Search Study

**Key thesis:** The conference has been admiring the problem. Time to solve it. Almost every AI visibility study runs **brand-down** (ask the model about a category, see what cites). But consumers ask with **intent and location**, which produces a completely different citation graph. Yext analyzed **17M citations in Q4 2025** and **155M in Q1 2026** from a bottom-up consumer perspective. The dominant sources are not Reddit and Wikipedia. They are **websites, Google Business Profile, MapQuest, Yelp, and other listings**. Citations per scan rose **28% quarter over quarter**. The fight you can actually win is the **supply chain of structured, real-time, consistent data** across every place your brand appears. Yext's Elo-style head-to-head testing found that updating data consistently in real time can lift Google rankings **3 to 6 spots** — with small businesses gaining the most.

![Yext Research slide — "Ads in AI." OpenAI is launching ads for free and Go tier. This has all happened before — do you remember how little data Google shared? Ad markets REQUIRE data to operate. Alongside: The Information chart projecting ChatGPT's paid subscribers to 306M by FY2030, with the ad-supported Go tier driving most of the growth (6M → 16M → 47M → 122M → 192M → 240M → 280M → 306M)](https://wsrv.nl/?url=https%3A%2F%2Fcustomer-assets.emergentagent.com%2Fjob_github-checker-8%2Fartifacts%2Fjwl3wc1u_IMG_2747.jpg&w=1080&q=70&output=webp)

### TL;DR

Stop running brand-down AI visibility studies — they misread the consumer journey. When you add **location + intent** to the prompt, the citation graph collapses away from Reddit/Wikipedia and toward **your website, Google Business Profile, MapQuest, Yelp, and other listings** — the sources you can actually control. Yext's 17M-citation Q4 study and 155M-citation Q1 dataset both confirm this. Citations per scan **rose 28% QoQ** — models are citing *more*, not less. Real-time, structured, consistent data across the full supply chain is now the moat. Elo head-to-head testing on 21M queries: consistent real-time data lifts ranks **~3 spots on average, ~5 for small businesses, ~6.2 in hyper-competitive markets**. Personalization is moving out of surveillance and into the AI's own context layer — **marketers will not get that data**.

### The "garbage in, masterpiece out" problem

- The classic SEO maxim was *"garbage in, garbage out."* With AI, that is **no longer true**
- You put garbage in, you get a masterpiece out. **The model polishes the input regardless of source quality**
- **Bordallo II analogy:** Portuguese artist makes 50-foot art installations from dumpster trash. Up close it is garbage. From a distance it is breathtaking. AI now does this with content
- **Incredibles syndrome:** when everyone is super, no one is. When all content is masterpiece-grade, differentiation collapses
- ChatGPT 5.5 was the first model that doesn't always default to em-dashes and *"it's not X, it's Y"* framing. Models are getting better at maintaining genuine voice. The output is harder to detect, which means **baseline content is harder to compete with**

### The platform shift in 30 days

- **Salesforce** launched 360 prompts. Benioff's framing: *"the API is the UI"*
- **Anthropic** released Claude Design the next day. Then **GPT 5.5** with computer use
- Anthropic **acquired a computer-use company** and integrated it into the model within 30 days
- **Apple** opened up model choice in Siri. Pick your own model. App layer becomes optional
- **Sam Altman** publicly said *"it feels like a good time to seriously rethink how operating systems and UIs work"*
- **Google patented** a way to auto-generate websites for brands because most existing websites are not AI-ready
- Direction is unambiguous: **websites become structured-knowledge conveyor belts feeding conversational interfaces**

![Yext Research slide citing the Google Patents filing "AI-generated content page tailored to a specific user" (Feb 27, 2026) — Google's patent to potentially rank your landing pages and generate their own AI version if your quality lacks](https://wsrv.nl/?url=https%3A%2F%2Fcustomer-assets.emergentagent.com%2Fjob_github-checker-8%2Fartifacts%2Fas8lgjka_IMG_2750.jpg&w=1080&q=70&output=webp)

### The Yext consumer-adoption study (March 2026)

- **1,120 adults** surveyed in March
- **59%** now use AI for general searches
- **47%** use AI for **local** searches. The *"tacos near me"* use case has crossed over faster than expected
- **52% of food/restaurant searches** have moved to AI
- **Wealthier users adopt first.** Free models underperform, paid models work, paid users keep coming back
- **The highest earners now START in AI, not Google**
- Only **6%** say they don't trust AI for local recommendations. Trust numbers are surprisingly high
- When ads hit AI search at scale, this acceleration will **compound** because ads will lower the cost of access for non-paying users

### Real-time is now structural, not optional

- **Any system that is not real-time will lose to one that is**
- If a cure for a disease is announced today, users want that answer **now**. They don't want last year's training data
- Per Krishna Madhavan's Day 1 keynote: **grounding (real-time retrieval) is the answer**. As compute costs fall, every AI interaction will route through grounding
- The only reason to answer from training is to save money. **That ceiling is dropping**
- Real-time data infrastructure is now the moat. Stale data infrastructure is a structural disadvantage

### The bottom-up vs top-down research blind spot

- Most AI visibility research today is **brand-down**. Ask the model about a category, count citations, declare Reddit and Wikipedia winners
- This research is cheap and easy because it just runs query fan-out. Useful for brand-level discovery, but it **ignores half the funnel**
- **Consumers don't ask abstract category questions.** They ask with **location and intent**: *"tacos near me," "best dentist in Roswell," "cheap surfboard in Jacksonville Beach"*
- When you put location and intent in the prompt, the citation graph changes **radically**. Reddit and Wikipedia largely disappear. **Listings and brand sites take over**
- If you ask any AI directly: *"Do you use my location when answering business or service questions?"* the answer is consistently **yes**. Location is one of the most important signals AI has about you

### The four citation control categories

- **Full control:** your website. You own it. Use it
- **High control:** listings (Google Business Profile, Yelp, MapQuest, Bing Places, etc.). You don't own them, but you control the data feeds. **Treat as data + distribution**
- **Limited control:** social and reviews. You can engage. You can't fully shape
- **Zero control:** news, Reddit, forums. Engage where appropriate. Don't expect to dictate
- **The dominant industry mistake:** spending most AI visibility energy on the bottom two categories where you have least control, while neglecting the top two

### The 17 million citation analysis (Q4 2025)

- **17M citations** across 4 major models, multiple sectors
- Prompts always included **location + product/service intent**
- Result: citation graph dominated by **websites and listings** (Google Business Profile, MapQuest, Yelp, etc.)
- Reviews showed up modestly — only material in food/restaurants where review density is core
- **Reddit, Wikipedia, news, forums almost invisible** from this consumer-intent perspective
- The pattern held across most sectors with industry-specific variation

### 155 million citations in Q1 2026 (first shared on stage)

- **Yext powers 2.5M businesses globally.** Also tracks all of their competitors
- Q1 2026 dataset: **155M citations.** Cohort comparison vs Q4 2025
- **Citations per scan rose 28% quarter over quarter.** Models are getting more cite-heavy, not less
- Different models cite different sources, but the structural breakdown holds: **websites and listings remain the two dominant cite categories you can actually control**

### Why structure beats prose

- AI loves structure because structured data costs **less compute** to process
- Nine paragraphs explaining why you went to the University of Florida vs. one structured field saying *"Education: University of Florida."* Same information, vastly different cost
- Lower cost = more frequent training inclusion + more frequent grounding retrieval
- This is a primary reason **MapQuest and similar listings** appear so heavily in AI citations. The structure is exceptional

### The Elo / head-to-head ranking experiment

- Yext built **Scout**, which uses **H3 hexagonal geographic resolution** to scan target businesses AND their local competitors per query
- A coffee shop in Roswell, GA does NOT need the same strategy as a coffee shop in Times Square. **The competitive set is fundamentally different**
- Adapted **Elo rankings** (chess, FIFA, college football) for SEO ranking analysis
- **21M head-to-head search queries** analyzed. Test variable: does updating data consistently in real time across all listings actually move ranks?
- **Results:**
  - **~3 ranking points** lift on average across the full 21M dataset
  - **Small businesses** lift ~5 points
  - **Hyper-competitive markets** (coffee in NYC, etc.) lift **~6.2 points**
  - Industry variance: in ultra-saturated location categories (coffee shops in dense urban areas), **location proximity dominates everything else**, including data quality

### The brand-identity sprawl problem

- AI does not see one version of your brand. It sees **many**: today's brand, last year's brand, blog posts you forgot to take down 9 years ago, old product pages
- This is one of the structural reasons **freshness signals matter so much**. AI uses recency to disambiguate which version of you is current
- If you update your website but don't update the third-party listings, you are sending a **mixed signal** that the model resolves probabilistically (and often wrong)
- **Consistency across the data supply chain is a primary signal AI uses to evaluate accuracy.** The classic sushi example: if 10 New Yorkers all say *"go to Bond"* you trust it. **AI works the same way mathematically**

### How AI evaluates accuracy — the four signals

- **Source authority.** Where is the information coming from?
- **Cross-source corroboration.** How many other authoritative sources say the same thing?
- **Update frequency / recency.** When was this last updated? How often?
- **Consistency.** Do all sources agree, or do they conflict?
- Optimize for all four. The biggest miss for most brands is **consistency across the data supply chain**

### Personalization is moving from surveillance to AI context

![Yext Research slide — "'Personalization' stops stalking us / Memory Rewrites Visibility." Memory tells AI who I am. Context tells AI what I need. Relationships tell AI why I care. OLD: Track the user (cookies, clicks, trails). NEW: AI finally delivers personalization — marketers do NOT get the data. Foundation becomes MEMORY + CONTEXT + RELATIONSHIPS. "Give the model better facts."](https://wsrv.nl/?url=https%3A%2F%2Fcustomer-assets.emergentagent.com%2Fjob_github-checker-8%2Fartifacts%2Fq9qikfif_IMG_2749.jpg&w=1080&q=70&output=webp)

- The 20-year history of digital marketing was effectively **user-level surveillance**: tracking pixels, cross-site cookies, browsing behavior, demographic enrichment
- *"You followed people around, looked through their trash, knew where their kids went to school"* is the cynical summary of that era
- That model is **dying**. Personalization moves into the AI's own **context layer**. Your AI knows you because **you told it**, not because you were tracked
- Surveillance-based personalization is being replaced by **consent-based, context-based personalization owned by the user's AI**
- **Loyalty programs as a callback:** physical loyalty cards died. **AI with perfect memory will resurrect loyalty mechanics.** Make sure your offers, perks, and brand promise are discoverable

### Quotes worth keeping

> "You put garbage into AI, and the masterpiece comes out."

> "This conference has been admiring the problem."

> "The website becomes the conveyor belt of structured knowledge to a conversational interface."

> "Any system that is not real-time will lose to one that is."

> "Reddit might be a brand problem. It's not your local-intent problem."

> "Unless you're a spiritual being, your physical location is one of the most important pieces of context AI can know about you."

> "AI doesn't see one brand. It sees many versions of your brand."

> "Citation per scan rose 28% quarter over quarter. The models are not citing less. They are citing more."

### Open questions

- How does the brand-down vs intent-up citation graph diverge for B2B SaaS, where physical location is irrelevant?
- What is the right cadence for re-syncing data across all listings to capture the freshness benefit without introducing noise?
- For brands with 1,000+ locations, what's the operational model to keep all locations in real-time consistency?
- How does Yext's Elo methodology handle queries where there is no clear competitive set (highly niche or emerging categories)?
- When ads ship in AI search at scale, will the listings advantage compress as paid placement disrupts organic citation patterns?
- Will Apple's open-model Siri produce a different local-citation graph than Google or ChatGPT?

### Action items

- Stop running brand-only AI visibility studies. **Add location and intent** to every priority prompt and rerun the analysis
- Map your full **citation supply chain**. List every place your brand data lives (website, GBP, Yelp, MapQuest, social, reviews, internal CMS)
- Audit **data consistency** across all listings. For top 10 fields (name, address, hours, services, pricing), check whether every source agrees
- Build a **real-time data update workflow**. Whenever brand data changes on the website, propagate to every listing within **hours, not weeks**
- For multi-location brands, audit the **H3 hexagonal competitive set** per location. Customize per market
- Audit historical web content. Identify outdated brand pages still cited in AI. Update or remove
- Convert prose to **structured data** wherever possible. Schema, JSON-LD, structured fields. Reduce the model's compute cost to process you
- Add **freshness signals** (last-updated dates, version markers) on top brand and product pages
- For local businesses, prioritize **listings hygiene before content production**. Listings beat content for local-intent queries
- Assume Apple's open-model Siri rollout is imminent. Plan for citation patterns to **fragment further** across model providers
- Visit **yext.com/research** for the full studies, datasets, and ongoing analysis
- Pair this session with **Profound's accuracy framework** and **iPullRank's relevance metrics**. Together they cover content quality + accuracy + supply chain
takeaways: Every AI visibility study runs brand-down — consumers ask with location + intent, which produces a completely different citation graph dominated by websites, Google Business Profile, MapQuest, Yelp
Yext analyzed 17M citations in Q4 2025 and 155M in Q1 2026 — citations per scan rose 28% QoQ (models cite more, not less)
March 2026 survey of 1,120 adults: 59% use AI for general search, 47% for local, 52% of restaurant search has moved to AI — highest earners now START in AI, not Google
Four citation control tiers: Full (website), High (listings), Limited (social/reviews), Zero (Reddit/news) — most brands waste energy on the bottom two
Elo head-to-head on 21M queries: real-time data consistency lifts ranks ~3 pts avg, ~5 for small businesses, ~6.2 in hyper-competitive markets
Structure beats prose because it costs less compute — this is why MapQuest-style listings dominate AI citations
AI accuracy = source authority + cross-source corroboration + freshness + consistency; consistency is the biggest miss
Personalization leaves surveillance — memory/context/relationships live in the AI's context layer, marketers WILL NOT get that data

## Crystal Carter — When Agents Fuel the Funnel: Optimizations for the New Validation Layer

**Key thesis:** Agents are no longer hypothetical. **~60% of enterprises are deploying agents**, Salesforce's Marc Benioff claims **25,000 of 60,000 employees will be AI agents**, and Apple just announced **Gemini will power Siri**. The classic marketing funnel is breaking apart because **consideration and evaluation are now done by agents, not humans** — the user only re-enters at **validation and purchase**. To stay relevant, websites need three things: **technical alignment** with agent protocols (MCP, AP2, NLWeb, A2A), **on-site context** that helps agents safely and confidently recommend you, and **audience-affirming content** that proves your offering is for the specific person the agent is serving. Brands with **singular intent** (L'Easy hats, NerdWallet's audience-specific deals) win. Brands that try to be everything to everyone lose.

![Crystal Carter on the SEO Week 2026 Future stage in a red dress, breaking down how agents rewrite the marketing funnel](https://wsrv.nl/?url=https%3A%2F%2Fcustomer-assets.emergentagent.com%2Fjob_github-checker-8%2Fartifacts%2Fxjn7y299_IMG_2766.jpg&w=1080&q=70&output=webp)

### TL;DR

Agents are now mainstream — Salesforce is replacing a third of its workforce with them, Apple is shipping Gemini inside Siri, and 32% of Americans say their #1 want from AI is an assistant that **does stuff**. That breaks the funnel: agents run consideration and evaluation, humans re-appear only at **validation** and **purchase**. To win, align your site with emerging protocols (MCP, AP2, NLWeb, A2A), make sure your brand is logically perceivable and comparable so agents can confidently recommend you, and build **audience-affirming content** (NerdWallet's audience-specific offer pages, Gymshark's profile-tagged reviews) that proves your fit. **Singular intent wins. Trying to be everything to everyone loses.**

### Why agents, why now

- **~60% of enterprises** are actively deploying agents. Some businesses are using them without realizing — Salesforce, Monday, and similar platforms are baking agents in
- **Marc Benioff (Salesforce):** of his 60,000 employees, **25,000 are AI agents**
- **32% of Americans** say their #1 want from AI is to act as an **assistant** — more than content editing, more than community help, more than a Disney pass
- Crystal's TL;DR for explaining agents: **"agents do stuff."** They handle work humans don't want to do
- What humans don't want to do: fill out forms, compare products across stores, monitor flight prices, manage payment confirmations, multi-step errands
- What's coming next: hotel availability checks, automatic rebooking when travel disrupts, multi-step planning

### Agents are everywhere already

- **Gemini** is now in Google Home, Workspace, Chrome, and Android
- Gemini will **screen phone calls** on Android. Crystal called her niece and Gemini answered *"do you want to talk to her?"*
- **Apple just announced Gemini will power Siri.** Major iOS user base about to get first-hand AI agent experience
- Protocols proliferating: **MCP, A2A (Agent-to-Agent), AP2 (Agentic Payments Protocol), Universal Commerce Protocol, WebMCP, NLWeb**
- *"You get a protocol, you get a protocol"* — **the web is being rebuilt for agentic users**

### The funnel is breaking (again)

- **Classic funnel:** awareness, interest, consideration, evaluation, purchase
- Google's **"messy middle"** already showed it isn't linear
- Now: the user has interest and intent. **Consideration and evaluation get handed to an agent.** The user only re-engages at **validation and purchase**
- The brand may not even surface to the human until the validation step. **Most brand-marketing energy aimed at "consideration" is now aimed at agents, not people**

### How intent works inside agents

- Agent intent comes from **three sources**: the **prompt** (what the user just asked), the **user profile** (ChatGPT's *"what is your job? what is your name?"* baked-in context), and the **system prompt of the tool itself**
- Example system prompt: *"You are an agent, a financial analyst that retrieves market data, executes searches, and delivers concise insights."* The agent has consistent intent every time it runs, regardless of user prompt
- Within ChatGPT or Claude, individual tools (find-your-hike, check-travel-variants) carry their own intent. **If your category has 10 popular agents, your site needs to match what those 10 agents need**
- **Brands with singular intent thrive.** L'Easy sells hats. Nothing else. Easy for an agent to map *"I want a hat"* → L'Easy
- Brands that try to do everything are harder to map. **Agents will skip them** in favor of brands they can confidently recommend

### How agents do consideration and evaluation

- Agents crawl **hundreds of websites in minutes**. Reasonable decisions in **milliseconds**
- **Brand needs to be logically perceivable.** Don't make agents work to figure out who you are and what you sell
- **Confidence:** the agent needs to be able to **confidently recommend** you. If your site doesn't make that easy, you don't get recommended
- **Comparable:** have explicit comparison signals so agents can place you against alternatives
- **Audience proof:** make it clear **who your offering is for**, with evidence

### The validation layer (where the human re-enters)

- **Agent validates:** can it transact safely? Does the protocol work? Is the recommendation backed by evidence?
- **Microwave / air-fryer combo example.** If Crystal's agent says *"this is a great oven,"* there has to be evidence. If she asks *"will it steam vegetables?"* and the site can't answer, she won't buy
- Decisions need confluence with the user's baked-in context. If Crystal said she's vegan, the agent shouldn't recommend a pot roast
- **Human validates:** are the recommendations real? Did the agent get my brief right? Did it understand *"vegan birthday party"* as I intended?

### The optimization layer — site tech alignment

- Make your site **accessible to agents.** Secure but transactable. Interoperable with their protocols
- **AP2 (Agentic Payments Protocol)** is Google's plan for agentic shopping. Builds on familiar pieces (APIs, MCP) and pulls them together
- Shopping feeds (already useful for Google Shopping) extend to AP2. **RSS feeds** also help
- **NLWeb (Microsoft)** is a building block. Lets agents read site content and structure in a way they can act on
- You may need a **protocol pivot.** AP2 isn't useful for every product type — subscriptions, personalized name-batch products, bundles, restricted goods (alcohol) may not be eligible
- **Workaround:** offer one-off versions of subscription products to make them AP2-compatible

### Security and partnerships matter

- Agents need to do good work **safely.** Big tech companies are aligning on safe transaction standards
- **Wix** is a signatory for AP2 and integrates with **Stripe's** agentic commerce suite
- **PayPal** has agentic commerce services integrated into eligible Wix sites
- Check your platform partners. They may already have agentic commerce tooling you can plug into

### Interoperability — be where agents work

- Wix has a **Claude skill** that lets people generate websites inside ChatGPT and Claude using MCP
- Find ways to make your site **actionable inside agentic environments.** If a user is working in Claude or ChatGPT, can they accomplish your transaction without leaving?
- Configure your **MCP server** with the parameters you want. **You don't have to expose everything**
- Add MCP support to existing services. Dealers, hospitality, hotels all have specific protocols emerging

### NLWeb explained

- Microsoft's **NLWeb** (with the FastAPI protocol) lets an agent visit your site, query in real time, and use your structured data, MCP, schema.org markup, and HTML tags to answer the user's question
- **Reduces hallucination** because the agent grounds answers in your actual site content
- Allows agents to answer using natural language while respecting security
- If your site has a well-configured MCP plus structured data, agents in Claude or ChatGPT can **complete their user's task without leaving the agentic environment**

### Audience-affirming content — the most overlooked layer

- **Audience-affirming content** clearly illustrates who your products or services are for
- Agents are **serving someone.** They need to know your content matches their user. ChatGPT memory already knows who its user is
- **NerdWallet example:** dedicated offer pages for **students, military, teachers, first responders, healthcare professionals**. If an agent serves a teacher, NerdWallet has explicit evidence the offer matches
- **Recipe sites** doing this well: gluten-free, dairy-free, low-FODMAP variations made explicit. Lots of FAQs with audience-specific framing
- **Gymshark reviews** are best-in-class. Each review explicitly states the reviewer's profile: *"I do strength training 3–6 times a week, age 45–54."* Same product, different reviewer profiles. **Agents serving different users find different evidence**

### Evidence patterns that work for agents

- Dedicated discount or offer pages by audience type
- **Audience-tagged reviews** (Gymshark model)
- Partner programs (university partnerships, professional associations) with public landing pages
- YouTube reviews from creators who explicitly serve the audience
- Make every claim about who your offering serves **backed by something an agent can verify**

### Quotes worth keeping

> "Agents do stuff. That's the TL;DR."

> "Agents do the stuff humans don't want to do."

> "The web is being rebuilt for agentic users."

> "Brands with singular intent will thrive."

> "You get a protocol, you get a protocol."

> "Brand is also utility. If your site doesn't give agents an opportunity to do stuff, you'll have a harder time in this era."

> "Make sure your brand is logically perceivable."

> "Agents are serving someone. Make it clear who you are for."

### Open questions

- If brands with singular intent thrive, what's the right strategy for category-spanning conglomerates and retailers?
- How quickly will MCP, AP2, NLWeb consolidate vs. fragment? Should you implement everything or wait for a winner?
- For brands without subscription/transactional surfaces, how does AP2 readiness translate?
- What's the minimum viable audience-affirming content footprint to be discoverable by an agent serving that audience?
- How do you measure agent traffic and conversion separately from human traffic in analytics today?
- If agents skip ahead to validation, do brand-awareness campaigns still work the way they used to?

### Action items

- Test your site as an agent. Run *"what is this brand for? Can an agent confidently recommend us for [target audience]?"* through ChatGPT, Gemini, Claude
- Audit **singular intent.** If you sell hats, lead with hats. If you do everything, segment your site by use case so agents can match cleanly
- Identify the **top 5–10 popular agents** in your category. Map what intents they carry. Make sure your site matches at least one cleanly
- Audit your e-commerce platform partners (Wix, Shopify, BigCommerce, etc.). What agentic commerce protocols do they already support? Activate them
- Check **AP2 product eligibility.** For ineligible product types (subscriptions, personalized, restricted), evaluate whether to offer an AP2-compatible variant
- Configure or audit your **MCP server.** Decide what tools to expose. Don't expose everything by default
- Implement **NLWeb** support if your platform allows. Reduces hallucination, improves agent recommendation quality
- Build **dedicated audience-affirming pages**: by profession (teachers, healthcare, military), by use case, by life stage. Mirror the NerdWallet pattern
- Add **audience tagging to reviews.** Encourage reviewers to state their profile (Gymshark model)
- Create FAQ content that explicitly states variations: dietary, accessibility, life stage, etc.
- Make every claim about audience fit **verifiable.** If you say *"great for runners,"* show evidence (reviews, partnerships, third-party validation)
- Read **Wix Studio's AI Search Lab** content (interviews with James Cadwallader, Stephanie Ray, etc.) for ongoing protocol updates
takeaways: ~60% of enterprises are deploying agents; Salesforce's Benioff says 25,000 of 60,000 employees will be AI agents; Apple just announced Gemini will power Siri
The funnel breaks — agents run consideration and evaluation, humans only re-enter at validation and purchase
Agent intent has three sources: the user prompt, the baked-in user profile, and the tool's system prompt — match at least one intent of the top 5–10 agents in your category
Brands with SINGULAR intent thrive (L'Easy = hats). Brands that try to be everything to everyone get skipped by agents
Stack the tech alignment: MCP, AP2 (Agentic Payments Protocol), NLWeb (Microsoft), A2A, Universal Commerce Protocol — check your platform partners first
NLWeb + well-configured MCP lets agents complete transactions inside Claude/ChatGPT without leaving — huge for interoperability
Audience-affirming content is the most overlooked lever — NerdWallet's profession-specific offer pages, Gymshark's profile-tagged reviews are the models
Every audience-fit claim needs evidence an agent can verify (partnerships, dedicated landing pages, tagged reviews, third-party validation)

## Jordan Leschinsky — Earned Architecture for AI Visibility

**Key thesis:** Everything you own (your website, your blog, your code) is just the **entry fee** for AI visibility. The actual engine is everything you **earn**. AI is now acting as a **global brand PR for your company — with no contract, no agreement, no accountability**. To survive, SEO has to merge with PR, social, and community work. Jordan's **earned architecture** stacks owned content as the floor, then earned media, traditional PR, source databases, and community management on top — because real influence happens in the consensus AI is consuming. Real audit data: for one major brand, **editorial content drove 54% of AI visibility**; owned content drove **single digits on unbranded queries**. The places where you most need visibility are the places you have least control over. The shift is from optimizing your **website** to optimizing **the web**.

![Jordan Leschinsky on the SEO Week 2026 Future stage — title slide "Earned Architecture for AI Visibility," Jordan Leschinsky, VP Strategy, Vayner Media](https://wsrv.nl/?url=https%3A%2F%2Fcustomer-assets.emergentagent.com%2Fjob_github-checker-8%2Fartifacts%2Fqngwn8vz_Screenshot%25202026-04-30%2520at%25203.11.23%25E2%2580%25AFPM.png&w=1080&q=70&output=webp)

### TL;DR

Showing up in an AI list is not the same as being recommended by AI. Jordan's audit of Nike (and the same pattern across pet care, finance, and other industries) showed editorial content drives **~54% of AI visibility**, social drives **~25%**, and owned content lands a distant third — collapsing to **~2% on unbranded queries**, the very moments you need new audience the most. AI doesn't know what's true; it knows the **published consensus**. To shape that consensus, SEO has to merge with PR, social, and community. The unit of work shifts from *"another blog post on our site"* to *"where else can we credibly contribute to the consensus AI is consuming about us."*

### The reframe — traffic isn't the goal anymore

- Most online retailers and publishers don't actually care about traffic for its own sake. Traffic is the necessary evil to drive what matters: **revenue and brand**
- **Wil Reynolds** said the same thing on Day 1. Traffic is a vanity metric if it doesn't drive the business outcome
- Industry has evolved partway. Clients stopped asking *"is my traffic up?"* and started asking *"am I visible in AI search?"*
- That's directionally right, but **not far enough**. Showing up in an AI list isn't the same as winning the recommendation

### The Ordinary skincare example

- Jordan asked Gemini for skincare recommendations. Got a list. **The Ordinary appeared as a top option**
- As the conversation progressed, the recommendation **softened**. By the end, Gemini was telling her to *"put The Ordinary down and walk away slowly"*
- Visibility was 100%. The actual recommendation was **negative**
- The lesson: **showing up in AI is not the same as being recommended by AI.** Brand sentiment inside the AI conversation is the metric that matters, not appearance

### AI as your unaccountable global PR

- The shift is not about losing traffic. **It's about losing brand-goodness control**
- AI is no longer just a summarization assistant. It's acting as a **global brand PR with no contract, no agreement, no accountability**
- AI doesn't know what's true. **It knows what the published consensus says is true.** That's what it returns
- If the consensus is wrong about your brand, AI confidently tells the world your brand is whatever the wrong consensus says it is

### The digital PR misalignment example

- Jordan asked PR teams whether *"digital PR"* is something they do. The answer was **no.** They don't use the term. To them, **all PR is digital now**
- Asked AI to define digital PR. AI said the #1 focus is *"securing do-follow backlinks"*
- That's an SEO definition, not a PR definition. PR practitioners don't measure success in backlinks. They measure **narratives in target publications**
- If you get coverage in NYT or WSJ, you usually don't get a backlink at all (or it's nofollow). **Real PR isn't a link-building exercise**
- SEOs have been dominating the digital PR conversation online with 200-word blog posts about backlink tactics. PR practitioners themselves haven't been publishing about their work. So **AI's definition of PR is whatever the SEO industry has been saying about PR**
- *"SEOs don't have a PR problem. PR has an SEO problem."* Their narrative is being shaped by people who don't actually do their job

![Jordan mid-keynote on the SEO Week stage walking the audience through the earned-architecture audit data](https://wsrv.nl/?url=https%3A%2F%2Fcustomer-assets.emergentagent.com%2Fjob_github-checker-8%2Fartifacts%2Fge1bqlj7_IMG_2774.jpg&w=1080&q=70&output=webp)

### The Nike audit (real data)

- Jordan ran a full GEO audit on **Nike** (well-known enough that scale exposes the pattern)
- **Editorial content (PR, articles, journalism, third-party media) drove 54% of Nike's AI visibility**
- **Social drove ~25%**
- **Owned content (Nike.com) came in third**
- **Branded queries** (where you'd expect Nike.com to dominate) — Nike.com performed well, as expected
- **Unbranded queries** (the ones where you actually need to win net-new audience): **Nike.com showed up single digits, ~2% of the time**
- The single most important visibility moment for new audience acquisition is where owned content is **structurally weakest**

### The pattern is industry-agnostic

- Jordan ran the same audit across **pet care, finance, and other industries**
- **Same shape every time.** Owned content is the entry fee. The earned ecosystem is the engine
- The percentages varied by industry, but the pattern held: **editorial and earned media dominate.** Owned content drives a fraction of unbranded visibility
- If your team budget is mostly aimed at owned content, **you're underfunded against the actual influence ecosystem**

### The earned architecture framework

- **Owned (the floor):** your website, blog, code. Necessary entry fee. SEOs already do this well
- **Earned media (PR, traditional or digital):** editorial placements, journalism, podcast interviews, event panels. SEOs and PR converge here. **Stop chasing only NYT and WSJ.** Look for outlets that actually appear in AI's source set for your category
- **Source databases / experts:** Quora, Reddit, Wikipedia, Substack authors, podcasters, influencers. **Treat them like journalists.** Build relationships
- **Community management (the hardest, most valuable):** Reddit first, then everywhere else. Long-term play. Engage authentically, contribute, educate, respond. **Activate subject-matter experts, executives, even your engineers and designers**
- **Social content created for AI:** doesn't have to be optimized for human engagement. AI algorithms filter for relevance. **Post AI-ready social content even if it doesn't perform with humans**
- The discipline above everything: **SEO, PR, social, brand all working together**

### PR has the skills SEO doesn't

- PR knows how to build relationships with **journalists, authors, podcasters, influencers**
- SEO can guide which outlets actually matter for AI visibility (per the audit data)
- PR's traditional metric (**share of voice**) translates well to AI. Track narrative themes, not just mention counts
- The intersection: **SEO tells PR which outlets to target based on AI source maps. PR opens the doors. Together, you shape the consensus AI is reading**

### How to do an AI visibility audit — Jordan's rules

- Audits are **highly manipulable.** You can pick prompts that make any brand look great or terrible. The industry needs a standard
- **Rule 1:** separate **branded from unbranded** prompts. Analyze them apart. Awareness and consideration tactics differ
- **Rule 2:** use **personas.** Prompt as a college student, a parent, a marathon runner. Each persona surfaces different sources. **YouTube dominated for college students.** Reddit only surfaced for **parents looking for community support**
- **Rule 3:** hold the **master prompt constant.** Change ONE variable at a time (brand, persona, product type). Compare across consistent baselines
- **Rule 4:** reject the GEO-as-answer-engine framing. **AI is a conversation, not an answer engine.** Prompt across the full conversation flow, not just the first response

![Jordan on stage during the audit walkthrough — close-up of the Earned Architecture deck mid-talk](https://wsrv.nl/?url=https%3A%2F%2Fcustomer-assets.emergentagent.com%2Fjob_github-checker-8%2Fartifacts%2F9ujt0ck2_IMG_2775.jpg&w=1080&q=70&output=webp)

### Track the conversation, not just the first response

- The Ordinary went from *"top recommendation"* to *"put it down"* within **one conversation**
- Most AI visibility tools only track the **first response** to a prompt. That's not the whole picture
- Use a tool that tracks the **full conversation.** Trio Sense was Jordan's recommendation
- For the same brands she audited, conversation-level tracking showed **visibility shifts of 50%+** from first response to deeper turns

### Stop publishing only on your site

- Spending all your content effort on your owned website is contributing to a **fraction** of where AI is actually getting its sources
- Activate **subject-matter experts.** Encourage them to publish on third-party platforms. Build podcast appearances. Get interviewed
- Create AI-optimized social content even if it doesn't perform for humans. **AI is reading social**
- The unit of work shifts from *"another blog post on our site"* to *"where else can we credibly contribute to the consensus AI is consuming about us"*

### Quotes worth keeping

> "Everything you own is the entry fee. Everything you can earn is the engine."

> "AI is acting as our global brand PR — with no contract or agreement in place."

> "AI doesn't know what's true. It knows what the published consensus is, as truth."

> "SEOs don't have a PR problem. PR has an SEO problem."

> "Showing up in the list isn't enough. The recommendation is what matters."

> "Optimize the web, not just the website."

> "It's not about answering anymore. It's about being part of the conversation."

### Open questions

- For mid-market brands without dedicated PR teams, what's the minimum viable earned-architecture investment?
- How do you measure earned-media impact on AI visibility quickly enough to justify ongoing investment?
- How do you avoid the cherry-picked-prompt problem in audits when standardizing across an agency client portfolio?
- For brands with negative AI sentiment (like The Ordinary), what's the recovery path? Counter-narratives, reviewer partnerships, or rebuilt owned content?
- Are there industries where owned content still dominates AI visibility, or has the earned-architecture pattern fully generalized?
- What's the right org structure to actually merge SEO, PR, social, and community work? Reporting lines, KPIs, budget integration?

### Action items

- Run Jordan's GEO audit framework on your top brand or client. Branded vs unbranded prompts. Multiple personas. **Full conversation, not just first response**
- Use **Trio Sense** or equivalent for conversation-level tracking. Compare visibility at first response vs end of conversation
- Quantify the split: what percentage of your AI visibility comes from owned vs earned vs social vs community? Use the result to **reset budget allocation**
- Identify the editorial outlets that actually drive your AI visibility. **Stop chasing only the prestige names.** Map outlet importance to category-specific AI source data
- Connect SEO with PR. Share the audit. Make outlet selection a joint exercise
- Build a Reddit strategy if you don't have one. Start small. Engage authentically. Treat it as **long-term community investment**
- Activate SMEs across the org (executives, engineers, designers, product) to publish on third-party platforms
- Create AI-optimized social content. Don't worry about human engagement metrics. **Optimize for relevance signals AI reads**
- Audit existing AI sentiment on your brand. If conversation-level analysis reveals negative drift, prioritize counter-narrative content in earned channels first, owned channels second
- Stop optimizing only your website. Allocate **at least 50% of new content effort** to earned and community channels
- Reframe internal reporting from *"AI visibility share"* to *"AI conversation sentiment + share."* Track both
takeaways: Owned content is the entry fee, earned media is the engine — Nike audit: editorial drove 54% of AI visibility, social ~25%, owned content single digits (~2%) on UNBRANDED queries
Showing up in AI ≠ being recommended — The Ordinary went from 'top pick' to 'put it down and walk away' inside ONE Gemini conversation
AI doesn't know what's true; it knows the published consensus — it's now your global brand PR with no contract or accountability
SEOs don't have a PR problem — PR has an SEO problem; AI's definition of 'digital PR' is whatever the SEO industry blogged about backlinks
Earned architecture stack: Owned (floor) → Earned media → Source databases (Quora, Reddit, Wikipedia, podcasters) → Community management → AI-optimized social
Audit rules: separate branded vs unbranded, use personas (college student vs parent vs marathon runner), hold master prompt constant, track the FULL conversation not just first response (Trio Sense)
YouTube dominated for college students; Reddit only surfaced for parents seeking community — persona surfaces different source sets
Reallocate at least 50% of new content effort to earned and community channels — stop publishing only on your owned site

## Brittan King — Managing the FUD Out of Change: Cognitive Sovereignty in the Age of AI

**Key thesis:** FUD (fear, uncertainty, doubt) is **not a feeling — it's a deliberate strategy**. It has been used since Machiavelli, weaponized by Big Tobacco for 20 years, and is now being deployed at **AI scale** to manipulate organizational decision-making. The amygdala fires before rational thought. Uncertainty is more stressful than confirmed bad news. Doubt is exhausting because belief is the default. The antidote is **cognitive sovereignty**: the capacity to remain the genuine author of your own thinking. The shift: **from fear to fuel, from uncertainty to understanding, from doubt to discernment**. The frame: stop chasing categorical certainty (which is fake right now) and embrace **clarity through ongoing ambiguity**. Bob Johansen's *Full Spectrum Thinking* and the inverted VUCA framework are the operating manual.

![Brittan King on the SEO Week 2026 Psychology stage — white one-shoulder top, black skirt, closing out the FUD-to-cognitive-sovereignty talk](https://wsrv.nl/?url=https%3A%2F%2Fcustomer-assets.emergentagent.com%2Fjob_github-checker-8%2Fartifacts%2Frpjjq92i_Brittan%2520King.jpg&w=1080&q=70&output=webp)

### TL;DR

FUD is a deliberate decision-attack strategy — same playbook Big Tobacco used for 20 years, now running at AI speed and scale. The neuroscience: amygdala fires first, uncertainty hurts more than a confirmed punch, doubt is more effortful than belief. The antidote is **cognitive sovereignty** — staying the genuine author of your own thinking. Invert VUCA (Volatility→Vision, Uncertainty→Understanding, Complexity→Clarity, Ambiguity→Agility), default to belief, pick what to doubt, and treat fear as fuel. Reward clarity, **punish certainty** — because right now, certainty is fake.

### What FUD actually is

- **Fear, uncertainty, doubt.** A deliberate strategy designed to **attack decision quality**
- The phrase dates to the 1920s. The pattern dates to Machiavelli
- It is meant to influence perception via propaganda. **It's not an accident or a feeling. It's a tool**
- Used in sales, parental-control software, political ads, defense procurement, IBM-era enterprise tech, Big Tobacco
- AI is now simultaneously the greatest FUD-generation machine ever built **and** the most powerful tool for eliminating FUD inside organizations. Same technology, opposite uses

### The decision-quality crisis right now

- Major business decisions are stalling. Why? **Past data no longer reliably predicts the future**
- Annual budget planning used to be based on the prior year. Now neither side knows what the year will look like
- **67% of marketing leaders** expect major AI-driven disruption. The number is functionally **100%**
- **83% of consumers** expect disclosure when AI is being used in content. **It almost never is**
- Trust is the top decision driver, but deepfakes and AI-generated content are **eroding it faster than disclosure norms are forming**

### The neuroscience of FUD — the body always knows first

- The **amygdala hijacks** the body before the prefrontal cortex even processes the threat. Fight-or-flight fires first
- It feels like a bear, but it's just a deadline or an angry email
- Three-stage loop:
  - **Uncertainty creates doubt**
  - **Doubt creates fear**
  - **Fear creates uncertainty**
- Self-completing circuit. One headline can trigger it. Each cycle reinforces the next
- Like a **sprained ankle** — the more often you roll it, the easier it rolls again. FUD has the same mechanic

### The Big Tobacco case study

- Tobacco companies started seeing the link between smoking and cancer in the **1940s**
- The Surgeon General's warning didn't come until **1964**. They had a **20-year window**
- They got ahead of it with marketing campaigns featuring doctors and dentists endorsing specific brands
- *"Lucky Strike is toasted. It protects your throat"* became a category-wide framing device
- The lesson: a coordinated FUD campaign with credible-looking authority figures can **postpone consensus on objective harm for two decades**
- The pattern is now being run at **AI scale across multiple categories**. The timeline compresses, but the strategy is the same

### The Google story — FUD inside the seller

- Two years ago, before Bard was renamed Gemini, Brittan was at Google. Major enterprise clients were demanding *"an AI presentation from Google"* with no specific question or scope
- Google teams were freaking out trying to deliver something. **Clients couldn't articulate what they wanted**
- The reality: clients didn't know what to ask. Their CEOs were panicking. **The panic flowed downstream as urgent vague asks**
- FUD doesn't just shape buyers. **It shapes sellers too.** The pressure to respond to engineered urgency burns time and credibility on both sides

### The future requires Full Spectrum Thinking

- Reference: **Bob Johansen**, *Full Spectrum Thinking* (Institute for the Future)
- **Categorical thinking** promotes certainty: this is purple, that is gold, that is good, this is bad. It feels safe
- Categorical thinking is being **weaponized** against us. It locks us to outdated data and prevents adaptation
- **Full spectrum thinking** moves toward clarity while accepting non-certainty. Uncomfortable, but accurate
- **The future will reward clarity but punish certainty**
- Categories are fake right now. We do not have certainty about the future. Clinging to it makes us **easier to manipulate**

### The VUCA inversion (from the US Army War College)

- Original **VUCA:** Volatility, Uncertainty, Complexity, Ambiguity. Used to describe the post-Cold War world
- **Johansen's flip:**
  - **Volatility → Vision.** Clear direction without demanding certainty
  - **Uncertainty → Understanding.** What do we know more today than yesterday?
  - **Complexity → Clarity.** Open thinking, not closed thinking. *"That didn't work last time"* is closed. *"Let's try it again differently"* is open
  - **Ambiguity → Agility.** Married to the end result, not the path. Pivot freely
- FUD exploits the original VUCA. **The inversion is the antidote**

### Fear as a signal, not a strategy

- Fear means you give a fuck about something. **It's a compass**
- *"You can be afraid. You should be. You just need to be more brave than scared"* (Brittan to her daughter)
- Fear is **fuel for action** when you treat it as information instead of instruction
- Use fear to do the things that scare you (creative work, public speaking, hard conversations) instead of avoiding them
- **Mountain-biking example** from the audience: training and fundamentals eliminated the kids' fear of the trails. **The antidote to fear is competence**

### Uncertainty as understanding

- The brain finds **uncertainty MORE stressful than confirmed bad news.** The Mike Tyson framing: *"the surprise hurts more than the punch"*
- When you cannot plan, biology takes over. Cortisol, adrenaline, no time to think
- The fix: **name the uncertainty.** *"I don't know if this will work. Nobody does."* That admission is itself stabilizing
- **Self-awareness is the lever.** If you know you're stressed, you can apply the right tool (rest, exercise, restorative work) before the next decision
- You can't make the world certain. **You can change your relationship to its uncertainty**

### Doubt as discernment

- **Belief is the default cognitive state. Doubt requires effort**
- Healthy skepticism is fine. Doubting everything is exhausting and self-reinforcing
- The pervasive sense of burnout, brain fog, and overwhelm in the industry right now is partly an effect of **constant doubt**
- The antidote: **discernment.** Pick what to doubt deliberately. Default to belief on the rest. Conserve cognitive energy
- Discernment requires knowing the difference between a **real signal and engineered noise**

### Cognitive sovereignty — the central concept

- **Definition:** the capacity to remain the genuine author of your own thinking, attention, and focus — free from digital algorithms and external manipulation
- **Personal version:** you choose what to consume, how to participate, when to think critically
- **Organizational version:** the capacity of a leadership team and brand to make decisions from **signal rather than engineered noise** — to remain the genuine author of your strategy, culture, and market position in the age of AI-generated content at scale
- It's the difference between organizations that **lead** and organizations that **react out of fear**
- Cognitive sovereignty does NOT mean ignoring market factors. It means **knowing the difference between a signal worth responding to and a threat engineered to provoke a response**

### The new FUD

- **Fuel** instead of Fear
- **Understanding** instead of Uncertainty
- **Discernment** instead of Doubt
- Goal: maintain cognitive sovereignty individually and bring it to your organization. **That posture is itself the differentiator**

### What this looks like in practice for marketers

- The patience is gone. Clients and bosses are pushing urgent vague asks. **Most of that urgency is fake panic, not real signal**
- Most companies don't actually know how much they should spend on marketing. There's no benchmark. They're **guessing under pressure**
- People are sending snippy emails because they're **afraid of losing their jobs**, not because the work is bad
- **Compassion for the panic on the other side of the table changes the conversation.** They're scared. So are you
- Show up with grounded direction. The right inputs, the right framing, and a willingness to acknowledge *"nobody knows for sure"* can be more reassuring than any false certainty

### Quotes worth keeping

> "FUD is an attack on your decision quality."

> "Fear is not a feeling, it's a strategy."

> "The future will reward clarity but punish certainty."

> "Categories are fake. We do not have certainty about the future."

> "Uncertainty is more stressful than confirmed bad news."

> "Belief is the default cognitive state. Doubt requires effort."

> "Be more brave than scared."

> "Cognitive sovereignty is the difference between organizations that lead and those that react."

> "From fear to fuel. From uncertainty to understanding. From doubt to discernment."

### Open questions

- How do you institutionalize cognitive sovereignty into hiring, onboarding, and leadership development?
- What does the equivalent of a Full Spectrum Thinking framework look like for product roadmapping under AI uncertainty?
- How do you tell the difference between a real signal and engineered noise when both come from credible-looking sources?
- For agency owners and consultants, how do you sell discernment to a client culture that pays for certainty?
- If FUD is being deployed at AI scale, what does an organizational immune system look like?
- How does the VUCA-to-V/U/C/A inversion translate into actual planning cadences, KPIs, and post-mortems?

### Action items

- Read **Full Spectrum Thinking** by Bob Johansen
- Inventory the urgent vague asks you've received in the last month. For each, identify whether it's a **real signal or engineered noise**
- Practice **naming fear** when it appears in a meeting. *"I notice we're rushing because we're worried about being behind. Is that the right reason to make this decision?"*
- Build a personal **regulation routine**: how do you reset your nervous system between high-pressure decisions? Yoga, walks, breathwork, sleep
- Audit your team's information diet. Are they consuming engineered urgency content or genuine signal?
- Try the **VUCA inversion exercise.** For each volatile area in your work, map: vision, understanding, clarity, agility
- **Default to belief.** Pick three things to deliberately doubt this quarter. Don't doubt everything. Conserve cognitive energy
- When clients or executives bring panic, **acknowledge it. Don't reflect it back.** Stabilize the conversation by naming what no one knows for sure
- Frame strategy decisions in terms of clear direction without claiming certainty. *"Here is where we are heading. Here is what we will learn along the way"*
- For your next budget conversation, bring a **market potential analysis** (assumptions made explicit) instead of false projections
- Build the language of cognitive sovereignty into your org. *"Are we responding to a signal or to engineered noise?"*
- Pair this with Ilana's parts framework. **Internal protection (parts) + external protection (cognitive sovereignty) = complementary**
takeaways: FUD (fear, uncertainty, doubt) is not a feeling — it's a deliberate decision-attack strategy running from Machiavelli to Big Tobacco, now at AI scale
Neuroscience: amygdala fires before prefrontal cortex; uncertainty is MORE stressful than confirmed bad news ('the surprise hurts more than the punch')
Johansen's VUCA inversion: Volatility→Vision, Uncertainty→Understanding, Complexity→Clarity, Ambiguity→Agility
The future will reward clarity but PUNISH certainty — categories are fake, clinging to them makes you easier to manipulate
Fear as signal (not strategy): the antidote to fear is competence; 'be more brave than scared'
Belief is the default cognitive state — doubt requires effort; pick what to doubt deliberately, default to belief on the rest
Cognitive sovereignty = remaining the genuine author of your thinking, free from AI-scale engineered noise
The new FUD: Fuel instead of Fear, Understanding instead of Uncertainty, Discernment instead of Doubt

## John Doherty — The Death of the Middleman: Why "Good Enough" AI is Killing Traditional Marketing

**Key thesis:** In 2011 it took John an hour and a favor from Mike King to build an SEO tool he needed. In 2025, he built **four lead-magnet calculators in an hour with Claude alone.** Production is solved. Content is no longer the bottleneck. The work that's left is **taste, the right questions at the right time, and real-world nuance**. The pyramid of producer / manager / strategist has collapsed — **everyone is a builder now**. Agencies and in-house teams who still sell *"we do the work so you don't have to"* are dead. The new value is business outcomes: leads, conversions, revenue. The new pricing model is **outcome-based**. The new framework is Dan Martell's **10/80/10**: humans at the start (direction, the right questions), AI in the middle (production), humans at the end (judgment, taste, review).

![SEO Week 2026 Psychology stage — Day 2 afternoon session on the post-AI shape of agency and in-house work](https://wsrv.nl/?url=https%3A%2F%2Fcustomer-assets.emergentagent.com%2Fjob_github-checker-8%2Fartifacts%2F79zxf0is_John%2520Doherty.jpg&w=1080&q=70&output=webp)

### TL;DR

Production capacity used to be the constraint. It isn't anymore. Julia runs a 7-figure Instagram business on Claude output; one of John's clients spun up a complete lead-gen + ad + landing-page stack in **4 hours** that used to take a team months. The old agency pitch — *"we do the work so you don't have to"* — is dead. The new value is business outcomes, and the new pricing is outcome-based (e.g. **$3K strategy + $250 per qualified lead** instead of a $5K flat retainer). Use Dan Martell's **10/80/10**: you own the first 10% (direction) and the last 10% (judgment); AI runs the middle 80%. The pyramid of producer / manager / strategist has collapsed — **we are all builders now**.

### The 12-year tool story

- **2011:** John at Distilled prepping his first SEO talk in NYC, needed a tool to scrape social profiles. Couldn't build it himself. **Mike King volunteered to build it in about an hour**
- **2025:** John built **4 lead-magnet calculators** for his own site in about an hour with Claude. No developer. No favor. No Mike King
- The 12-year arc: production capacity **used to be a constraint.** It isn't anymore
- What was the "real work" then? Building the thing. **What's the real work now?** Getting people to use it, building the distribution, doing the marketing

### The "How does AI affect that?" question (Costa Rica, January 2023)

- John sold his first agency in September 2022. **Three months later ChatGPT launched**
- At a Mutiny mastermind in Costa Rica with 100 entrepreneurs, every conversation about his new content-editing business hit the same question: *"How does AI affect that?"*
- Three years later, he wrote **15M+ words at EditorNinja**, sold it to a competitor in December 2025, and is now coaching agency founders
- The question hasn't gone away. Every agency owner, every in-house team, every marketing role is being asked it constantly. He's now the one asking it back to his clients

### Production is solved. Strategy and distribution are not

- **Julia** (a creator John mentioned) uses Claude for all her Instagram content. **Millions of monthly views. Thousands of weekly leads. 7-figure annual revenue in 18 months**
- What Claude doesn't do for Julia: pick the right topics, find the hooks that actually spread, build the distribution, manage the audience
- *"AI can make the content but it can't make people care"*
- SEO audits used to take weeks. One of John's clients runs a boutique agency that uses Claude to generate audits as a lead magnet. Reviews for 5 minutes, sends them out, **books sales calls daily**
- One side effect: he had to **slow down delivery** because clients didn't trust audits returned that fast

### SEO is becoming change management (the WordPress HTTP→HTTPS find)

- John rebuilt his personal site on WordPress with Claude. Custom plugins, theme, all of it. Easy to build
- Claude caught that his XML sitemap, hreflang, and other URLs were emitting **HTTP not HTTPS**. He'd been on HTTPS for 12 years and **never caught it himself**
- The actual SEO work was never auditing or sitemap inspection. That's all production. **The real work is change management:** getting the fix prioritized, deployed, and verified
- SEO has always been change management. **It's now MORE so**, because the production half is gone

### Three things AI doesn't have (and humans do)

- **Taste.** AI follows the brief. It hits the keywords. It matches intent. But it doesn't quite sound like the brand. You can feel it. AI can't. We can improve briefs, AI can improve, but **the final review is irreducibly human**
- **Asking the right questions at the right time.** AI is the best junior analyst you've ever had. It says *"do you want me to do this next?"* A senior strategist asks *"why are we looking at this in the first place?"* **That reframe is human**
- **Real-world nuance.** AI has processed every case study ever published. **You've LIVED through dozens of them.** You know which ones to bring into a sales call, which stories actually land

### Francis Schaeffer detour (the philosophical anchor)

- **L'Abri** community in Switzerland, started 1955, where John spent two years in his 20s
- Schaeffer's framing: being human means inherent dignity, rationality, and capacity for moral choices. **We are not machines. We are not just pattern recognition**
- You don't need to share the worldview to feel the weight of the framing. AI is sophisticated, fast pattern recognition. AGI may be coming. **It is not here yet**
- Until it is, the human edge is in the categories pattern recognition cannot reach

### The pyramid has collapsed

- **Old structure:** producers at the base (worker bees), managers in the middle, strategists at the top. Agencies sold hours. In-house teams hired headcount
- AI **obliterated the producer layer.** Every line between producer, manager, and strategist has blurred
- Real-world example John heard from a hedge-fund partner on the plane: a portfolio company had 2 PMs and 100 engineers. **They just fired 80 engineers and are hiring 16 more PMs**
- *"We are all builders now."* The old world needed different people for each layer. **The new world needs fewer people who can move fluidly between all of them**

### The hiring question

- Person with **1 year of experience who knows AI well**, or person with **15 years experience who doesn't know AI at all**?
- Unfair question. The answer is option C: **15 years of experience PLUS strong AI skills**
- The new senior is the experienced operator who has internalized AI. **Nothing else competes**

### The death of the middleman (the value-proposition shift)

- One of John's coaching clients runs a **$100K/month, 5-person agency**. Built his entire lead-gen and sales pipeline himself: lead magnet, Facebook ad copy, ad campaign, budget logic, landing pages, follow-ups, lead scoring
- Used to take a team months plus ongoing software costs. He did it in **4 hours with AI.** *"Tuesday afternoon"*
- The traditional value prop (*"we do the work so you don't have to"*) is **dead.** That was never the real value anyway
- The new value prop: **business outcomes.** Leads, conversions, revenue, ROI
- **Y Combinator** (per a recent blog post): *"AI lets service firms deliver finished work at higher margins, turning agencies into software-like businesses."* YC is now actively funding agencies in their batches — would not have happened 5 years ago

### The pricing model shift (outcome-based)

- **Sir Martin Sorrell** (founder S4 Capital, former CEO WPP): *"We've been paid on time taken. We need to shift to output-based pricing"*
- John's recommendation: instead of charging **$5K flat** for lead generation or ad management, charge **$3K for strategy + implementation, and $250 per qualified lead**
- Aligns incentives. Once the client gets more than **8 qualified leads**, the agency starts making more than the old retainer would have produced
- Same logic applies to in-house teams. Aspirational version: base salary plus bonus tied to marketing-driven revenue. Most companies won't go there yet, but the conversation is worth having
- John has a free **pricing calculator** on his site for agencies modeling outcome-based pricing

### If a client doesn't know their numbers, you charge for discovery

- Outcome-based pricing requires knowing the unit economics. **What's a lead worth? What's a customer worth over 12 months?** What does a 10%, 20%, 50% increase mean for the business?
- If a client doesn't know, **sell a discovery project up front** to figure it out
- *"With production taken care of, you can solve all of their problems, not just the ones you wanted to solve"*

### The optimist's bet — the pie gets bigger

- Companies that couldn't justify a $10K/month retainer for "good enough" work can now afford a **$3K/month engagement that produces real outcomes**
- More small agencies, more diverse industries served, more total work done across the market
- **Headcount will compress, but team count will expand.** Smaller teams getting better results
- John's caveat: the recent layoff wave (Block, Square, etc.) is partly correcting pandemic over-hiring, not pure AI substitution. **Many companies cutting headcount in the name of AI will regret it later**
- The better question: **how do we use the people we already have to deliver dramatically better results?**

### Dan Martell's 10/80/10 framework

- Source: **Dan Martell**, *Buy Back Your Time*
- **First 10% (humans):** set the direction, ask the right questions, apply the taste
- **Middle 80% (AI or other):** the building, drafting, execution, production
- **Final 10% (humans):** judgment, review, final taste check
- Sir Martin Sorrell's version of the same idea: **stay involved at two points only — ideation and the final check**
- Use the framework to figure out which work to delegate to AI and which to keep on your plate

### In-house — same dynamics, fewer dollars

- John ran growth for **Zillow.** His later in-house team was 7 marketers, 4 developers, half a designer. $100K+/month in costs
- That team today, with AI, could deliver the same output with half the headcount, **OR 3–5× the output with the same headcount**
- The opportunity for in-house leaders: **don't reduce headcount, multiply output.** Test more, ship more, deliver more
- Cross-functional change management, getting work prioritized, building consensus across teams — **this is where humans shine.** AI cannot run your cross-functional meeting for you

### Quotes worth keeping

> "AI can make the content but it can't make people care."

> "Production is solved. The real work is strategy and distribution."

> "AI is the best junior analyst you've ever had. It is not the senior strategist."

> "We are all builders now."

> "The old value prop was 'we do the work so you don't have to.' That's dead."

> "You can no longer say we don't know the ROI of our work."

> "More small teams, doing better work, for more clients." *(the optimist's bet)*

> "How do I use the people I have to get better results, not how do I cut headcount."

> "The first 10% is direction. The middle 80% is production. The last 10% is judgment."

### Open questions

- For agencies in regulated industries (legal, healthcare, finance), how does outcome-based pricing actually work when liability is asymmetric?
- What's the right way to measure outcome attribution when AI Overviews and AI search obscure click data?
- If everyone is a builder, what does the new entry-level job look like? What's the path for someone in their first marketing role?
- How do you protect the human-judgment layer from being eroded by automation creep over time?
- For in-house teams who CAN'T move to outcome-based comp, how do you reframe the value conversation upward to the C-suite?
- If headcount cuts justified by AI are mostly mistakes, when does the correction wave come and what does it look like?

### Action items

- Identify which 30% of your weekly work is pure production. **That's your first AI delegation list**
- For each delegation candidate, apply the **10/80/10** framework. What's your first 10% (direction)? What's your last 10% (judgment)?
- Audit your current pricing model. Is it time-based, deliverable-based, or outcome-based? **Plan a path to outcome-based**
- For your top 3 clients (or your in-house leadership), identify the unit economics: **lead value, customer value over 12 months, conversion-lift impact in dollars**
- If a client doesn't know their numbers, sell a **discovery project.** Do not skip this step
- Build at least **one new lead magnet, calculator, or tool with AI in under 4 hours.** Use it to test the production-is-solved thesis personally
- Audit your team structure. Where do you still have producer / manager / strategist silos? **Plan the merge**
- For in-house leaders: instead of reducing headcount, define what **3–5× output** looks like with the team you have
- Read *Buy Back Your Time* by Dan Martell for the full 10/80/10 framework
- Try John's **outcome-based pricing calculator** on his site before your next pricing review
- Build a "real work" list — the work that still requires taste, the right questions, and real-world nuance. **Protect that work and resource it**
- **Resist the temptation to pitch "we use AI"** as the value prop. Pitch business outcomes
takeaways: Production is solved — John built 4 lead-magnet calculators in an hour with Claude alone; what used to need Mike King in 2011 now needs zero devs
Three things AI doesn't have: taste, asking the right questions at the right time, and real-world nuance from stories you've actually lived through
The producer/manager/strategist pyramid has collapsed — everyone is a builder now; a portfolio company fired 80 engineers and is hiring 16 more PMs
Dan Martell's 10/80/10 framework: humans set direction (first 10%), AI does production (middle 80%), humans apply judgment and taste (final 10%)
The traditional 'we do the work so you don't have to' agency pitch is dead — the new value prop is business outcomes: leads, conversions, revenue
Outcome-based pricing model: replace a $5K flat retainer with $3K strategy + $250 per qualified lead — aligns incentives and uncaps upside past 8 leads
If a client doesn't know their unit economics (lead value, 12-month customer value), sell a discovery project before quoting outcome-based work
In-house play: don't reduce headcount — multiply output 3-5× with the same team; cross-functional change management is where humans still win

## Garrett Sussman — Run Persona Run: Personalization Is the New Frontier (Google Personal Intelligence + the Search Twin Playbook)

**Key thesis:** Personalization is the missing variable nobody addressed yesterday. **Google Personal Intelligence** connects your Gmail, Calendar, Photos, and Search history into AI Mode results — meaning every user sees a *different* SERP based on context Google already has on them. Garrett ran two experiments: 12 months of persona-tagged prompts (180K queries, 1M citations) and a controlled three-account study where he seeded one Gmail with emails, photos, and brand mentions. **The seeded account showed an 80% share of voice for personally referenced brands.** Direct mail showed up. Unopened newsletters showed up. Spam emails showed up. Google AI Mode hit ~25% adoption in the past month. **Build "search twins" with synthetic Gmail accounts to see what your real customers see.**

![Garrett Sussman on stage at SEO Week 2026 in his teal hoodie + sneakers, opening Day 2's personalization deep-dive](https://wsrv.nl/?url=https%3A%2F%2Fcustomer-assets.emergentagent.com%2Fjob_github-checker-8%2Fartifacts%2F4so538dt_IMG_2636.jpg&w=1080&q=70&output=webp)

### TL;DR

Personalization is the missing variable nobody addressed yesterday. Google Personal Intelligence connects your Gmail, Calendar, Photos, and Search history into AI Mode results, meaning every user sees a different SERP based on context Google already has on them. Garrett ran two experiments: 12 months of persona-tagged prompts (180K queries, 1M citations) and a controlled three-account study where he seeded one Gmail with emails, photos, and brand mentions. The seeded account showed an **80% share of voice** for personally referenced brands. Direct mail showed up. Unopened newsletters showed up. Spam emails showed up. Google AI Mode hit ~25% adoption in the past month. Build "search twins" with synthetic Gmail accounts to see what your real customers see.

### The setup — AI Mode adoption is real and accelerating

- Per **Similarweb data**: AI Mode adoption jumped from **~5% (last year, this time) to 20–25% over the past month**
- Search perception of AI is climbing. The 90% spike last March was a tracking artifact (bots), but the real curve is solidly upward
- **Sundar Pichai and Liz Reid** have telegraphed the roadmap. AI Mode is where everything is consolidating. Expect more announcements at Google I/O in May
- The watershed moment Garrett is calling: **Apple Personal Intelligence** connecting Siri to your data ecosystem. Apple has fumbled the bag twice already, but third time will likely succeed. When it does, every Apple user gets first-hand AI personalization

### Google Personal Intelligence — what it actually is

![Slide — "PERSONAL INTELLIGENCE IS COMING. GOOGLE WANTS YOUR DATA." with @rmstein's tweet thread embedded: "Today, we're opening up access to Personal Intelligence for AI Mode in Search in the U.S. 🚀 This feature has totally changed how I use AI in Search. Here's how it works: 1) Opt in to connect apps like Gmail and Google Photos. Search connects your info to give you responses that uniquely match your specific context and interests. 2) Start asking for things like ideas and recommendations, where this is particularly helpful. For example: I wanted new podcast ideas and Personal Intelligence in AI Mode gave me spot-on recs for AI and product building shows that are similar to some of my favorites (hey @lennysan!). It even found some unexpected options around dad life working in tech."](https://wsrv.nl/?url=https%3A%2F%2Fcustomer-assets.emergentagent.com%2Fjob_github-checker-8%2Fartifacts%2Frwyzcz3q_IMG_2638.jpg&w=1080&q=70&output=webp)

- **You explicitly opt in.** Google then reaches into Gmail, Calendar, Photos, and Search history to personalize AI Mode results
- Currently **free** (no Ultra subscription required as of recording)
- Right now limited to Google ecosystem apps. Future: socials, banking, anywhere you grant permission
- **Google published a public PDF** documenting how Personal Intelligence works AND its known limitations. Worth reading directly
- Liz Reid has explicitly said Google wants *"deliberate consent."* Garrett's take: it's only a matter of time before opt-in language gets buried in T&Cs in fine print

#### Even without Personal Intelligence enabled — Google has your data

![Slide — "EVEN WITHOUT PERSONAL INTELLIGENCE, GOOGLE HAS YOUR DATA. — Mordy Oberstein, Head of Brand, SE Ranking. THANKS, MORDY." Right side: AI Mode response showing Yankees / Cubs / Mariners / Reds franchise rankings with the live processing animation reading "Checking for relevant personalized info" — even on an account NOT opted in. Source: seroundtable.com/ai-mode-results-personalized-to-user-behavior-41065.html](https://wsrv.nl/?url=https%3A%2F%2Fcustomer-assets.emergentagent.com%2Fjob_github-checker-8%2Fartifacts%2F6gos504w_IMG_2639.jpg&w=1080&q=70&output=webp)

- **Even without Personal Intelligence enabled, Google is already personalizing.** Marty Weintraub (referenced via Mordy Oberstein) showed an AI Mode response that displayed *"checking for relevant personalized info"* in the live processing animation — on an account NOT opted in to Personal Intelligence
- Conclusion: opt-in or not, the personalization is happening. Opt-in just *increases* the surface area and *makes it more visible*

### The mental model shift — query → context → person

- **Old model:** query goes in, results come out
- **New model:** every query is interpreted through what the system already knows or infers about the person asking
- **Two flavors of context:**
  - **Explicit context** — what the user types into the prompt (budget, kids, dates, location)
  - **Implicit context** — what the system pulls from Gmail, Calendar, Photos, search history
- **Query fan-out itself is now personalized.** Example: *"which streaming services are worth paying for"* expanded to include *"best streaming services for kids"* because the system knew Garrett has a daughter
- **You cannot just map content to a generic fan-out anymore. The branches diverge per persona.**

### Experiment 1 — persona-tagged prompts at scale

- **Setup:** appended explicit persona context (e.g., *"I am a female business owner, 58, salary X"*) to generic prompts about coffee machines, running shoes, etc.
- **Scale:** 12 months of data, **180K+ prompts**, 4 product categories, 8 AI search platforms, **1M+ citations**

#### "AI doesn't recommend the same bank to everyone"
