## Zach Chahalis — Why You Need a Relevance Engineer Driving the Car

**Key thesis:** Rankings and traffic alone cannot diagnose what is wrong with your content for AI retrieval. iPullRank built **8 NLP-based diagnostic metrics** — semantic coherence, comprehensive coverage, entity density, explanatory efficiency, verifiable claims, optimal chunkability, conceptual depth, information gain — and ran them against three AI-content-heavy sites. The productivity SaaS site that fell from **8,000 AI Overview inclusions to 1,700** had **83% of its content unrelated to its core offering**. The metrics are diagnostic levers, not content scores, and the right lever depends on industry and content type. Like a 1980s Mercedes 500 with a soul, AI search needs a relevance engineer behind the wheel — you cannot set it and forget it.

![Zach Chahalis on the SEO Week 2026 Ecosystem stage — title slide "Why You Need A Relevance Engineer Driving The Car" with iPullRank · AirOps branding](https://wsrv.nl/?url=https%3A%2F%2Fcustomer-assets.emergentagent.com%2Fjob_github-checker-8%2Fartifacts%2F71nc92vg_IMG_2728.jpg&w=1080&q=70&output=webp)

### TL;DR

If you only measure rankings or traffic, you cannot diagnose what is actually wrong with your content for AI retrieval. iPullRank's 8 diagnostic metrics surfaced exactly why one site collapsed from 8,000 AI Overview inclusions to 1,700: 83% off-topic content, 2,200-word average length saying half as much, templated junk that *looked* chunkable, almost zero verifiable claims, and visible ChatGPT apology artifacts left in published copy. The metrics are not one-size-fits-all — what matters most depends on whether you publish how-tos, explainers, or transactional content. AI search is changing every few weeks; without a relevance engineer running diagnostics, you cannot keep up.

### The car metaphor

- Zach is a 20-year car enthusiast who got bored with modern cars (no soul, all look the same) and bought a **1980s Mercedes 500** instead
- The same boredom hit him in SEO around **2022** — he almost left the field
- The shift to AI search was the soul coming back: new tooling, new diagnostic challenges, new things to reverse engineer
- Older cars require a driver who can work on them, understand the mechanics, intervene when things go wrong
- **AI search requires the same.** You cannot rely on autopilot. You need someone who can read the diagnostics and turn the wrench

### How measurement has to evolve

- Performance metrics still matter, but **traffic alone is not enough**. Track events, conversions, engagement depth, revenue per session
- Add **input metrics** that show whether your content and site align with how bots interpret you
- Measure how visible and well-represented you are inside the **brand entity space**
- **Drop pure rank tracking.** Replace with share of voice, citation rate, citation quality, citation sentiment
- AI Overviews are demonstrably changing user behavior — even **Wikipedia traffic dropped after AIO launch** (clear inflection point on the chart)
- Organic search still matters as a discovery channel and as a retrieval source for RAG models. **Rankings remain table stakes for AI Search appearance, not the finish line**

### Why a custom strategy beats a generic playbook

- Personalization (per Garrett's earlier session) and persona variance (per Wil's) mean the same playbook will not work across sites
- You need: industry context, ecosystem and channel reality for your audience, custom data and measurement layer, constant experimentation
- The biggest reality of the AI search era: **everything changes every few weeks** — new models, new behaviors, new ranking signals
- What works today may not work in 3 weeks. **If you are not testing, you fall behind**

![Zach mid-talk on the SEO Week stage — gray quarter-zip and tan chinos, walking the audience through the relevance-engineering case studies](https://wsrv.nl/?url=https%3A%2F%2Fcustomer-assets.emergentagent.com%2Fjob_github-checker-8%2Fartifacts%2F0fe5b375_IMG_2732.jpg&w=1080&q=70&output=webp)

### The 8 relevance engineering metrics (defined by iPullRank)

- **Keyword cosine similarity** — topical coherence and focus. Does your content match the semantic neighborhood of the rest of your site? Penalizes semantic drift
- **Comprehensive coverage index** — balance of length with informational value and completeness. A composite of multiple quality signals
- **Strategic entity richness score** — weights entity counts by relevance. Penalizes irrelevant entity stuffing
- **Explanatory efficiency index** — fact density per word. Penalizes narrative bloat. Are you explaining or just filling space?
- **Verifiable claims** — are the claims in your content substantiated against other trusted sources on the internet?
- **Optimal chunkability** — how well the document's structure aligns with its underlying semantic structure. Can it be cleanly broken into retrievable units?
- **Conceptual depth score** — specificity and hierarchical depth of concepts. Rewards detailed expert-level information
- **Information gain** — are you adding unique insight, or republishing what everyone else has? Penalizes redundancy
- **Entity density** — ratio of entities to content length. Ensures information density without crowding

> Critically, these are **diagnostic levers, not content scores**. Don't optimize *to* the metrics. Use them to find what is broken.

### The experiment — three AI-slop sites diagnosed

- **Site 1 — Productivity SaaS:** major project management company. Page-1 rankings dropped **~90% from their early-2025 peak**
- **Site 2 — Financial info:** personal finance content (mortgages, credit cards, calculators). Page-1 rankings relatively flat
- **Site 3 — Tech how-to:** step-by-step instructional guides (Android updates, device settings). Page-1 rankings increased through last year, started trending down post-recent core updates

**AI visibility results:**

- **Productivity SaaS:** collapsed from **8,000 AI Overview inclusions to ~1,700** in the last year
- **Financial site:** relatively flat citations across all AI platforms
- **Tech how-to site:** slight downward trend, mostly flat

The productivity SaaS site was the obvious failure. The metrics revealed why.

### Productivity SaaS — what the metrics revealed

- **83% of content was off-topic.** Sample articles included *"How to make a strikethrough in Google Docs," "Tea alternatives," "Office party ideas," "Tuesday motivational quotes for work."* Almost none of it tied to task management
- **2,200 average word count** vs. 1,200 (finance) and 1,100 (tech how-to). They use the most words and say the least
- **Half the explanatory efficiency.** Finance site scored 3.5 explanations per 100 words. Productivity SaaS came in at less than half that
- **62% optimal chunkability — but for the wrong reason.** Looks high until you realize every page uses the same template, same headings, same format. Templated junk at scale, not genuinely chunkable knowledge
- **Verifiable claims completely absent.** Finance site had **218% more** verifiable claims. Tech how-to site had **575% more**
- Productivity SaaS literally left **ChatGPT response artifacts** in published copy (*"I'm sorry I got that wrong, let me try again"*)

### Why the metrics are NOT one-size-fits-all

- The tech how-to site looked weak on explanatory efficiency. **That is normal for the format.** Step-by-step instructions are not supposed to be word-dense explanations
- The tech how-to site excelled at **entity density** (device names, OS versions, settings, menu items). For their format, that is the right signal
- The finance site was the most explanatorily efficient (**3,379 explanations per measurement window**). For their format, that is the right signal
- Each industry and content type has different metrics that matter most. **You need a relevance engineer who knows which lever to pull**
- This is why generic SEO checklists fail — they cannot tell a how-to template from an explainer template from a transactional template

### Org and team structure has to evolve too

- **Direct plea to heads of marketing: do not shrink your SEO team right now.** The opposite is needed
- What needs to change is *how* your team works with the rest of the org — cross-functional integration with PR, organic, paid, content, product, brand
- *"Engineering relevance"* is now a multi-team sport. **No single function can deliver AI visibility alone**
- This is the same conclusion Brie Anderson hit earlier in Day 3: you only own 2 of 7 AEO levers — the work is influence across the other 5

### Case study 1 — global financial services leader (121% qualified leads)

- Used the relevance engineering metrics to identify which levers to pull. The diagnosis showed **semantic coherence** as the gap
- Focus: semantic optimization of content (aligning page-level meaning to topical neighborhood)
- **Result: 121% increase in qualified leads**
- The metric they cared about was *leads*, not traffic. Traffic was incidental — get the right people on the site, not more people

### Case study 2 — the 499 status code correlation

- Direct callback to **Mike King's morning session** on the 499 status code
- Found a direct correlation between **499 spikes and AI citation drops** on a client site
- What 499 means: client gave up waiting because the page was too slow. **AI bots especially won't wait around**
- Fix the 499s, citations recover. Demonstrated in production
- Reinforces a Day 1 theme: technical infrastructure is the **eligibility gate**. If bots can't reach your content fast enough, no diagnostic metric on content quality matters

### Practical takeaways

- **Off-brand content actively hurts AI visibility.** The productivity SaaS site is the case study
- Long word counts do not equal authority. They can equal **bloat**
- **Verifiable claims are now a major signal.** If your content cannot be fact-checked against trusted sources, AI systems discount it
- Templated content at scale **looks like AI slop to retrieval systems**, even if a human wrote some of it
- Visible AI artifacts (ChatGPT apology text left in published copy) are a clear signal of an unsupervised AI workflow. **Audit your published content for this**
- Your strategy is only as good as the relevance engineer driving it. Unlike Tesla autopilot, **you cannot set and forget**

### Closing arguments — the buyer-beware checklist

- **Buyer beware.** Define your risk tolerance. Understand your testing scope. Know that outcomes are not guaranteed
- **Industry context matters.** The same approach won't work for a tech how-to site and a financial services site
- **Measure before you modify.** Establish a clean baseline before changing anything. Without that, you can't tell if your changes worked
- **Rely on real analytics data.** Don't guess. Watch the data. Validate every change against the baseline
- **Define your target metric explicitly.** What are you optimizing against? Pick **one diagnostic lever per intervention**, not all 8 at once
- **Watch for second-order effects.** Optimizing one metric can degrade another. Monitor the full cascade, not just citation count
- **Monitor beyond citations.** Conversions, engagement, sentiment, downstream pipeline impact

### Quotes worth keeping

> "The idea of just looking at rankings is dead."

> "Your strategy is only as good as the relevance engineer driving the car."

> "Unlike Tesla autopilot, you cannot turn it on and forget it."

> "Diagnostic levers, not content scores. Don't optimize to the metrics — use them to find what's broken."

> "83% of the content on a productivity SaaS site had nothing to do with their core offering."

> "Everything is constantly changing. What works today may not work in three weeks."

> "Measure before you modify."

> "If you are a head of marketing thinking about shrinking your SEO team — do not."

### Open questions

- How do you operationalize 8 diagnostic metrics across thousands of pages without manual review?
- What is the right cadence to re-run these diagnostics? Per publish? Monthly? Quarterly?
- Are there open-source equivalents to the iPullRank metric definitions, or is this only available through their tooling?
- How does the chunkability metric handle dynamic content that changes often (news, e-commerce inventory, real-time data)?
- For sites with multiple content types (how-to, explanatory, transactional), how do you weight the metrics differently per template?
- How quickly do AI systems detect and demote AI-artifact leakage (visible ChatGPT responses) in production content?
- What second-order effects are most common when optimizing for one metric at a time? Where do trade-offs typically appear?

### Action items

- Watch the iPullRank webinar on relevance engineering metrics for the full methodology
- Audit your top 100 pages for off-topic content — what percentage is core to your offering?
- Audit for visible AI artifacts (apologies, refusals, system prompts left in copy). Strip and republish
- Calculate **explanatory efficiency** on your top pages: how many verifiable explanations per 100 words?
- Audit verifiable claims — for each major claim on a top page, can it be substantiated against an external trusted source?
- Audit chunkability the right way: is the high score because the content is genuinely well-organized, or because every page uses the same template?
- Define which of the 8 metrics matter **most** for each of your content templates (how-to, explainer, transactional, listicle, etc.)
- Set up a **quarterly diagnostic review** using these metrics as inputs to content pruning decisions
- Identify content that fails 3 or more diagnostic levers — decide: rewrite, redirect, or remove
- For new content, use the metrics as a **pre-publish QA checklist, not a writing guide**
- **Pull log files for 499 status code spikes.** Cross-reference against AI citation drops in the same window
- Establish a baseline before any optimization. Pick **ONE metric** to optimize per intervention, not all 8 simultaneously
- Build a **second-order effects monitor**: when one metric improves, which others move? Track the full cascade
- For agency or in-house leaders: pitch **increasing** the SEO/relevance team, not shrinking it. Use the case studies (121% qualified leads, 499 fix recovering citations) as the budget justification
takeaways: iPullRank's 8 diagnostic metrics (semantic coherence, coverage, entity density, explanatory efficiency, verifiable claims, chunkability, conceptual depth, information gain) are diagnostic LEVERS, not content scores
Productivity SaaS site collapsed from 8,000 → 1,700 AI Overview inclusions because 83% of its content was off-topic to its core offering
Verifiable claims is now a major signal — finance site had 218% more, tech how-to 575% more than the failing SaaS site
Templated content at scale reads as AI slop to retrieval systems even when a human wrote it; visible ChatGPT artifacts in published copy = automatic demotion
Metrics are NOT one-size-fits-all — entity density matters most for how-tos, explanatory efficiency for explainers; pick the right lever per template
Case study: 121% increase in qualified leads from semantic-coherence optimization on a global financial services client
Case study: 499 status-code spikes correlate directly with AI citation drops — fix the timeouts, citations recover
Measure before you modify, optimize one metric per intervention, monitor second-order effects, and do NOT shrink your SEO team

## Ross Simmonds — Inception: Plant Your Brand Into the Memory Layer of Every LLM

**Key thesis:** Memory is going to be the most important concept in marketing for the next 48 months. AI tools are building persistent memory of every user interaction, and the brands that **influence what gets remembered** (through distribution, off-site presence, and category creation) will own the future. Stop arguing about SEO vs. GEO vs. AEO. Focus on two things in your circle of control: **how you create value on the internet, and how you influence the memory of the tools your buyers use**. The 10 blue links are dead. Google is now a destination. Win with E-E-A-T fundamentals, distribute everywhere, and **create things once to distribute forever.**

### TL;DR

Memory is going to be the most important concept in marketing for the next 48 months. AI tools are building persistent memory of every user interaction, and the brands that influence what gets remembered (through distribution, off-site presence, and category creation) will own the future. Stop arguing about SEO vs GEO vs AEO. Focus on two things in your circle of control: how you create value on the internet, and how you influence the memory of the tools your buyers use. The 10 blue links are dead. Google is now a destination. Win with E-E-A-T fundamentals, distribute everywhere, and create things once to distribute forever.

### The "Winky Wink" story — memory as the central frame

- **Personal story:** accidentally turned his face into an emoji on a video call with his daughter. She loved it. **A year and a half later, she still calls him "Winky Wink"**
- One small moment created a permanent memory that defines a relationship
- The same mechanism is now happening at scale **inside AI tools**. Every user interaction trains the persistent memory of their AI tools
- These tools are learning what users like, dislike, who they trust, what brands they prefer, what context to bring forward
- Memory is going to be the most under-discussed lever in marketing for the next 4 years. Almost no one is preparing for it

### The "bread and circus" warning

- Roman Empire framing: *free bread and circus acts kept the public distracted while the empire crumbled around them*
- The SEO industry is doing the same thing — arguing about acronyms (SEO, GEO, AEO, HEO) while the underlying shift goes unaddressed
- Stop the acronym debate. Focus on the things in your **circle of control**: value creation and memory influence
- The 10 blue links are not coming back. **Google has become a destination.** Said since 2018, now reality

#### Google is still the front page of the web

![Q4 2025 Share of Search Across 41 Major Sites (USA), Datos × SparkToro — Google 73.7%, Amazon 7.83%, Bing 4.31%, YouTube 3.65%, ChatGPT 2.86%, All Other Sites 7.65%. The slide caption: "REMEMBER: Google is still the front page of the web."](https://wsrv.nl/?url=https%3A%2F%2Fcustomer-assets.emergentagent.com%2Fjob_github-checker-8%2Fartifacts%2Fggktw238_IMG_2679%25202.jpg&w=1080&q=70&output=webp)

- **Google still owns 73.7%** of search across 41 major sites in Q4 2025
- ChatGPT is at **2.86%** — meaningful, but not the substitute the industry is treating it as
- The mistake is treating ChatGPT/Perplexity/Gemini as a replacement layer when they're actually a *new layer on top* — they read what Google has already organized
- *"Don't sell this as snake oil — Google is still the front page of the web. The work hasn't changed; it's been added to."*

### Layer 1 — experience and E-E-A-T fundamentals

- Google is still where the vast majority of search happens. **E-E-A-T (Experience, Expertise, Authoritativeness, Trustworthiness) is non-negotiable**
- Listicles still work, just not trash listicles. Humans operate in lists (grocery, doctors). LLMs return lists. Make your lists better with proprietary data, video, UGC
- Commodity content still has a role in immature markets where it doesn't yet exist. In mature markets, it's a losing bet because LLMs can produce it instantly
- Non-commodity content is where AI visibility actually thrives because **LLMs are looking for evidence (data, stats, stories) to back up answers**
- Think like investors, not artists. Drive business results. Match content investments to your audience, budget, and resources
- **Tactical move:** upload high-value queries from your niche into AI visibility tools. Study which URLs are being cited. Most are commodity content. Build a calendar to make 10× better versions

### Editorial review board pattern (the NerdWallet model)

- NerdWallet has an editorial review board. **Every published piece shows both author and editor names**
- Adds expertise and credibility signals AI can verify
- Operationalize: put SMEs on retainer, set up a private Slack, share each piece for green-check approval
- Approved pieces get the SME's name on the byline. Builds verifiable expertise signals at scale

### Backlinks still matter — and statistics-as-an-asset wins

- *"Citations replace links"* is wrong. **Google owns Gemini.** Google's been training models on link signals for years. Links remain the strongest authority proxy
- Foundation analyzed which content assets are most likely to earn links. Result: **statistics roundups dominate at 4.25× — almost 3× the next-best format**
- *"50 stats on AI"* or *"40 stats on electrolytes"* perform as backlink gold

- **Templates dead-last at 0.68×.** Counter-intuitive — but most templates are commoditized. AI generates them in seconds

### Layer 2 — distribution rules everything around me

- Per Ahrefs research: **85% of brand mentions in AI search come from third-party content**

- If you're not thinking about how to show up on *other people's sites*, you're missing the biggest visibility lever in AI search
- **Review sites:** traffic is collapsing, but their citation share in LLMs has never been higher. Their influence on buyers is now happening **inside the LLM**, not on their site

### Reddit is structurally undervalued

- Reddit gets cited heavily in LLMs **even when buyers don't have accounts**. CFOs, CIOs, CTOs are influenced by Reddit through AI answers
- **Foundation B2B analysis:** **94% of "best [software]" queries had a Reddit thread** as the most influential link in the top results
- The longer the search query, the more likely Reddit shows up. LLMs love Reddit because users have asked very specific, niche questions there for 15+ years
- **Per industry:** SaaS, CRM, email marketing, digital marketing each have one or two dominant subreddits. **Identify yours**
- **The reputation defense playbook:** if Reddit is showing negative content about your brand at the top of branded search, **create your own subreddit (r/yourbrand)**. Run a content calendar inside it. Drive your email list to the subreddit. Build the community. Outrank the negative thread on recency
- **Hypothesis (directional, not proven):** the Reddit-to-LLM pipeline is real. Brands that participate authentically on Reddit get into LLM training data faster than those that don't
- **Hypothesis (directional, not proven):** Reddit ads do two jobs. Reach today + influence training data tomorrow. The ads themselves aren't indexable, but they drive conversation volume in the subreddit, and that UGC is what gets trained on

- YouTube videos are showing up in AI Overviews at growing rates
- Foundation correlation analysis: YouTube videos vs. CPC of queries. **YouTube is dramatically undervalued for high-CPC queries**
- For SaaS: YouTube is winning over brand sites for *"best [tool]"* and *"[tool] alternative"* queries
- **The playbook:** research key topics for your ICP, create non-commodity how-to content, target high-CPC queries, modify into YouTube Shorts, run paid amplification, partner with creators, embed videos back on your site
- Embedding YouTube on your own site is preferable to self-hosted video because Google has an ad-revenue interest in promoting watched YouTube content (directional theory)
- **Recent data: YouTube.com citations jumped 84% in AI Mode**

### Other platform-citation data points

- **Perplexity is 162× more likely to cite LinkedIn than Gemini is.** Likely because LinkedIn is owned by Microsoft, Gemini is Google
- If your audience is in finance, Perplexity bias toward LinkedIn matters disproportionately
- **Medium.com** citations have grown over the last 6 months
- **Quora** citations have consistently declined
- **Reddit** citations dropped on Perplexity but are flat or growing on most other platforms

- **vidIQ** for thumbnail optimization. Auto-pulls images from your videos and scores thumbnails against best-in-class training data
- **Sea Dance + HeyGen + ElevenLabs** for AI-generated short-form video. Upload past podcasts, generate shorts at scale. Ross showed an AI version of himself saying things he never recorded — *indistinguishable on camera*
- **VideoDatabase** pulls top-performing TikTok and Instagram videos. Identifies viral hooks for content inspiration

- **"Analyze the day on" button** Foundation is testing on their blog. One click sends the article into ChatGPT, Claude, Grok, or Perplexity for the user. Gets users to incorporate Foundation content into their LLM context (and memory) directly

### Layer 3 — create once, distribute forever (category creation)

- The deepest layer of inception: **create the category, own the language, and let the audience use your terms forever**
- Competing for *"best CRM"* is a bloodbath. Competing for a niche, hyper-personalized variant your brand owns the language for is a win
- **Real B2B example:** a buyer prompts the LLM with detailed context (company size, hiring 5 SDRs this month, replacing existing stack, has uploaded confidential docs). The LLM runs query fan-out incorporating ALL of that context
- If you've created language that maps to those specific contexts and that language exists across many third-party properties, **you win the personalized fan-out**
- *"Revenue intelligence platform"* as an example: if your brand is the only one talking about that exact category framing, you become the default answer
- **Memory + category creation = inception.** The user's LLM remembers them, runs personalized queries, and your category language is what gets retrieved

## Mike King — Accounting for Gaps in SEO Software

> Most SEO tools are stuck in 2018. They report keyword density, TF-IDF, and "compare to top 20 pages" — but that's a worldview Google hasn't operated under for years.

The talk had **four big moves** I want to remember.

### 1. Embeddings have site-level and author-level dimensions

Google's retrieval models score relevance not just for the query-document match but for the broader context: how the site as a whole maps to a topic neighborhood, and whether the *author* has a track record in that domain.

![Mike King keynote](https://seoweek.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/01/Frame-1597879909-1.png)

### 2. Information Gain is the underrated 2024 concept

The question Google's models are answering is: **"How much does this page add to what's already in the SERP?"**

- Pages that say the same thing as the top 10 = wasted index space
- Pages that introduce a *genuinely new angle* get rewarded
- Internal data, original surveys, expert quotes = simplest path to Information Gain

### 3. Hybrid retrieval — keywords aren't a moat anymore

Mike showed examples of pages ranking for queries where the exact keyword phrase doesn't appear anywhere on the page. With dense retrieval running alongside lexical, semantic similarity carries pages over the line.

### 4. Click metrics are confirmed in the rank stack

The DOJ documents made it official: NavBoost is part of how Google ranks. Specifically, the `longest last click` is a strong satisfaction signal.

> Design for the last click. If you're page 3 in the SERP, your job isn't to outrank — it's to be the page someone clicks AFTER they bounced off page 1.

### Reference video

https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=dQw4w9WgXcQ

### Action items

1. **Audit our top 50 pages** for Information Gain
2. **Run our top 200 pages** through embedding similarity
3. **Switch title-tag tests** from rank position to last-click rate
4. **Volunteer** to contribute to the Search Telemetry Project
takeaways: Information Gain > content length
Click metrics confirmed in rank stack
Open-source SEO data initiative coming

## Andrea Volpini — Beyond the Million-Token Window: TurboQuant and RLM-on-KG

**The thesis.** Context windows grew 2,000,000× between 2017 and 2026 — from 512 tokens (the first WordLift model) to 1M+ on Gemini. The question is no longer capacity; it's *navigation*. When everything fits, the bottleneck moves from indexing to traversal. Andrea's talk laid out two pieces of WordLift research that change what "findable" means for AI: TurboQuant (a quantization scheme that doesn't silently degrade retrieval) and RLM-on-KG (an LLM that navigates a knowledge graph instead of brute-forcing the corpus).

**Act 1 — The context explosion.** KV cache grows O(N²). Vector search space explodes. Neural context loss creeps in. Architectural responses (bigger models, more throughput) buy time but don't solve the problem. The philosophical response — smarter memory, selective retrieval, navigable structured knowledge — is what compounds. Memory and structure are first-class citizens now.

**Act 2 — Structure makes AI smarter (Paper 1).** WordLift's three-tier experiment: plain HTML (baseline) → +JSON-LD (modest lift) → enhanced entity pages (+29.6% retrieval accuracy with Agentic RAG). Same content, different memory conditions. The variable is whether the system can *traverse* the structure. Structure matters when it changes retrieval behavior, not just when it validates markup.

**Act 3 — TurboQuant: the compression paradox.** Bigger context requires compression. But bad compression breaks retrieval silently — no crash, no warning, rankings just degrade. TurboQuant uses polar quantization (magnitude + direction on a sphere) instead of Cartesian. Result: 45× smaller, 8× faster, with provably unbiased inner-product estimates via QJL correction. First algorithm to be unbiased, codebook-free, GPU-native, AND data-oblivious simultaneously. The point isn't speed — it's that geometry is preserved, so similarity rankings stay reliable at billion scale.

**Act 4 — RLM-on-KG: navigation, not similarity.** Instead of treating the LLM as a speed-reader scanning sequentially, RLM-on-KG treats it as a librarian navigating the catalog. Head-to-head against Microsoft GraphRAG on the same benchmark: RLM 45.8 F1 vs GraphRAG 45.6. But on *complex reasoning with 11+ scattered evidence chunks*, RLM wins 71% of the time (+4.55pp F1). When evidence is concentrated, both work; when it's scattered, adaptive navigation wins. Separation of concerns: LLM explores, vectors rank.

**Act 5 — The SEO playbook.** Visibility is shifting from *mentions* (be cited) to *reasoning utility* (be reachable, verifiable, citable). 7% of AI citations are "ghost citations" — cited content that never appeared in the top-10. They were navigated through entity links, not ranking signals. The pipeline isn't crawl → index → rank anymore; it's **explore → verify → cite**. Consistency beats crawling: high-volume content with inconsistent entity naming gets a *lower* citation rate than moderate-volume content with consistent naming. Same entity, three weak signals instead of one strong one.

**The moat.** Context windows will keep growing. Models will keep getting cheaper. The variable that compounds is your data connectivity. The moat is not the model — it's the graph.
takeaways: Context windows grew 2,000,000× — the bottleneck is now traversal, not capacity

TurboQuant: polar quantization preserves geometry at 45× compression — first scheme that's unbiased AND codebook-free AND GPU-native
RLM-on-KG beats GraphRAG by +4.55pp F1 on complex reasoning with scattered evidence (71% win rate)
7% of AI citations are 'ghost citations' — pages never in the top-10, reached through entity links
Visibility shifted from mentions (be cited) to reasoning utility (be reachable, verifiable, citable)
Pipeline is now explore → verify → cite, not crawl → index → rank

## Mike King — F*CK It, I'll Do It Myself

**The provocation.** Since 2016, Mike has said "Her" was search's future — an invisible interface where chatbots and agents become abstractions on top of search. We're now there, and SEOs got lapped. The community has the skills but not the tools or the vision. Are you playing to win or playing to play?

**Re-examining the state of the art.** It's been nearly two years since the Google Content Warehouse API leak and the IR data exploit. *Nothing meaningful has changed about SEO software.* Modern search is driven by semantic understanding of users, websites, authors, and entities. We still don't have a vector index of these things. We've been operating in the dark for 14 years. The leak literally described site-focus and site-radius scores, sourcetype metrics (FRESHDOCS bucket), and an approximation of NavBoost — and no crawler has added any of it. Tools just slap ChatGPT and MCP servers onto the same lexical architecture. New entrants don't have these problems because they build based on the state of the art.

**Agentic RAG era.** We're past naive RAG. Now there are many agents across the pipeline — each one a visibility gatekeeper. Candidate chunks get pairwise analysis; you may lose simply because of how you worded something or because consensus disagrees with a fact you stated. You'll never see the reasoning chain. The move is *model distillation* — never know the internal decisions, but distill the model's behavior from its outputs and use that to inform relevance engineering. That's where modern SEO software needs to spend its time.

**Actionable detour: 499s.** The 499 status (client disconnected because the server took too long) is the AI search quick win nobody mentions. AI surfaces fetch pages in real-time; if you're slow, you're not considered. Most teams have never even tracked 499.

**Build what platforms won't.** Open source equivalents exist for every closed platform. Use n8n for microservice APIs. Human-in-the-loop via messaging integrations. Ollama for local open-source models. Three embeddings models worth trying: Microsoft's Harrier (top of leaderboard), Google's EmbeddingGemma (closest to Google's architecture), MixedBread (consistently solid across platforms). Google's LangExtract for chunking. Google AI Studio + Antigravity for full-app build-and-host from a single prompt. The Karpathy skill for vibe coding.

**Introducing Search Telemetry Project.** Open-source crawler that derives as many of the leaked Google metrics as possible — Gemma 4 + Similarweb + Semrush APIs to fill the blanks. "By no means do I believe this is accurate, but it is precise."

**Introducing Vectour.** Mike decompiled Majestic's MJ12Node distributed crawler and asked: what if we replicated that architecture for an *embeddings index*, using nodes for storage too? Vectour is a distributed peer-based web index of vector embeddings, crawling locally and embedding the web with Harrier + EmbeddingGemma + MixedBread Large. Anyone can run a node; you set your storage contribution and content-type limits. Open source.

**Introducing Vector Workstation.** Once you have embeddings, what do you do with them? 3D topical maps showing relevance relationships. Overlay keywords on top to see relevance against your content (outliers = low relevance). Compare any URL to any URL or keyword. Detect semantic drift with Gemma 4. Prune internal and external links that pollute your link graph. Also open source.

**The call.** SEO is in the agentic search era. Each agent is a gatekeeper. We can't keep adding ChatGPT to dashboards and calling it AI — we have to modernize the fundamental architecture. The question is who steps up.

## Noah Learner — Build the Tool Your Team Actually Needs: A Product Thinking Playbook for SEOs

**The opening scar.** Noah was six. He kicked through a glass door, missed the main artery by a millimeter, 45-minute drive to a Jerusalem hospital. 45 years later, the scar is still there. This talk is about scars — the ones that make you better operators.

**Why now.** Three quotes set the stage. Aimee Jurenka: "These LLMs will be our customers." Jordan Choo: "SEOs focus on thinking work (strategy), not execution." Bradley Porter: "I can build the thing I want without bugging the dev team. If you're an SEO product person, you have to live here." Your domain expertise + AI = the leverage to build useful solutions.

**The proof — 46 days.** Empty folder to production platform. 1,055 commits (vs ~150/month for an average 5-person engineering team — Noah shipped 670 in a month, solo). 9,356 tests. The Operator's Law: **Output = Code × Domain × Discipline**. Painkillers, not vitamins.

**The scars.** "I wrote a BigQuery query. Claude said it was fine. I hit enter." Big bill. Confidence is the bug — when Claude is most certain, be most skeptical. Bugs have ghosts: if it happened once, it'll happen again. Noah paid the bill and built a hook to prevent the same class of error.

**Context management is the leverage point.** Most best practices come from one constraint: Claude's context window fills up fast, and performance degrades as it fills. Stay in the first 20% of your context window. Use `/statusline`. Build a `/handoff` skill (or steal Noah's at github.com/serpfire/claude-harness-examples/blob/main/skills/handoff.md). Most advanced harnesses drown in their own rules; Claude says files over 200 lines reduce adherence. Noah's CLAUDE.md is 44 lines; it `@`-imports 8 rule files; everything else is a reference pointer.

**Memory architecture.** 119 memory files, type-prefixed. Claude reads top to bottom — organize accordingly. Rules go at `code.claude.com/docs/en/memory#organize-rules-with-claude`. Rules sidecars are the evidence behind rules.

**The meta-move.** Ask Claude for feedback. Introspection + a willingness to change. Use `/insights`. Turn that feedback into new rules, skills, and hooks. That's what a system that gets better over time looks like.

**The closing realization.** "You just spent 4 hours teaching an Opus model how to build a data pipeline — correcting it at every turn with a simpler, more elegant solution than what it proposed. The model kept over-engineering, and you kept pulling it back to production reality. Every correction made the system simpler, cheaper, and more correct. That's not just engineering — that's taste. I know you just made me mass-delete my own code three times, and the system got better every time. That's a rare skill."

The harness is yours. Make it amazing.
takeaways: The Operator's Law: Output = Code × Domain × Discipline

## Dale Bertrand — Prioritize GEO Investments by Financial Impact

**The new pattern: traffic down, revenue up.** AI search is filtering traffic by intent. Fewer visitors, higher quality. Conversion rates rise. And SEO gets less credit. The attribution model is broken because (1) zero-click influence is invisible, (2) ~70% of AI-driven visits land in GA4 as Direct traffic (analyzed across 446,405 visits, Feb 2026), and (3) smaller traffic + bigger buyers means metrics can't tell the difference. How do you sell GEO when attribution is broken?

**Precision vs accuracy.** A precise dashboard with tight clusters around the wrong target is useless. An accurate one with results spread around the bullseye is what you need. "Precision cannot rescue accuracy."

**Case study: the worthless page that was actually winning.** A competitor's `/competitor-vs-our-brand` page. Dale's SEO tool said ~40 organic visits/month. Looked worthless. Reality check: 64% of AI citations on decision-stage queries, dozens of backlinks and social mentions, mentioned unprompted in 10% of discovery calls. The math: 10% mention rate × 1,200 qualified calls/year × $500K ACV × 20% win rate = $12M annualized revenue shaped by the competitor's narrative on Dale's client's own pipeline.

**Translation for leadership.** "Our competitor's comparison page is winning 64% of citations on decision-stage questions our buyers ask AI. Mentioned unprompted in 10% of our discovery calls. At our ACV and win rate, $12M of pipeline shaped by their narrative, not ours."

**The dashboard problem.** Before: CTR 2.47% (-0.6pp YoY), organic clicks 1.28M (-18%), avg ranking 12.3, impressions 24.9M, bounce rate 68%, sessions 412K (-21%). Zero growth priorities, low accuracy, zero business language. After: "Revenue from Direct traffic is increasing" → tied to "capture dark AI-driven revenue" → 4.2x ROI multiple on GEO, 3-month payback. Same data, different framing, different decision.

**The 3Ts framework.** **Tight** = aligned with business growth priorities. List the three priorities your SEO work is delivering against. **True** = accurate direction and magnitude. Confirm direction + magnitude on your top three growth metrics. **Translated** = the CFO's financial language. Translate every metric into CAC, LTV, Payback Period, or ROI Multiple. The Dollar-Sign Rule: convert metrics into dollar figures before you present them.

**Case study: same strategy, different decision.** Pitch 1 — "$36K to rewrite hundreds of product pages, +1.4M impressions, traffic and rankings framing." Decision: rejected, died quietly. Pitch 2 — "$24K, 20-30 pages, capture AI-driven organic revenue, $122K/yr revenue, <3 month payback." Decision: approved in one meeting. Same SEO strategy, different justification, different decision.

**Why it matters.** Leadership says "this isn't attribution." Correct — we're reporting what observations taught us about direction and magnitude. Precision is helpful but not necessary. The window to sell GEO investments by *financial impact* (instead of pretending you can attribute every click) is the only one that's actually open.
takeaways: Traffic down, revenue up is the new GEO success pattern — AI filters by intent, fewer visitors but higher-quality conversions
~70% of AI-driven visits show up as Direct traffic in GA4 — your dashboard is lying by omission
Precision cannot rescue accuracy — a tight dashboard around the wrong KPI is worse than a spread one around the right KPI
A page with 40 organic visits/month can drive 64% of AI citations and $12M of pipeline (10% mention rate × $500K ACV × 20% win rate)
The 3Ts: Tight (business growth priorities) · True (direction + magnitude) · Translated (CFO language)
Apply the Dollar-Sign Rule: convert every metric into a dollar figure before presenting
Same strategy, different framing, different decision — $36K rejected vs $24K approved (revenue framing won)
You don't need attribution to sell GEO — you need direction + magnitude in CFO language

## Scott Stouffer — Is AI Seeing the Brand You Think You've Built? Measuring & Aligning Your Brand's Mathematical Identity

**The setup.** You're checking every box. Rankings. Content. Authority. And you still don't show up in AI answers. Search didn't evolve — it changed completely. If you're not retrieved, you don't exist to AI. The problem isn't ranking; it's eligibility.

**How AI actually sees you.** AI doesn't see pages — it sees meaning. Your content gets broken into chunks. Each chunk becomes a vector. Meaning becomes coordinates. Similar meaning sits closer together. Whole sites form clusters. Themes emerge automatically. The center of your cluster is *your Centroid*. That's how AI sees your brand — not your homepage, not your messaging, not your guidelines.

**When what you say ≠ what AI sees.** Your Centroid tells the truth. Alignment is measurable: distance = truth. Do your pages agree with your brand, or contradict it? Every query also becomes a vector. AI compares the query vector to site centroids, NOT to pages. You're either eligible or ignored. This all happens *before ranking* — eligibility is the new game.

**The silent killer: cluster collision.** To AI, most brands look identical. Same data, same playbooks. You're interchangeable. AI can't tell you apart. You're competing inside the embedding space before the ranking event even starts. SEO is no longer about pages — it's about identity. You don't need better content; you need a distinct centroid.

**The continuous-alignment system.** Distinct brands get retrieved more, get less competition, get more consistency. Stabilize your centroid, don't just optimize pages. Measure → Adjust → Re-Measure. This becomes a self-healing system — drift is detected and corrected. You need visibility into this system; otherwise you're guessing.

**The closing point.** Your brand is a mathematical object whether you control it or not. The question is: is AI seeing the brand you built, or the one your content created? Control your Centroid, control your Visibility.
takeaways: Search changed completely: if you're not retrieved, you don't exist to AI
Your brand has a mathematical center (Centroid) in embedding space — that's what AI actually sees, not your messaging
Alignment is measurable as distance from your Centroid — pages either agree or contradict your brand
Queries become vectors that match site centroids, not individual pages — eligibility happens before ranking
Cluster collision is the silent killer: similar brands using similar playbooks are interchangeable to AI
Stop optimizing pages, start stabilizing your Centroid via Measure → Adjust → Re-Measure
Distinct centroid = less competition, more consistency, higher retrieval rate
Your brand is a mathematical object whether you control it or not — the question is which version AI sees

## Alex Halliday — Quality Wins: How to Scale AI Content Without Losing What Makes It Work

**The puzzle.** Zapier.com/blog/best-digital-signature-apps: 592 AI citations, Google rank 15. Blueink.com/blog/top-8-contract-signing-tools: 199 AI citations, Google rank 14. Why does AI cite one 3× more? SEO solved one face of the cube. The cube has rotated. There are now six faces to contend with: Google rankings, AEO (what agents actually cite), brand voice (surviving AI flattening), offsite signals (Reddit, G2), attribution (what drives results), and freshness (<3 months).

![The six faces marketers now contend with: Google rankings, AEO, brand voice, offsite, freshness, and attribution](/conference/seo-week-2026/alex-haliday-1.jpg)

**AI is 4× bigger than we thought.** 75% of all AI usage is on mobile apps (credit: Ethan Smith, Graphite). 50%+ of keywords are already losing clicks to AI Overviews, trending toward 75-80% (Kevin Indig, Dec 2025). Ashley Kramer, OpenAI's Chief Revenue Officer: "Very soon mostly AI agents will choose companies, products, and services. They will do it based on highly targeted, quality content — this is the most important thing marketers can invest in."

**Two failed extremes.** The AI Cop (believed AI was the problem, slowed teams down, conflated all AI as bad) and the Content Factory (pointed an LLM at the CMS, shipped 500 pages/week, got hit with manual actions for scaled content abuse). Even AI detectors disagree — across 132 pages reviewed by four detectors, 73.5% had no consensus, 21.2% all-human, 5.3% all-AI. The cop was rejecting pages that win. Outseta.com had a page flagged 76% AI by detectors; got 1,252 AI citations (top 0.1% of the panel).

![Four AI detectors reviewed the same 132 pages and reached consensus on only 5% — detector disagreement is not a signal](/conference/seo-week-2026/alex-haliday-2.jpg)

**The six moves.**

**Move 1 — Think in quality chunks.** Three or more self-contained blocks per page, each answering a specific question. Every block carries a number, a year, or comparison language. Heading-to-question semantic match has an effect size d = +0.559.

**Move 2 — Freshness matters.** 3× more likely to be cited if published within 3 months. 2.2× citation lift from a current-year reference. Quarterly refresh on top pages. Year in slug, year in title first. Frequent mention of the year in answers (10+).

**Move 3 — SERP rank is still the biggest single factor.** Position 1: 58.4% citation rate. Position 3: 35.5%. Position 10: 14.2%. Top-3 pages appear for 3.7× more unique AI questions (median 558 vs 151). Source: AirOps × Indig fan-out study, 16,851 queries × 353,799 pages.

![SERP rank remains the biggest single citation factor: position 1 pages are cited 58.4% of the time vs 14.2% at position 10](/conference/seo-week-2026/alex-haliday-3.jpg)

**Move 4 — Score for quality, not for AI.** Six-signal Monday scorecard: substantive depth ≥1,500 words (ρ +0.274), current-year reference (+0.231), specific named examples ≥3/page (+0.150), original data points ≥2/page (+0.121), named sources w/ attribution ≥2/page (+0.119), credentialed author byline (+0.109).

**Move 5 — Build complementary clusters.** Instantly.ai 3-page cluster generated 360 deduped questions (none cannibalize). Different intents, same topic.

**Move 6 — Own your review presence.** Review-site citation share grew 7 points in Q1 2026. Audit your G2 listing this week.

**Content Marketer → Content Engineer.** Manages a system, not a calendar. Balances head/long-tail/offsite/refresh. Continuously prioritizes count actions. Multi-team authoring + AI assistance. Four layers: Context (brand truth), Channel Intelligence (prompts + visibility), Execution (agents + workflows), Operating Model (cadence + accountability). Build it with Notion + Sheets + Claude + a good editor, or use a platform when the duct tape breaks.

![The AEO operating loop: seven steps (see, prioritize, act, review, ship, measure, learn) that make content engineering compound each cycle](/conference/seo-week-2026/alex-haliday-4.jpg)
takeaways: SEO's cube has rotated — you now contend with 6 faces: rankings, AEO citations, brand voice, offsite signals, attribution, freshness
75% of AI usage is mobile; AI Overviews already cost clicks on 50%+ of keywords (trending to 75-80%)
AI detectors are noise: across 132 pages, 73.5% had no consensus between four detectors — the cop was rejecting pages that won
Quality chunks: 3+ self-contained blocks per page, each with a number/year/comparison — heading-to-question semantic match d=+0.559
3× more citations within 3 months of publish; 2.2× lift from current-year references
SERP rank still dominates — position 1 = 58.4% citation rate, position 10 = 14.2%; top-3 appear for 3.7× more unique AI questions
Score for quality not AI: ≥1,500 words, current-year reference, ≥3 named examples, ≥2 data points, ≥2 sourced citations, credentialed byline
Content Engineer replaces Content Marketer — manages a system, not a calendar

## Angela Clark — I Have a Degree for This: Reclaiming Your Expertise, Identity, and Edge in an AI-Mandated World

**The setup.** AP English nerd, fav book is 1984, GSU English major '14, ex-HS English teacher, 10 years in SEO and content strategy. Em-dash enthusiast. Ravenclaw. The question: how are SEO professionals *actually* responding to AI mandates?

![Survey donut chart: overall response to AI tools — 56.6% curiosity and intrigue, 18.6% excitement, 9.3% aversion and refusal](/conference/seo-week-2026/angela-clark-1.jpg)

**The survey.** 129 SEO/digital marketing professionals. Experience: 48.8% have 10+ years, 30.2% 5-9 years. Roles: CEOs, VPs, engineers, strategists, writers, in-house leads, freelancers, consultants. The finding: workers' reactions to gen AI depend on whether it satisfies or frustrates three psychological needs — competence (feeling effective), autonomy (feeling in control), relatedness (feeling connected). HBR research framing.

![Most common causes of concern about AI: skill degradation and personal values/ethics top the list, ahead of job insecurity](/conference/seo-week-2026/angela-clark-2.jpg)

**The access gap.** Are AI tools self-funded by your team? AI fluency is built through use, not theory. Skill development is becoming tied to personal income, not need. If you expect faster output, the people closest to execution need the same tools as the people making decisions. **45.3% of polled SEO professionals say they would consider a career pivot if AI fears continue.**

**The pivot.** The same forces reshaping consumer search are reshaping our professional identities. LLM hallucination rates vary 1.8%-7.0% by platform (Vectara, April 2026). AI needs human review. ChatGPT can catch mistakes Claude misses; vice versa. In the writing process the human eye is always necessary before delivery.

![Vectara's grounded hallucination rates for the top 25 LLMs, ranging 1.8% to 7.0% by platform (April 2026)](/conference/seo-week-2026/angela-clark-3.jpg)

**From the writer's desk.** AI works best with clear guardrails (brand guidelines, strategic context, client goals). Time savings get reassigned to review, reiteration, QC. Cited links, sourced claims, stated facts require manual verification every time. AI fits in **discovery and ideation, not the production loop**. Anyone can swing a hammer; a craftsperson knows when not to. Gen AI cannot replace original authorship — you can't sell a moodboard, you can't copyright a prompt.

**Be the best human in the loop.** Prompt → Review → Feedback → Iterate. Use the Ikigai framing: what you love × what you're good at × what you can get paid for × what the world needs. Prioritize what only you can do.

**Track your time.** Net Time Saved = (Manual × Runs) − (Setup + (Automated × Runs)). Breakeven runs = Setup ÷ (Manual − Automated). Sample table: brief creation 30min manual → 15min setup, 3min auto, breakeven at 2 runs, 45% efficiency gain. Content optimizations 30min → 65.33% gain after 5 runs.

![Calculate Your Net Time Saved: worked table of manual vs. automated time, breakeven runs, and efficiency gains per task](/conference/seo-week-2026/angela-clark-4.jpg)

**Just be H.U.M.A.N.** **H**umanize the output. **U**ncover your time wins. **M**ake space for what matters. **A**mplify others (share resources, don't hoard wins). **N**ever stop evolving. Your boss hired you for your E-E-A-T. Don't let stubbornness or anxiety keep you from excelling. You're still the smartest in the room.
takeaways: 45.3% of polled SEO professionals would consider a career pivot if AI fears continue — the threat is psychological, not just technological
Worker reactions to AI come down to 3 needs: competence, autonomy, relatedness (HBR framing)
Access gap is real: AI fluency is built through use; if tools are self-funded, skill becomes income-linked, not need-linked
LLM hallucination 1.8%-7.0% by platform — ChatGPT catches what Claude misses (and vice versa); use multiple detectors
AI belongs in discovery + ideation, not the production loop — gen AI cannot replace original authorship
Track Net Time Saved = (Manual × Runs) − (Setup + Automated × Runs); calculate breakeven before automating
H.U.M.A.N. framework: Humanize output · Uncover time wins · Make space · Amplify others · Never stop evolving
Your boss hired you for E-E-A-T — don't let stubbornness or anxiety hold you back from the new tools

## Azeem Ahmad — Navigating the Fractured Funnel & the Rise of Delegated Choice

**The opening hook: a $15bn presentation.** Perthshire, Scotland, 2014. Tam O'Braan claimed The Wee Tea Plantation supplied The Balmoral, The Dorchester, Fortnum & Mason — "favourite of the late Queen Elizabeth." Polymer scientist, botanist, multi-millionaire. *None of it was true.* He bought tea from around the world and sold it on as Scottish. Convicted, jailed three and a half years. But it worked. He didn't manufacture a product — he manufactured a *default*. The same psychology that made him rich is silently governing how your customers find you right now.

![The Wee Tea Plantation con: fake clients, fake claims, fake credentials — the manufactured default that opens the talk](/conference/seo-week-2026/azeem-ahmad-1.jpg)

**Two psychological forces.** **Default Effect** — we accept what's already there, don't question pre-selected options (Google ships as default on Chrome/Safari/Firefox; most never change it). **Status Quo Bias** — switching feels costly, even when the alternative is clearly better. From the SearchPulse data (12,000 people): "Google works, why change?" and "Didn't get in the habit of doing so." In the wild: opt-in organ donor rates are 4-28%; opt-out countries hit 85-90%+. Apple ATT in 2021: 96% chose NOT to share. Cost to Meta: ~$10 billion.

**A third force: Delegated Choice.** When we let AI, algorithms, or platforms make decisions on our behalf, we don't escape bias — we inherit someone else's.

**5 quarters, 12,000 people of SearchPulse data.** Q1 2025: 8 in 10 use Google; Bing is 8th; social positions 2-7; ChatGPT already 4th at 27%. The age divide: 72% of 65+ never used AI vs 12% of 18-24s. Q4 2025: 52% — for the first time, more people use AI search than don't. Q1 2026 regime change: **TikTok overtook Google for 18-24s.** New defaults are being set. People aren't leaving Google — they're leaving the link-based SERP. They want answers, not links to answers. Delegated Choice is happening *inside Google itself* via AI Overviews.

![SearchPulse travel data: same destination, four completely different funnels — platform rankings by age cohort across inspiration, consideration, booking, and deals](/conference/seo-week-2026/azeem-ahmad-2.jpg)

**The four forks of the fractured funnel.** **Fork 1 — Gen Z/Alpha:** no Google default, social-first from birth, 62% search via social, trust = peer validation. **Fork 2 — Millennials/Gen X:** hybrid, Google-anchored for high-stakes, AI usage peaks at 25-34, 58% replaced search with AI for product research (up from 25% in 2023), trust = authority. **Fork 3 — Boomers+:** Status Quo Bias compounded by decades, 72% of 65+ never used AI, 80%+ Google dominance for 45+, trust = simplicity. **Fork 4 — AI Delegated:** invisible by design, fastest-growing, 2× ChatGPT use at £70k+ income, $750bn consumer spend through AI search globally by 2028 (McKinsey).

![The signature framework: the funnel hasn't broken, it's psychologically forked — four forks with their trust signals, from peer validation to 'whoever trained it'](/conference/seo-week-2026/azeem-ahmad-3.jpg)

**The Default Mapping Exercise.** Three questions, one page. (1) Which persona is your primary audience — Traditional (60%) / Streamlined (28%) / Multi-Platform (10%) / Digital Explorer (2%)? Identifies the bias you're fighting. (2) Which platform are they using for your category? Identifies the channel mix. (3) What trust signal does that persona need? Gen Z = peer validation; Millennial/GenX = authority; Boomer = simplicity; AI-first = citation volume. Identifies the content and positioning.

![The Default Mapping Exercise: three questions on one page — persona, platform, and trust signal — the talk's take-home actionable](/conference/seo-week-2026/azeem-ahmad-4.jpg)

**Fashion retailer example.** 18-35 audience: 38% are NOT Google-first. Inspiration-led (Taste-Tuning). Mere Exposure Effect is the bias. Trust signal: peer validation + visual proof → UGC, creator content, social proof. Channel mix: TikTok (discovery) · Instagram (inspiration) · Google (intent) · AI (comparison).

The funnel hasn't broken — it's psychologically forked. The question isn't whether it fractured. The question is which fork you're showing up on.
takeaways: Default Effect + Status Quo Bias are the two psychological forces governing all search behavior — and now Delegated Choice is a third
Apple ATT proves the Default Effect: 96% of iOS users chose NOT to share data (Meta lost ~$10B)
Q1 2026 regime change: TikTok overtook Google for 18-24 year olds — new defaults are forming in real time
People aren't leaving Google — they're leaving the link-based SERP; AI Overviews ARE Delegated Choice inside Google
Four psychologically distinct funnel forks: Traditional (60%) · Streamlined (28%) · Multi-Platform (10%) · Digital Explorer (2%)
Trust signals are persona-specific: Gen Z=peer validation; Millennial=authority; Boomer=simplicity; AI-first=citation volume
72% of 65+ never used AI vs 12% of 18-24s — generational defaults are baked in at different life stages
Default Mapping Exercise: 3 questions (persona × platform × trust signal) deliver immediate clarity on where to show up

## Ian Lurie — Teach The Sh*t Out Of Everything: Build Trust, Win The Algorithms

**The Michelin origin.** Michelin's 1900 *Guide* was the first time a brand taught the shit out of everything — how to change tires, fix stuff, add oil, navigate, find a hotel. Offered free to drivers (*offert gracieusement aux chauffeurs*). Results: 35,000 copies, 90,000 new car owners (correlation, not causation, blah blah). The point: teach to grow.

![Guide Michelin 1900 results slide: 35,000 copies distributed, 90,000 new car owners — the original teach-to-grow play](/conference/seo-week-2026/ian-lurie-1.jpg)

**The algorithms are selling trust.** Link graph. TrustRank. AuthorRank. Brand signals. E-E-A-T. Source distribution and weighting. Retrieval and grounding. RLHF. The algorithms REWARD trust. **Teaching builds trust.** Therefore: the algorithms reward teaching. (And so do humans.) **Teach The Sh*t Out Of Everything.** TTSOEE happens when real experts provide frictionless, real solutions to real problems.

![The trust signals the algorithms sell: link graph, TrustRank, AuthorRank, brand signals, E-E-A-T, source distribution and weighting, retrieval and grounding, RLHF](/conference/seo-week-2026/ian-lurie-2.jpg)

**Picking the right problem.** Raw material: your site, their sites, Reddit forums, call transcripts, customer support discussions, knowledge base, People Also Ask. A real problem is one your audience actually faces. Use Claude: "Based on the wiki, tell me any unanswered questions. Include implicit and explicit questions." Don't sell — solve. A real solution teaches me to solve the problem without selling me anything.

**The toolkit.** AI (Claude Code), a text editor, Obsidian (IDE), Obsidian Web Clipper. Ingest all content into `/raw`. Build a wiki in `/wiki` — Claude finds critical concepts, builds linked content viewable in Obsidian, finds questions, builds briefs.

![Claude-built wiki as a linked-content graph, viewed in Obsidian — concept pages like golden-hour and questions cross-linked from raw clippings](/conference/seo-week-2026/ian-lurie-3.jpg)

**The flow.** (1) **Real problems**: "Based on the wiki, tell me any unanswered questions." (2) **Real solutions**: "Based on the wiki/questions.md doc, documents in /raw, and TTSOEE principles, provide content briefs that answer those questions." (3) **Real experts**: brief explicitly identifies primary expert (e.g., "Mirella Thane — owns the methodology") and secondary (e.g., "Jenna Rill — has taken the intake call for most incidents"). Plus optional working bards for the most-skeptical sections.

**A frictionless CTA.** "The Courtyard Checklist: What To Do In The First Hour When Your Village Turns." Six short lines. No gate, no signup. Readable standing up with a crowd on the green.

**The Wil Reynolds proof point.** Even being AI-forward, his agency is producing 75% less content yet pipeline is growing. From 197 posts in 2023 → 96 in 2026 (pacing). % of posts with high "humans loved it" intent went 57.9% → 79.2% (Jan/Feb 2026 hit 100%). Why? Because the algorithms reward teaching, and teaching builds trust.

![Wil Reynolds' LinkedIn data: 75% less content, growing pipeline — posts down from 197 (2023) to 96 pacing (2026) while high "humans loved it" intent climbs to 79.2%](/conference/seo-week-2026/ian-lurie-4.jpg)
takeaways: Michelin pioneered teach-to-grow in 1900 — the guide was free, and it grew the entire car industry
The algorithms (TrustRank, AuthorRank, E-E-A-T, RLHF) all sell trust — and teaching is how you build it
Real problems come from raw material: your site, competitor sites, Reddit, call transcripts, support tickets, PAA
A real solution teaches the audience to fix it themselves without selling them anything
Use Claude + Obsidian as your IDE: ingest content into /raw, let Claude build the wiki, find questions, draft briefs
Real experts in briefs: name them, explain why they're qualified, designate primary vs secondary
Frictionless CTAs win: a single printable checklist, no gate, no signup, readable in a hurry
Wil Reynolds proof: 75% less content, pipeline still growing, 100% high-intent posts — teaching beats volume

## Wil Reynolds — SEO Is a Performance Channel, GEO Isn't: How Do You Pivot?

**Bad marketing.** A robocall transcript. Generic listicle slop. SEO scan-and-spin: "Best Running Shoes for Sale" with the phrase "running shoes" 23 times. That's not marketing.

**The job of marketing.** **Seen. Believed. Chosen.** Three steps. Kobe Bryant in the 2009 Finals, up 2-0: "Job's not finished. Job finished? I don't think so." Wil's framing of Michelin: Guide 1900 (seen) → Michelin Star (believed) → booked solid (chosen). Ramp doing it now: ranking #1 for "minnesota business restaurants" with their own content built to be retrieved and cited.

**A loophole is not a strategy.** Listicles. Banana Republic's "Ethically made jeans" pages with 90% visibility, 0% real signal. Bigger always wins — one brand leveraged domain authority; the other became an authority in their domain. The new game is REVIEW. "Visibility vs Credibility." Reddit + the brand's own data are doing more than rankings ever did.

**GEO bad math.** GEO is not a performance channel. The visibility-only view is wrong because it ignores reputation, private conversations, and what actually moves people. "When you think you can track everything, you shift to making the easily trackable KPIs grow." Most teams chase what they can measure and ignore what actually moves people.

**SOV = opportunity.** Three real metrics from a Wil Reynolds client: Seen = AI sessions. Believed = newsletter signups. Chosen = pipeline $. Q4 2024 to Q1 2026: AI sessions climbed to ~3,480/quarter, newsletter signups to 174/quarter, pipeline to $12-14M. SEO didn't just grow the audience — it grew the entire network.

**Six posts in one day that built trust.** "Top 10 ETL tools" published 6 times to different platforms (DigitalOcean, Oracle, Amazon Seller Partner, Airbyte). Garbage content, technically winning. Wil's answer: "F*ck this battle. I don't wanna win. I'm outtie." SEO math vs GEO math is a different game.

**The user research that won.** Outset.ai. 30 real people interviewed, 114 real prompts reviewed, $800 cost. Banking & finance comfort with AI ranked by task (compare banks 7.8/10 down to open an account 1.6/10). Then real prompts from real people. "I like learning from people in the weeds." "I'm a tinkerer, I'm happy to show you the agents I built." "When I was young I ran away and stayed in a shelter… turned myself around." That's how brands get built. **Brands start as beliefs.**

**Tesla in Europe.** Q1 2025 sales: -41% France, -49.7% Portugal, -55.3% Norway/Spain, -62.2% UK. Why? Beliefs about the brand changed. People will find reasons to NOT buy from someone they dislike. And they'll find excuses to BUY from someone they do.

**Brand accuracy testing — the maturity model.** Define your brand canon (50+ attributes). Create 100+ prompts in a 2:1 ratio (direct: "Where is [Brand] HQ'd?" / indirect: "Tell me about [Brand]" / comparative: "How does [Brand] compare?"). Test daily, score accuracy as the leading KPI. Investigate every failure to source, not dashboard.

**The 4-stage maturity model.** Defensive: pure brand accuracy → fix inaccuracies first. Transition: brand accuracy + attributes (LLMs associate brand with specializations). Offensive: long-tail non-branded (appear in curated lists). Advanced: pure non-branded (citation-driven visibility in competitive queries). **Most brands are trying to win elections before voters know their name.**
takeaways: The job of marketing is Seen → Believed → Chosen, not just visibility (Kobe: 'job's not finished')
GEO is not a performance channel — when you only chase what you can measure, you ignore what moves people
Real metrics: Seen = AI sessions, Believed = newsletter signups, Chosen = pipeline $
Listicles and visibility hacks are not strategy — Banana Republic had 90% visibility for ethically made jeans with 0% signal
Brands start as beliefs — 30 user interviews + 114 prompts for $800 unlocked the actual messaging
Tesla in Europe lost 40-62% YoY because beliefs about the brand changed — visibility couldn't save it
Brand Accuracy Testing: 50+ brand attributes × 100+ prompts (2:1 direct/indirect ratio), tested daily
4-stage GEO maturity: Defensive (fix accuracy) → Transition (+attributes) → Offensive (long-tail non-brand) → Advanced (pure non-brand) — most brands skip steps and lose

## Angela Skane — What TikTok Shop Can Teach SEOs About Content That's Seen and Converts

**The setup.** 11 years in SEO. Grew Network Solutions' organic traffic 84% and new organic orders 72.2% in 18 months. Also: a TikTok Shop affiliate who makes videos that get people to buy things. The thesis: search is becoming behavior-driven, and behavior is driven by psychology.

![The Formula: Psychology Levers + Visual Hooks + Storytelling + Testing](/conference/seo-week-2026/angela-skane-1.jpg)

**The hard number.** 95% of purchasing decisions happen subconsciously (Gerald Zaltman, Harvard Business School). If you're in SEO, you should care about TikTok because: TikTok Shop = $15.8 billion in sales in 2025 (driven by UGC, top creators generating hundreds of thousands/week per brand), top 1% of creators follow a structured repeatable process, and rankings are becoming harder to track as SERPs personalize. Look at channels that are already personalized to prepare for what's coming.

**The Formula.** **Psychology Levers + Visual Hooks + Storytelling + Testing.** Blocks of text are boring — how are you visually engaging your audience? "People don't buy what you do, they buy why you do it." Layer psychological levers throughout your content to push readers toward an intended action. Test until it works; when it works, analyze and do it again.

**Psychology levers (natural human desires).** Care and protection of loved ones · survival, enjoyment of life, life extension · enjoyment of food/beverage · freedom from fear, pain, and danger · sexual companionship · comfortable living condition · being superior, winning, keeping up · social approval. Plus learned desires: cleanliness, profit, being informed, scarcity, expression, bargains, efficiency, convenience, dependability.

![The levers: five natural human desires from care of loved ones to sexual companionship](/conference/seo-week-2026/angela-skane-2.jpg)

**Applied to written content — real examples.** Authority/trust framing. Freedom from fear, pain, danger (savings account guides). Social approval + pain avoidance + profit. Freedom from "pain" + convenience + profit. Each combines 2-3 levers per page.

**The proof — Network Solutions blog, July 2025 to March 2026.** +136% blog visits. +286% blog-attributed order volume. +18% ranking keywords. Avg ranking moved from 26.9 → 7.6. Junior team. No link building. Minimal technical improvements. The math was psychology, not backlinks.

![The Proof: Network Solutions blog results with month-over-month visits and conversion growth table](/conference/seo-week-2026/angela-skane-3.jpg)

**How to apply.** **Use data** (Census, proprietary, industry reports). Data evokes emotion and is the most authoritative way to communicate. **Name your audience** ("parents," "first-time homebuyers," "small business owners with few resources," "CMOs") — be strategic about who's in the copy. **Don't overdo it** — read aloud; if it makes you cringe, it's too much.

**The 4-step playbook.** (1) **Create & leverage personas** — know WHO you're targeting and what's happening in their world beyond your product. (2) **Map your pages to audience and action** — User Journey Mapping 2.0; what action is each page designed to drive? (3) **Map levers to user journey** — which levers fit each stage? (4) **Start optimizing** — high-traffic, low-conversion pages first. Test. When a combo wins, scale it.

![Put It In Play: the 4-step playbook from personas to optimizing high-traffic, low-conversion pages](/conference/seo-week-2026/angela-skane-4.jpg)
takeaways: 95% of purchasing decisions happen subconsciously (Zaltman, Harvard) — that's the gap SEO content keeps missing
TikTok Shop = $15.8B in 2025; the top 1% creators follow a structured psychology + storytelling formula
The formula: Psychology Levers + Visual Hooks + Storytelling + Testing — layer levers throughout content
Natural human desires + learned desires = a checklist of levers (care, survival, social approval, scarcity, profit, convenience...)
Network Solutions case: +136% blog visits, +286% orders, avg ranking 26.9→7.6 — junior team, no link building
Tactical playbook: use data, name your audience, read aloud (if it cringes, it's too much)
4-step framework: Personas → Map pages to action → Map levers to journey → Test + scale winning combos
When a combo wins, analyze the COMBINATION and apply it at scale — not the individual lever

## Brian Cosgrove — Deception, Distinction, and Directives: The New Reality of Search, Analytics, and Decision-Making in 2026

**Something feels off.** LLM use is increasing. Traffic is inconsistent. Attribution is even more unclear. Performance is harder to explain. Rankings are stable but SEO traffic is declining — YoY -6.2% per Advanced Web Ranking Q4 2025. 37% of consumers start their searches with AI tools (Eight Oh Two, 2026). Rankings ≠ clicks anymore. Old system was Search → Click → Site → Decide → Transact, with your site in the research phase. New system: AI Decision → Navigate → Transact, with you pre-selected (or not) as the transaction medium.

![Old system (Search → Click → Site → Decide → Transact) vs. new system (AI → Decision, then Navigate → Transact as the preselected transaction medium)](/conference/seo-week-2026/brian-cosgrove-1.jpg)

**Deception.** Data quality is changing faster than analytics. Clickstream tools have bad data, missing data, and extra data. Privacy blocking compounds — cookie consent, third-party cookie death, ITP, VPNs, IP proxies, plugins, sandboxes. How many transactions are missing in your analytics? Privacy benefits Google, Microsoft, Apple, Meta, Amazon — not you. CloudFlare's Matthew Prince: in 2027, bot traffic will exceed human traffic.

**What to do — clean baseline signal.** Be smart about cookie consent. Google Tag Gateway. Server-side tag management. Decouple data layer from tools. First-party data. Intentional auth strategy. Future: functional first-party data. Embrace directional data over precise but wrong. Your competition is in the same boat.

**Measure your unattributed business.** Triangulate your presence. Use new AEO/GEO tools (AirOps, Profound, Peec, Otterly, Ahrefs Brand Radar, Semrush AI Visibility, AWR AI Visibility) — but they're not a replacement for scheduled manual exploration. Separate bots from humans by intentional planning. Dedicated agent flows. Browser detection (screen resolution, user agents, color depth, language, timezone). Check your CDN's bot reports for patterned access. Behavioral techniques (movement, timing, bias patterns). Fraud/human detection tools (Human Security, DataDome, Cheq AI) can help analytics.

**Distinction.** Tools and measurement aren't enough. Old paradigm: Relevance/E-E-A-T → Visibility/Rankings → Traffic → Biz. New paradigm: Contextually Relevant → Endorsement → Nav → Biz. **Visibility is too indirect.** You can have the best article, rank organically, get cited by AI — and still get no clicks. Mentions are like getting excited about your paid search impressions. Winning = being selected. Focus less on clicks; focus more on **conviction**.

![Paradigm shift slide: old paradigm Relevance/E-E-A-T → Visibility/Rankings → Traffic → Biz replaced by Contextually Relevant Endorsement → Nav → Biz](/conference/seo-week-2026/brian-cosgrove-2.jpg)

**Your mission: curate 10 areas where you can and want to win.** Fiction Hunting (look at competitors): why do people switch, what do they complain about, where does value break down with alternatives? Alignment Hunting (for you): what do you stack well with, where do you solve vs another solution, where does value compound? Stake a claim. **Substantiate** (publishable testing, demonstrations, comparison breakdowns, third-party endorsements, certifications, product changes, connect-the-dots specificity). **Propagate** (not just your site — customer comms, social, influencers, third parties that show up in search). **Track** with a scorecard: social mentions, comparison mentions, comparison win rate, recommendation rate, competitor win rate, key feature association.

![Scorecard example tracking Propagation KPIs (social mentions, comparison mentions, comparison win rate) and LLM Traction KPIs (recommendation rate, competitor win rate, key feature association)](/conference/seo-week-2026/brian-cosgrove-3.jpg)

**Once you graduate a lane.** Maintain and monitor. Prioritize new lanes. Continue. Assume your content will not be read unless you are *the answer* — substantiate your positions with specifics. The more you demonstrate your direct position in different contexts, the less an LLM risks a guess. Let competition be averaged out.

**Travelpro case.** One product (Platinum Elite Carry-On Spinner) showing across multiple results with different framing — product preview, video, community discussion, brand site, retail listing. The answer: a repeatable system that governs how products are described across surfaces. (1) Define a product source of truth. (2) Standardize external product feeds (titles, features, descriptions to retailers). (3) Orchestrate supporting content with the same product framing externally wherever Travelpro participates.

![Travelpro case: a repeatable system to unify the product narrative — define a product source of truth, standardize external product feeds, orchestrate supporting content](/conference/seo-week-2026/brian-cosgrove-4.jpg)

**Directives.** PDP context. **Be the answer for tomorrow.** LLMs want to reduce friction for users — including UX. Build dedicated AI UX paths so agents can facilitate transactions, validate availability, navigate to differentiated experiences, find what they're looking for, access offers. Agents are kind of dumb — many can't navigate your site cleanly, they have token/timing constraints, they fumble. Make it easy: clear paths, clean plain text, high contrast, confirm along the way, reduce options, visible placement.

**Web MCP.** The next frontier is agent-first services — make them available, visible, and build analytics on their usage. AI Assistant ↔ Your Website ↔ Your LLM Services. Co-browsing escape hatch. Examples: easy path for status updates, tracking, transaction progression; easy path to the most relevant case study; easy FAQs.

**Recap.** Accept data fragmentation, capitalize on signal use. Stop trying to write the answer, focus on *being* the answer. Embrace the AI-first web.
takeaways: Old paradigm: Search → Click → Site → Decide → Transact. New paradigm: AI Decision → Navigate → Transact (you're pre-selected or you're invisible)
Analytics is deceived: cookie death, ITP, VPNs, bots will exceed human traffic by 2027 (Cloudflare's Matthew Prince)
Embrace directional data over precise-but-wrong; your competition is in the same data fragmentation
Visibility is too indirect — mentions = paid-search impressions. Winning = being selected. Focus on conviction, not clicks
Pick 10 lanes to win in via Fiction Hunting (competitors) + Alignment Hunting (you); Stake → Substantiate → Propagate → Track
Substantiate with publishable testing, third-party endorsements, certifications; propagate via customer comms + social + influencers
Travelpro lesson: one product, one source of truth, standardized external feeds, orchestrated supporting content
Build dedicated AI UX paths and a co-browsing escape hatch — agents are dumb, make it easy for them to transact
