## Brie Anderson — We Had One Job (& It Wasn't Rankings)

**The whiplash.** "Where is my traffic?!" "Why are our impressions down?!" Then the GA4 view: -7.7%, -27.2%, -9.2%, -6.2%, grand total -4.7%. We f*cked up. Hear me out. The history of zero-click: 2004 Google Local → 2007 Universal Search → 2010 Google Instant → 2012 Knowledge Panels → 2013 Quick Answers → 2017 Featured Snippets / PAA → **2018 Zero-click passed 50%** → 2021 64.82% of Google searches zero-click → 2024 AI Overviews. We've been complaining about traffic disappearing since 2018.

![Timeline of zero-click search features from Google Local in 2004 to AI Overviews in 2024](/conference/seo-week-2026/brie-anderson-1.jpg)

**Wil Reynolds in 2017** ("I'd Rather Be Thanked Than Ranked") was telling us. We weren't listening.

**The fundamental error.** We SOLD rankings and traffic. The job was never rankings. The job was business outcomes. When traffic drops 7%, the question is whether the LOST traffic was valuable — or whether the smaller, higher-quality remaining traffic is converting better. Most SEO dashboards can't tell you.

**The new questions.** Rankings drop? — Are we losing traffic of value? Do we need a recovery plan? Search volume down? — Is the market shrinking? New language to adapt? Seasonal? Branded search up? — Did someone mention us somewhere? What's the sentiment? Are the right pages showing up?

**Industry-specific drives strategy. Business-specific shows value.** It's not that hard — what were you hired to do, for real? **Talk to stakeholders.** Goals. Fears. Investments. Own your outcomes. Track everything you do: cluster/pillar content, internal links, PR mentions, page speed, site structure, blog posts, citations, backlinks, structured data.

**Audit your traffic sources.** Most teams stop at "Direct, Organic Search, Paid, Referral." Look deeper. Brie's example showed referral sources nobody's tracking: chat.mistral.ai, gemini.google.com, perplexity.ai, claude.ai, chatgpt.com, adaptichat.com, chat.chatbotapp.ai, chat.corp.stripe.com, chat.zalo.me, chat.atxp.ai. Each is a new acquisition channel. If you're sending users from somewhere else, **use UTMs**. Have standards. Build a UTM builder that ensures GA4 channel classification works.

![GA4 referral report revealing untracked AI acquisition channels like chat.mistral.ai, gemini.google.com, perplexity.ai, and claude.ai](/conference/seo-week-2026/brie-anderson-2.jpg)

**The custom funnel proof.** Standard funnel: Visited site (318,514, 100%) → Viewed item (86,316, 27.1%) → Added item to cart (3,287, 1%) → Begin Checkout (1,851, 0.6%) → Purchase (170, 0.05%).

**The segment comparison that proves SEO drove revenue.** Filter to ONLY users who hit a specific blog post: 42,144 users, 1.63% conversion, 765 transactions, $147,366 total revenue → vs the comparison: 816 users, **6.86% conversion**, 66 transactions, $14,947 revenue. Variant rate 8.09% vs control 4.61%, +45.5% relative lift, p < 0.001. Statistically significant. **"Users are 3.4× more likely to purchase after viewing this page."** 2% of users generated 10% of revenue at $18.30/user.

![Significance test showing users are 3.4x more likely to purchase after viewing the blog post, with 99% confidence and +345.6% relative lift](/conference/seo-week-2026/brie-anderson-3.jpg)

**Track events (not just pageviews).** Tool use. Link clicks. Page views. FAQ interactions. Video watches. Use custom funnels in GA4 Explorations. Compare *features click → purchase intent event* (6.71% conversion) vs *all product page views → purchase intent event* (4.61% conversion). The feature you fought to build IS moving the needle. Statistically significant.

**Register custom dimensions.** Page speed, link type, content group, question, video title. Use them as breakdown dimensions in funnel exploration. Track CLICK TEXT specifically so you can see which CTAs convert. Ingredients clicks (1,214, 6.43%) vs Feeding Guide (716, 6.56%) vs Reviews (96, **16.67%** — small sample, big win signal).

![GA4 funnel exploration broken down by Click Text: Ingredients 6.43%, Feeding Guide 6.56%, Reviews 16.67% completion](/conference/seo-week-2026/brie-anderson-4.jpg)

**The point.** You weren't hired to make organic clicks go up. You were hired to make the business better. SEO didn't just grow our audience — it grew our entire network. Get the credit you deserve, but only by tying your work to the things the business cares about.
takeaways: Zero-click crossed 50% in 2018; 64.82% by 2021; AI Overviews accelerated it — we've had the warning for 8 years
Wil Reynolds told us in 2017 ('Rather Be Thanked Than Ranked'). We sold rankings instead
Stop dashboard-reporting traffic deltas — ask whether the LOST traffic was valuable or the REMAINING is converting better
Audit your traffic sources to the source/medium level — chat.mistral.ai, perplexity.ai, claude.ai are unaccounted-for channels
UTM standards: build a UTM builder, ensure GA4 channel classification, AKA AP (Always Properly tag)
Use GA4 Conditions Viewer + segment comparison to prove a single page is driving 3.4× higher conversion (statistically significant)
Track events, not just pageviews — features click → purchase intent funnel proves which features actually drive purchase
Register custom dimensions (click text, content group) so funnel exploration shows you the WHICH-CTA-WINS data

## Brie Moreau — Inside the LLM Black Box: 2,000 Hours of Research, 11 Million AI Citations, How Visibility in LLMs Actually Works

**The opener.** Pull out your phone. Open ChatGPT. Type "Best hotel to stay in Hawaii." Who didn't get either Four Seasons or Ritz-Carlton? Backstory: Brie's team used data science to rank a client #1 for "online casino." This works in every niche.

![The opener: ChatGPT answering "Best hotel to stay in Hawaii" — Four Seasons and Ritz-Carlton dominate the cited results](/conference/seo-week-2026/brie-moreau-1.jpg)

**Who they are.** A Data Science / AI SEO Research Lab specializing in backlinks and AI citations. Their thesis: give Google the cleanest signal. Page-level traffic, not site-level. Backlinks from pages ranking for the keyword *and* related keywords. They call it Semantic Backlinks. That's how Google sees you, not your DR.

**Common Crawl.** The foundational data set for LLMs. The ChatGPT/Google overlap is only 12% across 100 SERPs of 650 ChatGPT executions (Josh Blyskal study, 40M AI results). LLMs don't see the SERP — they see Common Crawl.

![ChatGPT and Google overlap only 12% — 100 SERP analyses of 650 ChatGPT executions (Josh Blyskal study)](/conference/seo-week-2026/brie-moreau-2.jpg)

**Sample poisoning is real.** You can attack an LLM with only 250 documents (Anthropic research). The threat model is asymmetric — small targeted negative content can shift representation.

**The microdose.** Think in 768 dimensions instead of 3. TensorBoard data projector view of embeddings, 100k points, dimension 768, cosine + euclidean similarity. The takeaway is that AI Citation Engineering is a vector-space problem, not a text problem.

**2,000 hours, 11M+ AI Citations analyzed.** In collaboration with Michal Suski (Surfer SEO) and Manik Bhan (Search Atlas). Method: Crawl, Extract, Vectorize, Embed, find correlations.

**Box-plot results, top-10 citations vs the rest:**
- Keyword Appropriateness to Page Content: top-10 cluster tighter and higher.
- Keyword Cosine Similarity to Page Content: top-10 cluster higher.
- Keyword Cosine Similarity to Topic Word: same pattern.
- Keyword Cosine Similarity to Page Title: same pattern.

**Context — most AI citations are FRESH.** The RRF top-N playbook. Recency dominates.

**Co-Citation Similarity — the gold strike.** Co-Citation Networks: A, B, C, D citing documents → E, F, G, H, I, J as direct citation links + co-citation links. Visualizing co-citation clusters reveals the structure of who cites alongside whom. One layer deeper: **Harmonic Centrality.** Analogy: Paris vs Frankfurt — which airport has more connections? Harmonic Centrality finds the influencers.

![Co-Citation Networks: citing documents A-D link to E-J via direct citation links and co-citation clusters](/conference/seo-week-2026/brie-moreau-3.jpg)

**Co-Citation Hijacking.** If you understand which sites are co-cited, you can hijack the citation network.

**AI Citations are dominated by listicles.** Why? Content type breakdown of 176M citations: Other 39.35%, **Comparative Listicles 32.5%**, Blogs/Opinion 9.91%, Commercial/Store 4.73%, Homepage 3.75%, Community/Forum 3.36%, Documentation/Wiki 2.73%, News 2.1%. (Josh Blyskal, Brighton SEO San Diego 2025.)

![Content-type breakdown of 176M AI citations: Comparative Listicles take 32.5%, second only to Other](/conference/seo-week-2026/brie-moreau-4.jpg)

**The SurferSEO dataset.** 90,914 unique root domains identified. 248,641 total URLs analyzed. Exact-match domain rate 7.85%. Even at 25% close rate that's a huge link opportunity for Surfer clients.

**What to do — DIY AI Citation Outreach.** (1) Start tracking prompts today. (2) Wait 1-2 months for a large sample (~100k AI citations from ~100 prompts in 2 months). (3) Cluster (use freeaudit.wldm.io). (4) Outreach the best clusters for link insertions. **Do you see it differently now?**
takeaways: ChatGPT vs Google SERP overlap is only 12% — LLMs see Common Crawl, not the SERP
Sample poisoning works with only 250 documents (Anthropic research) — small targeted negative content can shift LLM representation
AI citations correlate with semantic similarity: top-10 citations cluster tighter on cosine similarity to page content, title, and topic
Most AI citations are FRESH — recency dominates the RRF top-N playbook
Co-Citation Similarity is the gold strike: cluster the network of who cites alongside whom
Harmonic Centrality finds the influencer hubs (analogy: Paris vs Frankfurt airport connectivity)
32.5% of AI citations are comparative listicles (Josh Blyskal, 176M citations analyzed)
DIY playbook: track prompts → wait 1-2 months → cluster citations → outreach the best clusters for link insertions

## Carrie Rose — 7 Small Creative Changes That Lead to BIG Discovery Wins

**The setup.** CEO/founder of Rise at Seven (NYC, London, Manchester). Founded June 2019 to push the boundaries in both creative and technical SEO. The hypothesis: put search marketers and creatives in the same agency and see what happens.

**The landscape problem.** 35-50 new SERP features introduced by Google in recent years, and most aren't sending traffic. AI overviews, perspectives, discussions, forums, continuous scroll, Google Lens, shopping graph. The last four years has seen more creative content features than the previous decade combined.

![Google search features timeline 2014-2025: the last four years added more creative content features (AI overviews, Lens, shopping graph, AI mode) than the previous decade](/conference/seo-week-2026/carrie-rose-1.jpg)

**The framing.** "Effective SEO is about expanding your digital footprint across the entire online ecosystem" (Phil Clark). We break down team silos. We need to get as interconnected as algorithms. Tiny changes don't feel powerful in the moment — over time, they completely change where you end up.

**Change 1 — Become a search insight engine that fuels all channels.** The first thing you need is a voice in the room. Search is the gateway to behavior. Advertising puts brands in front of people not knowing what they want. We work in search; we know exactly what people want. Set up weekly rising-alerts for keyword growth. Track thousands of keywords with Glimpse. Pull keyword growth trends. Data is the heart of marketing — and search is the human truth.

![Stop treating SEO like a channel: old way (siloed PR/social/SEO/paid/onsite) vs new way with search insight at the centre feeding every channel](/conference/seo-week-2026/carrie-rose-2.jpg)

**Change 2 — Get specific on who you are.** In Digital PR, every outreach email is a chance to engineer what Google and LLMs know about you. "Airalo, leading tech start-up" → "What do you do? Sell eSims" → "Global eSim provider, Airalo." Then a comms framework for SEO across global / US / UAE / Indonesia, each with story types tailored to local media. Same trick for products: site-wide → sneakers → gym wear (each with their own expert team and story type).

**Change 3 — Get smart around link signals (keywords in proximity of a link).** You can engineer the semantic signals around your links. Media analysis: less than 1% of Airalo's referring domains have "eSim" in the surrounding text. (Holafly = 1.52%, Mint = 2.2%.) After 600 new links where 65% mention eSim in proximity → 70% LLM share of voice (per Profound). You can literally engineer signals for both Google AND LLMs.

**Change 4 — Get specific on who this is for.** The audience-insight industry is worth $140B annually, but brands spend ~90% of budget on activation, not understanding their audience. Build modular content pillars audience-first: "Freelancers working remotely in LA" + "wants a pool with afternoon sun after work" → "Best hotels in LA with pools that get sun after 3pm" → blog/listicle + TikTok walkthrough. Mattress pain analysis: physical/functional (can't sleep, bad back), effort-based, financial, emotional ("me and partner don't sleep in the same bed"). Mine problem phrases. Review-mine for emotional pain. Apify Reddit/TikTok scrapers for community sentiment.

![Modular content pillars built audience-first: Hilton, Peloton, and Dyson examples mapping audience → problem → longtail search → best content type](/conference/seo-week-2026/carrie-rose-3.jpg)

**Change 5 — SEO-optimized social content.** There are 12 search bars consumers might jump between before purchasing. From "entertainment and following friends" TO "discovering and researching." Optimize search-first content for all of them. Most brands optimize for feeds, not search — that's your opening. Slow content vs Fast content: slow = informational, search terms, evergreen discovery; fast = trends, engagement spikes, virality. Clear budget split: social/brand/demand for fast; SEO for slow. Volume-vs-opportunity: "Debt Solutions" 8K searches vs "How to get out of debt" 159K — go big.

**Change 6 — Build a reactive process for fresh content.** 50% of top-cited content is less than 13 weeks old. The Traitors. Love is Blind. WWE Royal Rumble. Build a real cultural calendar — winnable moments throughout the year — and lean in.

![The winnable-moments cultural calendar: The Traitors, Love is Blind, awards season, and WWE events mapped month by month for reactive fresh content](/conference/seo-week-2026/carrie-rose-4.jpg)

**Change 7 — (Implied from the closing) Build the system that does this continuously.** SEO didn't change — it moved. The job is no longer just keyword rankings; it's owning the entire discoverable surface.
takeaways: 35-50 new SERP features in recent years; most don't send traffic — the discovery surface keeps fracturing
Become a search insight engine that fuels all channels — search is the human truth advertising lacks
Engineer signals: Digital PR outreach copy directly tells Google + LLMs what to associate with your brand (Airalo → global eSim provider)
Keywords in proximity of links matter — Airalo went from <1% 'eSim' in surrounding text to 65%, drove 70% LLM SOV
Audience-first content pillars: 'freelancer + remote work + LA + afternoon sun' → modular long-tail
Pain-point analysis across physical, emotional, effort, and financial dimensions = bigger keyword universe than competitors
Optimize for social search: 12 search bars in a purchase journey; slow content (evergreen, SEO budget) vs fast content (trends, social budget)
50% of top-cited AI content is <13 weeks old — build a reactive cultural-moment calendar and lean into winnable moments

## Ray Martinez — Watch the Party Die: Engineering 'Answerability' for Prospective Students

**The opener.** R.I.P. The 10 Blue Links, 2000-2024. SEO is dead. Long live SEO. Ray's bio: VP of SEO at Archer Education, 15+ years SEO, 10+ in higher ed, adjunct at U of Florida, rapper/producer, former party promoter, LLMs.txt hobbyist. Archer: 180+ team members, supporting 200+ institutions.

![From Invisible to Cited: how one university partner grew from 3 to 362 AI citations in 19 months, reaching 194K AI impressions/month](/conference/seo-week-2026/ray-martinez-1.jpg)

**Case study 1 — From 3 to 362 AI Citations in 19 months.** A regional university with almost zero AI visibility. Archer's approach: targeted link building (relevance over volume) + refreshed program page content with structured data + filled knowledge graph gaps. Result: 362 AI citations at peak, 194k AI impressions/month. Notable links: columbia.edu (DR 91), usc.edu (DR 90), ca.gov (DR 93), oregonstate.edu (DR 89), ama.org (DR 83).

**Case study 2 — Earned millions of impressions at zero paid spend.** Regionally accredited university. 70 coverage pieces, 4.3M estimated views, $680K publicity value, 74 avg domain authority.

**Then the lights came on.** A regionally accredited nursing program once dominating SERPs saw traffic tank. Archer audited and found indexability + rendering issues. Refreshed content. Began Academic Thought Leadership. This program drives better quality at lower volume.

**Search vs Fetch — the diagnostic.** Two distinct AI retrieval modes; your fix depends on which is failing. **AI Web Search** (Perplexity, ChatGPT Search, Gemini): crawlability — can bots reach your pages? Domain authority — who trusts your site? Backlink profile — who links to you? Traditional ranking signals. **LLM Fetch** (direct URL retrieval for training & responses): parse-ability — clean readable HTML? Markdown-readability — logical structure? Low JS bloat — no render-blocking. Clear hierarchy H1→H2→content flow. Takeaway: is your problem **visibility** (Search) or **comprehension** (Fetch)?

![Search vs. Fetch diagnostic: AI Web Search signals (crawlability, authority, backlinks) vs. LLM Fetch signals (parse-ability, markdown-readability, low JS, clear hierarchy)](/conference/seo-week-2026/ray-martinez-2.jpg)

**Tim Wu quote.** "We sometimes treat the information industries as if they were like any other enterprise, but they are not, for their structure determines who gets heard." 70% of students are using AI to explore program options and make quicker decisions. Google AI Overviews decreased organic search traffic — a page maintaining the same ranking YoY may receive 25% less traffic.

**SEO + AI search work together.** ~80% of AI eligibility comes from traditional SEO foundations (Crawl → Index → Rank). ~20% is different: passage retrieval + source citation. Plus query fanout, which Archer has been engineering for.

**AI-Ready Organic Strategy = 4 pillars.** Academic Thought Leadership · SEO · GEO · Organic Social.

**Engineering relevance — 3 levers.** (1) **Semantic scoring** — use LLMs to measure how closely page content aligns with student search intent, not keyword density. Try: ask ChatGPT "What question does this page best answer?" (2) **Entity gaps** — map which entities (programs, outcomes, skills) competitors "own" in LLM responses that you don't. Try: "What are the best [program] programs for [outcome]?" — are you in the answer? (3) **Multimodal + Digital PR** — highlight faculty expertise. Try: 1 strong program page + 5 supporting articles + 2 faculty profiles = authority cluster.

**The Student-First Knowledge Graph — 4 entity pillars.** Programs (degree names, specializations, format, credits, duration, tuition). Skills (competencies, certifications, tools — match job-posting language). Outcomes (job titles, salaries, employer names, alumni paths). Faculty (research areas, publications, industry experience — strongest authority signal for LLMs).

![The Student-First Knowledge Graph: the four entity pillars AI models look for — Programs, Skills, Outcomes, and Faculty](/conference/seo-week-2026/ray-martinez-3.jpg)

**ArcherEDU Higher Education Schema.** Knowledge Graph Authority — AI promotes brands with thorough knowledge graphs. GEO Knowledge Graph Audit: an MBA program at 59% entity coverage (50 of 85). Content to prioritize: Admissions, Curriculum, Outcomes, Faculty + Promotion. Plus LLMs require dates for content freshness — Archer found sitemaps using static dates and missing date metadata.

**Case study 3 — 627 enrolled students from organic.** Microsite for 5 online programs. Day 1: consistent content growth + freshness + interlinking. Evolved: semantically score and expand high-impact topics. 24 months → 3,726 leads, 1,789 apps, 627 enrolled — all organic.

**Case study 4 — 314 enrolled in 20 months across 6 programs.** Semantically relevant microsite, dedicated program pages, consistent blog cadence, day-1 strategic interlinking. 1,639 leads, 726 applications, 314 enrolled.

**Academic Thought Leadership.** A modern approach to PR that engages faculty, promotes research, boosts brand, strengthens SEO/GEO. Brand Awareness + Thought Leadership + Organic Traffic Amplification & Retargeting + SEO. Case study: a college of nursing built brand and authority via faculty experts → media pitches → content engine. AI citations increased sharply because media placements create the third-party validation LLMs prioritize.

**Tested on Archer's own properties first.** Refreshed program content, structured data, increased inbound link volume, added LLMs.txt files. Built WordPress plugins for internal sites. Automated LLMs.txt and .MD files. AI citations rose steadily, LLM conversions tracked the same direction.

**Bullseye — Archer's internal research agent.** Multi-agent build with API connections and MCP tools. Interacts with content agentically to deliver strategic insight.

**3 steps to start the party.** (1) **Today, 30 min** — Test your top 5 URLs. Crawl in Screaming Frog. Analyze crawlability, JS rendering, semantic HTML. If key content isn't extracted cleanly or is missing, you fail the fetch test. (2) **This week** — Identify entity gaps. Test ArcherEDU schema or Google's UCP, or run entity queries for your program + outcome combinations. (3) **This week** — Build a new tool or content asset to test program pages: deepen the stack, sharpen the strategy, create measurable value.

![3 Steps to Start The Party: test your top 5 URLs today, identify entity gaps this week, and build a tool or content asset to test program pages](/conference/seo-week-2026/ray-martinez-4.jpg)

## Sam Torres — Your Competitors Are Still Prompting. You Could Be Building.

**Aloha y'all.** The state of AI in SEO: AI is everywhere, most work is one-shot prompts, prompts don't connect to your stack. Prompt → draft a strategic POV → one-time project → dead end. Not scalable, no system.

**Your tools give you data. Acting on it at scale is where most teams stall.** A repeatable framework saves time, maintains quality, and applies across business needs. The difference is **ML, not vibes**. Vibe coding / prompt engineering is one row of dots. Machine learning is a different row of dots.

![Slide: The difference is ML — vibe coding/prompt engineering (fast, flexible, unpredictable, black box) vs. machine learning (academically-tested, peer-reviewed, repeatable, documented)](/conference/seo-week-2026/sam-torres-1.jpg)

**What you leave with.** One framework. Two workflows. Hands-on notebooks.

**The framework — three layers.**
1. **Embeddings** — vector_space.npy. Turn pages into math.
2. **Clustering** — surface (k-means, BERTopic, HDBSCAN).
3. **LLMs** — interpret. CLUSTER_01 · Water Sports: competitor owns 3× depth. CLUSTER_02 · Footwear: missing entirely. CLUSTER_03 · Venues: parity reached.

Each layer answers a different question. Tool-agnostic. Workflow-agnostic. That's the point.

![Slide: Each layer answers a different question — Embeddings (what is similar?), Clustering (what belongs together?), LLMs (what does it mean?); tool-agnostic, workflow-agnostic](/conference/seo-week-2026/sam-torres-2.jpg)

**Alone, each layer breaks.** Embeddings alone = vectors without meaning. Clustering alone = topics without intent. LLMs alone = prompt-and-pray. Chain them together → automation.

**Four tips before starting.** (1) Direct & delegate like an intern — bright but never seen your stack, brand, or stakeholders. The clearer the brief, the better the work. (2) Think 80/20: 20% of work delivers 80% of result; ship the 80%. (3) Refer to "Is This Worth It?" — isitworththetime.com (xkcd 1205 effort-vs-frequency table). (4) Start small. Enjoy the wins.

**Workflow 1 — Competitor Gap Analysis.** Traditional comp gap tells you WHAT (missing keywords sorted by volume). Doesn't tell HOW DEEP a competitor owns a topic or where the structural holes are. Better business question: *"Who owns this topic space, and where are the gaps in breadth and depth?"*

Inputs: your crawl export + competitor URLs + GSC data.

Turn pages into math:
```
from sentence_transformers import SentenceTransformer
model = SentenceTransformer('all-MiniLM-L6-v2')
pages = pd.read_csv('crawl.csv')
vectors = model.encode(pages['content'])
# → (4,218 pages, 384 dims)
```

Cluster topics; output `clusters.jsonl`: water sports 18/52, destination guides 6/34, gear reviews 0/28, venue roundups 22/19 (you/competitor pages per cluster).

**Breadth × Depth.** Breadth = how many clusters you cover vs them. Depth = within shared clusters, how much content they have vs you. Label, identify, prioritize. Output: a prioritized gap report, grounded in structure. Three approaches: Rising Tide (lift parity clusters), Open Water (new clusters), Deep Sea (depth within owned clusters).

![Slide: Breadth x Depth — UMAP topic space map of your site vs. a competitor, showing cluster coverage (breadth) and content volume within shared clusters (depth)](/conference/seo-week-2026/sam-torres-3.jpg)

**Workflow 2 — Internal Linking Opportunity Automation.** Internal linking is high-leverage; most teams do it by hand. Manual is slow. Keyword-match tools miss semantic matches. ML pipeline solves both.

Linking sits at intersection of CMS + content strategy + crawl data + engineering. Same 3 layers, different direction — look inward instead of outward.

Required: your crawl export. Optional: existing link map. Clustering surfaces semantic relationships anchor-text matching would miss — pages that belong together even when they share no keywords. Output: `internal_graph.viz` — 3 clusters, 2 cross-cluster bridge opportunities detected. Recommends: which link, which anchor, priority.

**Side-by-side comparison.** Same pipeline, two workflows.

![Slide: Two workflows, one pipeline — side-by-side table comparing competitor gap analysis and internal linking across input, question, embeddings, clustering, and LLM output](/conference/seo-week-2026/sam-torres-4.jpg)
- Workflow 1 (Comp Gap): input = competitor crawl + GSC; question = who owns topic space; embeddings = content similarity ACROSS sites; clustering = topic neighborhoods (comp vs you); LLM output = gap report + content priorities.
- Workflow 2 (Internal Linking): input = your own crawl; question = where are my linking gaps; embeddings = semantic similarity WITHIN site; clustering = your content city; LLM output = linking recs + anchor text.

**Models to try.**
- Video: Whisper → ST Embeddings (free) / AssemblyAI → OpenAI (premium). Watch transcript quality, accents, jargon.
- Image: BLIP/CLIP (free) / GPT-4o Vision (premium). Scale costs.
- PDF: Tesseract → ST / AWS Textract → OpenAI. Scanned vs text-native matters.
- Multilingual: Multilingual-miniLM / text-embedding-3-small. Start with language detection.

**Try it with your own data.** Two notebooks at THESEOMERMAID.com/seo-week-2026 — competitor gap analysis and internal linking.

Your competitors are still prompting. Now you know how to build. *Mahalo nui loa.*
takeaways: Most SEO 'AI work' is one-shot prompts that don't connect to your stack — dead-end, not scalable
The framework is 3 layers: Embeddings → Clustering → LLMs. Chained together = automation; alone, each breaks
Traditional comp gap tells you WHAT (missing keywords). The better question: who owns the topic space and where are the depth gaps?
Workflow 1: Embed pages → cluster topics → quantify breadth × depth → 3 approaches (Rising Tide / Open Water / Deep Sea)
Workflow 2: Embed your own site → cluster semantically → surface internal linking opportunities anchor-text matching misses
Same pipeline, two directions: look outward (gap analysis) or inward (internal linking) — tool-agnostic, workflow-agnostic
Models scale across modalities: video (Whisper), image (BLIP/CLIP), PDF (Tesseract), multilingual (Multilingual-miniLM)
Treat AI like an intern: clear briefs, 80/20 effort, start small. Notebooks at theseomermaid.com/seo-week-2026

## Lisa Paasche — Making the Impossible Possible

**What AI will NOT replace.** Curiosity. Imagination. The senses: taste, sight, touch, hear, smell. Gut feeling. Connection.

**The credentials.** Founder & CEO of Verve Search 2009-2017 (SEO & Digital PR agency), sold to Omnicom. Now: Neuroscience Informed Leadership Coach, workshop facilitator, business transformation advisor, podcast host of "Being EKTE."

**The proof at Verve.** 65 creative campaigns/year across 8 countries. Best SEO Agency 3 years running. Coverage on TV (TV3 Sweden, NBC US, ITV News UK). Social coverage by Greenpeace, WWF, NASA. BBC collaborations (Secret Nationality quiz, British Accent quiz, Foodprint Calculator). Profanity on Film for Buzz Bingo — covered by The Guardian, NME, The Wrap, with Seth Rogen and Adam Levine commenting on Jonah Hill's Instagram. Electric Avenues for GoCompare — covered by ZDNet, cited in an Australian Senate inquiry.

**But it wasn't always like this.** 2009-2014 they were "just another SEO agency." January 2015 things looked a bit shit — 10% profit margin. 2 years later: 40% profit margin. What changed? "When everyone draws a cross, draw a circle."

![The talk's signature visual: a field of pink crosses with one lone circle — 'When everyone draws a cross, draw a circle.'](/conference/seo-week-2026/lisa-paasche-1.jpg)

**The 50s ad-exec mindset.** Big ideas. Bold campaigns. That's how we sell in any era. Strategy, creativity, results — and execute LIKE GEEKS. Lisa had to make 40% of the agency redundant. Not because they weren't good enough — because they didn't believe it was possible.

**Belief #1.** For decades people believed running a mile in under 4 minutes was physiologically impossible. Doctors said the body would break down. May 6, 1954: Roger Bannister, 3:59.4. 46 days later: John Landy, 3:58. Today: over 1,500 athletes have done it. The body didn't suddenly evolve in 46 days. **The belief did.** Expectation precedes perception. The brain looks for evidence to confirm what it already believes is possible. 6-10 million bits of sensory info register per second; you consciously deal with 50-100 bits because 99.9% goes to bodily function. But the 50-100 bits you notice, you have control over.

**Recruited for grit, not experience.**

**Belief #2 — Connection (the nervous system).** Sympathetic (fight or flight) vs Parasympathetic (rest and digest). Pupils dilate vs constrict. Heart rate increases vs slows. Digestion shuts down vs absorbs. Adrenals activate vs calm. A brain under threat is not a creative brain. When threat is perceived, the amygdala triggers cortisol/adrenaline/noradrenaline. The prefrontal cortex (logic, reasoning, future thinking) **goes offline**. Logical thinking impaired. Problem solving impaired. Future planning impaired. Decision making becomes reactive, impulsive, risk-driven. Survival mode: react, defend, escape, freeze.

![Fight-or-flight infographic: amygdala fires, the prefrontal cortex disengages, and logic, problem-solving, and future planning all shut down.](/conference/seo-week-2026/lisa-paasche-2.jpg)

**Fear narrows the future. Safety expands it.** When the brain perceives safety (vagus nerve signals), oxytocin/serotonin/dopamine release. Logical thinking, creativity, future imagination, perspective taking, decision making, learning all come back online. Psychological safety and social connection are associated with stronger parasympathetic regulation.

**Dr Arthur Aron 1997.** 36 progressively personal questions + 4 minutes of eye contact between strangers. Reported deep emotional closeness in 45 minutes. Vulnerability accelerated closeness; eye contact intensified it.

**Connection is not about always agreeing.** It's about being able to disagree and solve challenges by communicating. (Adam Grant's Giver / Taker / Agreeable / Disagreeable matrix.) Encourage people to disagree. DISC behavioral profiling for everyone. Conflict resolution.

![Adam Grant's Giver/Taker vs Agreeable/Disagreeable matrix, mapped onto Star Wars characters.](/conference/seo-week-2026/lisa-paasche-3.jpg)

**Love Week at Verve.** Everyone picked a name at random. Did something nice for that person every day for a week (secretly). Friday was reveal day. What started happening was magical. **Love Week increased performance MORE than payrises or bonuses.**

![Performance timeline with arrows marking each Love Week — the spikes that outperformed pay rises or bonuses.](/conference/seo-week-2026/lisa-paasche-4.jpg)

**The closing.** In the age of AI what will set you apart: the ability to regulate your nervous system, human connection, and the belief that you can. Reading recs: *Nervous System Reset* (Jessica Maguire), *Mind Magic* (Dr James Doty), *The Creative Act* (Rick Rubin). "I'm not a genius. I just thought I could. So I did."

Free 1h advisory consultation: lisa@ekte-vision.com.
takeaways: What AI will NOT replace: curiosity, imagination, senses, gut feeling, connection
Verve Search went from 10% margin (Jan 2015) → 40% margin (2 years later) by changing belief, not tactics — 'when everyone draws a cross, draw a circle'
Roger Bannister broke the 4-minute mile in 1954; 46 days later someone else did it; today 1,500+ athletes — the body didn't evolve, the BELIEF did
Expectation precedes perception: 6-10M bits of sensory info per second; you process 50-100 — you have control over which
A brain under threat is not a creative brain — fight/flight shuts down the prefrontal cortex (logic, future planning, decision making)
Fear narrows the future; safety expands it — oxytocin/serotonin/dopamine bring back creativity + future thinking
Connection isn't agreement — it's being able to disagree and solve via communication (Adam Grant's giver/taker matrix)
Verve's Love Week (secret kindness for a week) increased performance MORE than payrises or bonuses

## Paul Shapiro — One Day Your Mom Will Be An Agent

**The setup.** Lead Product Manager, Web Intelligence at Uber. The agenda: (1) State of AI today, where it's headed, and implications. (2) Agents and harnesses. (3) Thinking about AEO/GEO. (4) Conclusion (or is it...).

![Slide: Goldman Sachs forecasts 30% productivity gains, JPMorgan 40-50% in operations, and Wells Fargo budgets for a smaller 2026 workforce](/conference/seo-week-2026/paul-shapiro-1.jpg)

**Doom, gloom, or somewhere in the middle?** "You wrote a prompt. The agent did the work. You approved the output. That was George Jetson's job." Daniel Susskind: "A job is not simply a source of income but of meaning, purpose, and direction." Captain Picard: "The acquisition of wealth is no longer the driving force in our lives. We work to better ourselves and the rest of humanity." Goldman Sachs forecasts 30% median productivity gain on specific tasks. JPMorgan: 40-50% improvement in operations. Wells Fargo: budgeting for smaller workforce in 2026. When it doesn't work, the jobs still don't come back. Google modeling the end game: 700 jobs eliminated.

**"AI doesn't actually think."** "It's just autocomplete." "It hallucinates constantly." "This is all overhyped." Searle's Chinese Room: a person in a room handed Chinese characters and rules about how to respond. Hands back Chinese replies. From outside, looks like understanding. *Mai nafka minah* — what difference does it make? If it quacks like a duck. These systems reason about your brand. You are optimizing for whether you appear. There's a gap.

**Tools → Copilots → Agents.** The progression is real.

**Agents and harnesses.** **Harness Engineering** = the environment the model runs in: memory, tools, system access, permissions, execution context. The model does the thinking. The harness does everything else. Common agents and their harnesses: ChatGPT/Codex, Claude Code, OpenClaw, etc.

![Slide: common agents mapped on the harness spectrum from opaque (ChatGPT, Gemini) through opinionated (Claude Code, Cursor) and configurable (OpenClaw) to constructable (LangGraph, raw SDKs)](/conference/seo-week-2026/paul-shapiro-2.jpg)

**Hosting/hardware options.** Cheap VPS (inexpensive, reliable, headless), Mac Mini (Mac OS access, local models, UI), Old Laptop (no recurring costs, but fan runs, awkward), Raspberry Pi (cheapest, limited horsepower).

**Deployment structure.** Model Gateway: Primary = ChatGPT Codex OAuth (predictable cost, $20+/month, not per token). Backup = OpenRouter API Gateway (free models + low-cost Chinese models). Channels: Telegram (one of the best maintained integrations; pairing mode for DMs only; dedicated bot accounts per channel, not personal accounts/group chats). Integration rule: only listens locally (127.0.0.1, no external access).

**Network & access security.** No public ports. Ever. Tailscale Serve, not Funnel. Dedicated hardware ideally. SSH keys, not passwords. Dedicated OS user, not root.

**Configuration paradigms.** Dedicated accounts (not personal/work). OAuth over API keys when possible. Use your own self-created skills only. If using third-party skills, read SKILL.md like it may be adversarial code. **~12% of ClawHub Skills contain active malware** (Koi Security, Paul McCarty, Cisco Talos 2026). ~26% contain exploitable vulnerabilities. OpenClaw and open-source AI software is being targeted (LiteLLM incident).

**Credential storage.** Best = Vault (sops, Bitwarden, 1Password, Hashicorp Vault, AWS Secrets Manager). Suboptimal = env file (with SecretsRef). Avoid plaintext in openclaw.json, auth-profiles.json, or .env. `openclaw secrets configure` is the migration command. (Paul ran OpenClaw before SecretsRef and the migration wasn't smooth — `{id}` template substitution didn't work, systemd user service didn't pass env vars, OpenClaw exec provider uses JSON-RPC over stdin not CLI args. Had to write a 10-line wrapper to translate OpenClaw's protocol to sops CLI.)

**OpenClaw vs Claude Code — differences are blurring.** (1) Model-agnostic (any LLM: Claude, GPT, DeepSeek, local Ollama; Paul routes through ChatGPT OAuth at $20/mo). (2) Proactive, not reactive — HEARTBEAT.md runs every 30 minutes on its own. The agent reads a checklist, decides if anything needs doing, messages Paul if it does. Claude Code waits for you to type. (3) Workspace grammar for a whole life — SOUL.md, USER.md, AGENTS.md, HEARTBEAT.md, MEMORY.md + daily notes. A structured way to tell the agent who it is, who you are, and how to operate over months. Claude Code has CLAUDE.md and rules — great for code, not built for life. Paul runs both in parallel; OpenClaw orchestrates Claude Code when there's real code to write.

**What most people are getting wrong about AI optimization.** Bot hits, visibility, citations, share of voice, sentiment — the floor, not the building. **Audit AI answers beyond visibility & citations: how are you represented?** When the model talks about you: are the facts right? Does it describe you the way you describe yourself? Le Creuset example: you describe yourself as Heritage French Cookware, Premium tier, peers Staub, "Buy it for Life." The model's answer: names you "best overall," calls you "very expensive," instead routes users to Lodge.

![Slide: the Le Creuset representation gap — the brand says heritage French cookware and buy-it-for-life, the model says best overall but very expensive and routes users to Lodge](/conference/seo-week-2026/paul-shapiro-3.jpg)

**Analyze reasoning/thinking.** Presence and representation measure what the model says. **Reasoning analysis measures HOW it gets there.** Imperfect, but you should be mining it. The model is reading your content on the user's behalf — the human never sees your site. Reasoning walkthrough on "What's a good Dutch oven for a home cook?" → "Most people should buy this: Lodge 6-Quart Enameled Cast Iron Dutch Oven." The model decides what the user hears about you.

**Auditing reasoning — the aggregation method.** Reasoning traces ARE intent data. Read them, aggregate them, act on them.

![Slide: the five-step reasoning audit — query set design, batched trace capture, signal aggregation, failure rate mapping, then remediation and re-measurement](/conference/seo-week-2026/paul-shapiro-4.jpg)

**The conclusion.** When you're back in the office next: the future is agentic. An agent is reasoning, working on someone's behalf. If your brand can't survive the reasoning, your brand isn't in the answer. **The LLMs we're optimizing for reason. Almost nobody optimizes for that. That gap is where everything else lives.**
takeaways: Harness Engineering is the environment the model runs in — memory, tools, permissions, execution context. The model thinks; the harness does everything else
Forecasts: Goldman 30% productivity gain · JPMorgan 40-50% in operations · Wells Fargo budgeting smaller workforce · Google eliminated 700 jobs
Security: ~12% of ClawHub Skills contain active malware, ~26% have exploitable vulnerabilities — read SKILL.md like it's adversarial
No public ports ever; Tailscale Serve (not Funnel); SSH keys not passwords; dedicated OS user not root
OpenClaw is proactive (HEARTBEAT.md runs every 30 min); Claude Code is reactive (waits for prompt). Paul runs both in parallel
Workspace grammar for life: SOUL.md, USER.md, AGENTS.md, HEARTBEAT.md, MEMORY.md — tells the agent who it is, who you are, how to operate over months
Most AI optimization is bot hits + citations — that's the floor. The building is REASONING analysis: how the model gets to its answer
Reasoning traces ARE intent data — read, aggregate, act. If your brand can't survive the reasoning, your brand isn't in the answer

## Ruth Burr Reedy — Make It Count

**Bio.** Director, SEO Solutions at Microsoft. 20 years SEO. 10+ years hiring and managing SEO teams. 7 years agency leadership. Previous in-house: Houzz, Moz, GameHouse. Lives in Seattle. 1 spouse, 1 kid, 1 dog. What she does: Technical SEO, AI SEO, Measurement & Data Strategy across Microsoft Commercial (B2B), AI & Business Solutions, Cloud & AI Platforms, Security, GitHub & Developer, Education, Research, Operations.

![The impending talent pipeline problem: career pyramid from entry level to Manager/Expert IC, with entry-level work flagged as "all of this can be done by AI now"](/conference/seo-week-2026/ruth-burr-reedy-1.jpg)

**What she doesn't do.** *(The slide was blank — point made.)*

**The career question.** "What does this mean for my career?" The org chart: Senior level technical audits, content strategy, reporting instrumentation, advanced data analysis. Mid-level keyword categorization, content creation, reporting, executing technical recommendations. Entry-level keyword research, content optimization, manual link updates, title tags, meta tags. **SEO jobs are increasingly senior and in-house** (Previsible 2025 State of SEO Jobs Report).

**This stuff is harder than it used to be.** SEO has never been just one thing — content strategy, technical health, UX, mobile friendliness, outreach, CRO, internal link graph, A/B testing, brand building, web analytics, hreflang, semantic markup, content creation, governance, site speed, images. Machine-readable equivalents + human-readable quality signals. Modern SEO is multi-channel and multi-modal. New buyer journeys mean new business models and new marketing strategies. **Were y'all listening or nah? (September 3rd, 2013.)**

**Broad learning + specialty + ecosystem.** AI SEO, SEO, Social, PR, Paid Media — each with specialized inputs (topic coverage strategy, query fan-out, web analytics for SEO; user research, channel performance, media relationships for PR; budget, run rate, media assets for paid). **Shared KPIs**: mentions, citations, share of voice, brand signals. **Shared strategy**: technical foundation, messaging clarity, multi-modal readiness. Specialized tactics within each: content structure, technical health, taxonomy for SEO; influencer outreach, community engagement for social; influence AI-trusted sources, rapid testing for paid.

![The ecosystem framework: AI SEO, Social, PR, and Paid Media mapped by specialized inputs, shared KPIs, shared strategy, and specialized tactics](/conference/seo-week-2026/ruth-burr-reedy-2.jpg)

**How is the job you have now giving you the skills you need next?** Cross-functional pairings: Technical SEO + Web Dev = Crawlability Engineer. Content Marketing + PR + Social = Marketing Storyteller. Content Creation + AI SEO = Semantic Expert. Web Analytics + AI Tooling = Agentic Operations. Paid + Organic = Full-Funnel Strategist. Technical Skilling + People Management = Team Lead. (Source: SEMRush, 3,900 SEO Job Listings 2026.)

**Not all AI skills are created equal.**

**The talent pipeline problem.** Where is the entry level? Senior level absorbs the strategic + technical work. Mid level executes via tools. Entry level does keyword research and meta tags — work AI now does in seconds. Without entry level, there's no pipeline to seniority. Places to grow: agencies, small business, cross-channel learning, side hustles.

**Hiring is terrible on both sides right now.** Gen AI use in recruiting: 20% average reported time saved per work week (one full day). 4+ hours saved per open role. (LinkedIn Future of Recruiting 2025.)

**How to optimize a resume to get past AI-driven screening.** DO: summary with years of experience, standard headers, clean formatting (.pdf/.docx), mirror exact keywords from listing, use full terms AND acronyms, quantify achievements with metrics, structure as Action → Result → Metric, professional filename including name/resume/year. DON'T: tables, text boxes, images, graphics, unusual fonts; hidden white-text keywords or AI prompts; vague descriptions; generic terms instead of specific skills; untailored resumes.

![Resume DOs and DON'Ts for getting past AI-driven screening tools (and human reviewers)](/conference/seo-week-2026/ruth-burr-reedy-3.jpg)

**The blunt truth.** You can't always pass. The hiring manager says "Minimum 5 years of experience" but means "I need someone who already knows how to do this." The tool hears "4½ years? Get out." Network. Conferences (this one!). Social media (LinkedIn, Threads, X). Private communities (Slack, Discord). Local meetups (shoutout Seattle SEO Beers). If you hate networking, you're probably doing it wrong.

**Skills that matter next.**

![Project management tops SEMRush's key skills for senior SEO positions — "a tool can't make people do stuff" (3,900 job listings, 2026)](/conference/seo-week-2026/ruth-burr-reedy-4.jpg)
- **Project Management** — a tool can't make people do stuff. Time management, goal setting, collaboration, communication, conflict resolution, adaptability. "People find reasons to avoid working with someone they don't like." (Wil Reynolds, earlier in the week.)
- **Executive Presence** — can you hang in the room where it happens? Public speaking, data storytelling, budgeting/forecasting, quick pivots, building consensus, getting buy-in. **Agentic workflow**: build a repository of your exec's most-used words, phrases, and frameworks to translate deliverables into their language.
- **Aggressive Learning** — curiosity is the best predictor of success. Where do you stay current? How do you know a "best practice" works? What are you reading/listening to/learning? **Agentic workflow**: AI tools to collect your most trusted sources in a single information flow. But don't over-rely on AI summaries — they lack nuance.
- **Strategic Thinking** — work the problem, not the process. What do you do when your usual process breaks? How do you prioritize when you can't do everything? How do you know an expensive action is still worth doing? The "why" behind it all — understanding how LLMs and search bots crawl, parse, entity-relate, answer — future-proofs against tactic failure.

**The Duane Forrester quote.** "The practitioners who will matter in three years are building that foundation right now, using every tool available… they are not choosing between AI and thinking but using AI to think harder than they could before, and that is not a leveling effect but a compounding one."

**The closing.** AI gives you the vocabulary. It doesn't give you the expertise. **Marketers will continue ruining everything. You got this.**
takeaways: SEO jobs are increasingly senior and in-house — the entry level is being absorbed by AI, breaking the talent pipeline (Previsible 2025)
Modern SEO has never been one thing — content + technical + UX + analytics + governance + brand + multi-modal readiness
Shared KPIs across SEO/Social/PR/Paid: mentions, citations, share of voice, brand signals (the cross-channel scorecard)
Cross-functional pairings unlock the next role: Technical SEO + Web Dev = Crawlability Engineer; Content + AI SEO = Semantic Expert
Resume DO: years summary, standard headers, exact-keyword mirroring, quantified Action → Result → Metric, professional filename
Resume DON'T: tables/images/unusual fonts (AI screeners can't parse them), hidden white-text AI prompts, generic terms vs specific tool names
Four skills that matter next: Project Management, Executive Presence, Aggressive Learning, Strategic Thinking
Duane Forrester: 'AI gives you the vocabulary; it doesn't give you the expertise.' Not a leveling effect — a compounding one

## Ryan Jones — SEO vs GEO: Semantic Success Secrets

**About Ryan.** Day job: SVP at Razorfish, co-runs the SEO Practice, 15 years in, 6 company name changes. Night job: SERPrecon.com, his semantic relevance SEO tool. AI Share of Voice, GEO Optimization, real metrics. Coupon code SEOWEEK for 25% off for life. "I've been talking about AI search for over a decade." Also: too much cornhole.

**SEO vs AI — the metrics disagree.** Gen AI Market Share: 59.4% ChatGPT, 14.4% Microsoft Copilot, 13.5% Gemini, 5.8% Other, 3% Perplexity, 2% Claude. AI vs Google Market Share: Google 90%, Bing + Yahoo + Other 10%. 350M ChatGPT MAU vs Google's 16.5B searches/day. **31.8× more searches.** AI is real, but it's not 1:1 substituting for Google.

!["The Metrics Disagree" — Gen AI market share (ChatGPT 59.4%) vs Google's 90% search share and 16.5B daily searches, a 31.8x gap](/conference/seo-week-2026/ryan-jones-1.jpg)

**The clicks aren't coming back.** Especially if you're using AI content (ahrefs data).

**"SEO isn't dead. What you were doing wasn't SEO."** The S stands for Schrödinger. Many self-proclaimed SEOs are just spammers. We have a perception problem. So we rebranded — "AEO," "GEO," "ASO." Whatever we call this, bad SEO is dead.

**The evolution.** **From:** SERP & Keyword Focus. Winning #1 in Google. People using only search engines. Informed by keywords + historical search volumes. KPIs: awareness (impressions, rankings), consideration (clicks, users, sessions), conversion (site engagement). Keyword-optimized web pages. Goal KPIs: sales, conversions, brand growth.

**To:** Semantic Relevance. Winning brand SOV + inclusion wherever the audience is. People searching everywhere (search, social, retail, LLMs). Informed by topics, semantic relevance, audiences, experience. KPIs: visibility (impressions, citations), sentiment/referrals, business impact (direct + indirect conversions). Semantically relevant content across multiple formats and platforms. Goal KPIs: same — but measured differently.

!["We Need To Evolve" framework table — from SERP & keyword focus to semantic relevance across focus, audience, KPIs, content, and goals](/conference/seo-week-2026/ryan-jones-2.jpg)

**Your attribution models are broken.**

**For AI it's all about SOV now.** That's right — SEOs are coming for the brand budget.

**It's harder to game the algorithm.** So people are gaming the metrics. It's not the race you think it is. *Silly human, the internet is for bots.*

**The new user.** It's not just a person behind a keyboard. It's also the AI model reading your content BEFORE the person ever sees it. AI is now the first audience. It decides what to include, quote, or reference — using Search. We're optimizing for machines that summarize for people.

**Most AI searches have 0 historical search volume.** 80% of 1,955 keywords have less than 100 monthly searches. **How do you optimize what you can't measure?**

**The AI Overview patent — let's unpack it.** Generate LLM output. Generate synthetic queries (we can reverse-engineer these!). Then care about which content is retrieved for each synthetic query. Or use Google testimony for the same info.

![The Google AI Overview patent flowchart (FIG. 9) — receive query, generate LLM output, generate synthetic queries, then select search result documents](/conference/seo-week-2026/ryan-jones-3.jpg)

**You don't need to rank for that query. You need to be retrieved.** (Sorry link builders and guest posters.)

**GEO requires slightly different writing styles.** AI doesn't rank pages — it retrieves passages. Skip grandma's life story on recipe pages. Four levers: (1) **Answer-first** — content that clearly summarizes upfront is 33% more likely to be cited by AI (Princeton/ACM KDD 2024). (2) **Sourced stat** — specific sourced statistics increase LLM visibility 30-40% (SEMRush 2026). (3) **Definition** — cited sentences are nearly 2× more likely to *define* rather than describe (Search Engine Land 2026). (4) **Quotable** — structured into clear extractable chunks, AI visibility +30% (Princeton/ACM KDD 2024).

!["GEO Requires Slightly Different Writing Styles" — the four levers (sourced stat, definition, quotable, answer-first) with cited visibility lifts](/conference/seo-week-2026/ryan-jones-4.jpg)

**Step 1 — Understand the fan-out.** Use SERPrecon (or 67,000 other tools, or just hit the Gemini API directly).

**Step 2 — Create structured content that ranks for those queries.**

**Case study 1 — Whirlpool.** Dominating the appliance search landscape with AI brands consistently appearing side by side in AI Overviews + top organic. Approach: unified keyword strategy + single cross-brand loop. Performance: +165% shared page-1 KWs · +138% share of search · 150K AI Overview citations.

**Case study 2 — Oral-B.** Most purchases happen un-tracked in-person at retail. The recommendation was all that mattered. Influencers + YouTube strategy → increased offline sales at CVS/Walmart. Strong correlation between AI presence and offline sales lift.

**How do teams and SEOs adjust for this future?** How does the C-suite adjust? "Just make my clicks go up." "They're not coming back." "If it's just SEO, why do you need more $$?" **Your org structure and OKRs are the real problem.** Take more credit! Clicks are vanity metrics.

**The future will NOT resemble the past.** Tools need to do better. Historical keyword volumes won't cut it anymore. We need SOV and upper-funnel measurement. We need semantic relevance. So Ryan built SERPrecon — and the AI Overview Influence Tracker is FREE.

**Media Mix Modeling AI Overviews.** Wanted to isolate the effect of AI Overview increases against sales. When accounting for offline, **AI Overviews contributed almost as much as paid search** for this client (results varied).

**Tactics.**
- Ask AI what it knows and doesn't know about your business.
- Do you have a **Wikidata page?** All AI trains on it.
- Tokens are expensive. Chipotle Chat is free.
- Claude tracks who's being mean.
- If you're not nice to AI, this could be our future.

Other sites of his: WTFSEO.com · SEODataViz.com · ServerHeaders.com · SEOnews.pro. Code "SEOWEEK" 25% off SERPrecon for life.

## Ilana Gershteyn — Working Through a Google Drop

**Key thesis:** Any time a Google drop hits, you run diagnostics — rankings, crawl logs, JS rendering, Core Web Vitals. **You inspect every system in the stack except one: the one running between your ears.** That system decides how well every other system gets diagnosed. Ilana (Director of SEO at Edmunds, 13+ years in-house SEO + development, B.S. Computer Science, UCLA Anderson MBA candidate '27, TEDx speaker) brings Internal Family Systems psychology to the drop-day war room — and closes with the sharpest framing of the week: **in a world where AI commodified the analysis, self-awareness is the remaining edge.**

![Ilana's opening hook — you inspect every system in the stack except the one running between your ears](/conference/seo-week-2026/ilana-drop-hits.jpg)

### TL;DR

Your mind is not a mono-mind — it's a **system of parts** (Richard Schwartz's IFS, 'No Bad Parts'), and on drop day five of them fight for the keyboard: the Convincer, the Performer, the Frozen One, the Researcher, and the Fixer. Each drop archetype (bug/deploy, SERP change, site quality, site speed) triggers a signature dysfunction pattern between them. The fix isn't suppressing the parts — it's the **Director**: the Self that hears all five without becoming any of them. And because search itself is a component model (DOJ testimony + the API leak proved it), **your diagnosis has to be component-shaped too — anything else is a story, not a finding.**

### Meet the cast

![The five parts that show up on drop day](/conference/seo-week-2026/ilana-meet-the-cast.jpg)

- **The Convincer** — "I already know why." Formed when being undecided got mocked. Builds plausible narratives that incidentally exonerate the team.
- **The Performer** — "We need to look decisive." Formed when passed over for a position. Ships charts that look good while the P&L doesn't notice.
- **The Frozen One** — "Can't move. Wait and see." Formed by old trauma. Treats reversible causes as terminal — while the revert button sits right there.
- **The Researcher** — "Need more data." Formed by a costly under-informed mistake. Days spent hunting the single ultimate answer that doesn't exist.
- **The Fixer** — "Motion as proof of value." Formed when waiting looked like failing. Fires gut-shot reverts at every suspect; the cull obscures the cause.

### The four drop archetypes and their conflict patterns

- **Bug/deploy drop → Protection Cascade.** The visible Fixer ("roll back, ship something, anything") keeps the hidden Frozen One ("this might be the end") out of the room. Three reverts deep, nobody has diagnosed anything and the original cause is buried. The revert is SEO's "is it plugged in?" — and the diagnosis is often PEBKAC: your own deploy from two weeks ago, log never opened.
- **SERP changes → Gang Together.** Convincer: "AI Overviews ate our traffic." Performer: "Yes — pivot to GEO." **Two parts agreeing feels like consensus** — and the Researcher's real question (WHICH SERP features, WHICH query clusters, WHICH intents shifted) never enters the room. Context: AI Overviews now trigger on nearly half of tracked queries (+58% YoY), and personalization ended the universal SERP — "is it rankings or layout?" is a real diagnostic fork now.
- **Site quality → confident Gang Together, or Deadlock.** "Start killing thin pages today" + "our pages are stale, refresh now" + "we'll announce the cleanup as the cause" feels decisive — while the actual cause (a Navboost click-signal decay, an embedding/quality shift, a SERP feature takeover) goes undiagnosed for a quarter. Her antidote is quantitative: **segment pages by template, age, and performance decile; generate a vector interpretation and measure drift from the centroid — and interrogate how you defined the centroid.** The deadlock variant: Fixer ("just remove them") vs Researcher ("I need to segment first") — each escalation proves the other part right, and the middle path stays hidden.
- **Site speed → Two Opposites / One Solo.** Performer: "Core Web Vitals look perfect" vs the Researcher quietly finding 10MB of unused JS in one function. Or the Convincer soloing "it's TTFB — backend services," which hides the honest "I don't know yet." Anchors: LCP ≤ 2.5s, INP ≤ 200ms, CLS ≤ 0.1.

### Search is a component model — your diagnosis has to be one too

![Three exhibits: DOJ testimony, the May 2024 API leak, and Vertex AI Search selling the formula](/conference/seo-week-2026/ilana-component-model.jpg)

- **Exhibit 1 — DOJ v. Google (2023–2025):** Pandu Nayak named the components under oath: RankEmbed, PageRank, Navboost, Twiddlers, T* topicality — with **T* = f(Anchors, Body, Clicks)**.
- **Exhibit 2 — the May 2024 API leak:** ensemble models and versioned quality/authority embeddings — QualityAuthorityTopicEmbeddings, NSR, Qualityboost.
- **Exhibit 3 — Vertex AI Search:** Google literally sells the formula; you weight semantic_similarity, keyword_match, freshness, and custom_signals yourself.
- The implication: a drop is some subset of components moving. A diagnosis that isn't component-shaped — that doesn't name which signal family it suspects — is a narrative, and probably a part wrote it.

### Act 3 — The Direction

![Every part is trying to protect you — meet them in calm, use their superpower in chaos](/conference/seo-week-2026/ilana-protect-you.jpg)

Every part is trying to protect you. Met in calm, each has a gift: the Frozen One set your alert thresholds back when things were quiet, and with the Fixer it **holds the pause**; the Researcher **finds the signal**; the Convincer and Performer **carry the story** to leadership. Above them sits the **Director** — Schwartz's Self, the one who can hear all five without becoming any of them (the 8 Cs: calm, curious, clear, compassionate, confident, creative, courageous, connected). Leading SEO isn't having the answer — it's holding the room while the answer gets found, without letting the loudest part run the meeting.

### The practices worth stealing

- Before you type a reply, **name which part is at the keyboard.**
- **The first hypothesis is usually a part, not a finding.**
- **If your theory exonerates you, a part wrote it.**
- Give the Researcher **a deadline**. Give the Fixer **a constraint**.
- Calm isn't a feeling — **it's what's left when no part is in the lead.**

### The closer — EQ is the new IQ

AI ate the analysis: every SEO has the same crawlers, the same LLMs, the same dashboards — raw IQ is infrastructure now. What's left is **judgment under pressure**: which part of you is at the keyboard, when to act, when to wait, which voice to amplify. It's a practice, not a tool — **the Director isn't downloaded, it's developed.** The new edge isn't smarter. It's more self-aware.
